## Page 1

Segment Limitation

Audience - Segments - Interactive Segment - Create New Segment

A new feature will be added to the segment creation screen that allows users to define limits
specific to each segment group. When the user clicks on the limit icon, a modal will open,

allowing them to set a limit for the selected segment group.

During this process, the number of people in the segment group will not be calculated. For
example, if a segment group contains 80 people but a limit of 100 is defined, the process will
proceed without any restrictions. No warning or notification will be shown to the user

regarding this situation.

Each segment group can have an independent limit. If multiple segment groups are
combined or if a new filter is added to a group with a defined limit, the set limit will remain

unchanged. The user can manually update the limit value later if needed.

In larger segment groups that include multiple segment groups, the limitation will be applied

based on the defined limit of the largest segment group.

Limits will not be applied in the following areas:

- Segment Builder inside the Drop Condition
- Segment Builder within the Audience Builder in Automated Flow

- Decision Split node within the Campaign Flow

adding new columns and a time filter to the search functionality. This will allow users to
access more detailed information in the reports and to filter logs based on specific time

ranges, improving the usability and accessibility of the data.

## Page 5

Sending geofence to segment

In geofence targeting, the goal is to send notifications to a specific audience when creating a
campaign. This development aims to allow targeted push notifications to individuals entering
an event area, such as inviting only selected people to showroom events for clients like

Borusan. As a result, only designated contacts or devices will receive notifications in specific

events or locations.

Business Requirements

Adding a Segment Selection Screen

- Asegment selection section should be added to the campaign creation screen specifically
for geofence targeting.

- When launching a geofence push campaign, users should be able to select their target
audience.

Audience Definition via Segments

- The geofence push campaign audience should be restricted based on a predefined

segment.

- For example, push notifications should only be sent to contacts within segments like
"Attendees from Borusan" or "Participants from Dengage."

Segment Integration into Campaign Flow

- Users should be able to select the target segments for geofence push notifications within

the campaign flow.

- The segment selection screen should allow choosing from previously created and saved
segments.

Alignment of Geofence Criteria with Segments

- Geofence targeting criteria should be aligned with segment criteria.

- For instance, if a segment is created for invited event attendees, the segment should only
be active when individuals enter the geofence area.

Workflow

1. Segment Selection: Users select the target audience from the segment selection screen
during campaign creation.
2. Geofence Area Definition: A geofence area is assigned to the selected segment, and

notifications are triggered only when individuals enter this area.

## Page 6

3. Push Notification: Only individuals who enter the geofence area and match the segment
criteria will receive a notification.

4. Analysis & Reporting: The success rate of sent notifications, recipient identities, and
geofence segment criteria are analyzed

## Page 9

Language Support for Onsite Template Content

anguage support has been added to onsite content. When the "Add Language" option is
clicked on an empty content screen, the user is presented with two options:
- Copy From Content: Copies the filled fields from the existing content to the new language.

- Create Blank Onsite Content: Creates entirely blank content of the same type.

The language addition option is displayed only if no language has been added yet. If multiple
languages already exist in the content, a new language can be added using the "+" button in

the language list.

Language Addition and Management Process
When the user clicks the "Add Language" option, a modal appears.

- This modal lists the languages added in Settings > Content Language.

- The user selects the desired language and fills in the content.

- If the required language is not listed, the user must activate it from Settings > Content
Language.

- The user can edit the content of added languages and deactivate them if necessary.

Mandatory Fields and Save Process

To save the content as "Save Draft" or "Publish", all required fields must be filled in for each

language.

- A default language can be set in Settings > Content Language.

- Newly created content starts with the designated default language.

- The user can change the default language in the language addition modal but cannot
remove it completely.

- Therefore, the checkbox next to the default language in the modal appears as disabled.

Copy From Content Option
If the "Copy From Contentâ€ option is selected:

- The filled fields from the existing content are copied to the new language.

- The user can edit and modify the copied content.

## Page 10

- The copying process only includes content fields and does not transfer custom
configurations or language settings.

Language Prioritization and Content Display
Content is displayed based on the following priority order:

1. Page Language: The system first checks the page language.

2. Browser Language: If the page language is unavailable, the system checks the browser
language.

3. Default Language: If no matching content is found, the system displays the default
language.

Acceptance Criteria

1. Language Addition Functionality

- When the user clicks the "Add Language" button, a modal should open.

- The modal should list the languages activated in Settings > Content Language.

- The user should be able to select a language.

- The user should be able to choose between the following options:
o Copy From Content: Copies existing content to create a new language version.
o Create Blank Onsite Content: Creates an entirely blank content entry.

- The user should be able to edit the added language content.

Content should not be saved as "Save Draft" or "Publish" unless all required fields in all

languages are filled.

2. Editing and Deactivating Languages

- The user should be able to edit the content of added languages.

- The user should be able to deactivate languages from the content management screen.
- Deactivated languages should not be used for content display.

- A deactivated language should be reactivated when needed.

3. Default Language Management
- A default language should be configurable in Settings > Content Language.
- Newly created content should start with the default language.

- The user should be able to change the default language in the modal but not remove it
completely.

- In the modal, the checkbox next to the default language should be disabled.

4. Content Display Rules

## Page 11

- When a user views content, the system should first display content based on the page
language.
- If the page language is unavailable, the system should use the browser language.

- If no content is available in the browser language, the default language should be used for
display.

USE CASES AND EXPECTED BEHAVIORS

General Description:

Within the Dengage platform, users can create marketing content (such as InApp, Onsite,

Email, SMS, Push) in multiple languages. Thanks to the newly developed AI-powered

automatic translation feature, users will be able to translate content automatically with AI
instead of translating manually.

This feature will be integrated into two different UI areas:

- As an AI translation checkbox on the â€œAdd Languageâ€ modal screen

## Page 15

- As an AI translation icon under each language card on the content detail screen

Usage Flow (Summary)
1. The user creates content.
2. They open the "Add Language" modal and select a new language.
3. On this screen, they choose between:
0 â€œCopy from Contentâ€ or
o â€œCreate Blank Contentâ€

4. After selecting languages, they can enable the â€œAutomatically translate all languages

using AIâ€ checkbox.
5. Each added language is displayed on the content screen.

6. Each language card includes an AI translation icon, allowing users to trigger translation

manually.

Use Cases and System Behaviors:
1. When "Copy from Content" is selected:
- The content from the default language is used as the reference.
- If the AI option is selected:

o All selected languages are automatically translated using AT.
- If the AI option is not selected:

o The same content is copied to other languages without translation.

2. When "Create Blank Content" is selected:
- If AI translation is selected:

o Blank content fields are created (translation may be triggered later).
- If AI translation is not selected:

o Blank content fields are created.

3. When a new language is added later:
- If the AI option is active:
o The new language content is automatically translated from the default language
using AI.
- If the AI option is not active:

o Content is either blank or copied (based on user selection).

4. When a language is deleted:
- All content related to the deleted language is removed.

- If re-added, the same logic above is re-applied.

## Page 16

5. When the user manually edits AI-translated content:
- The system saves this edit and flags the content as â€œmanually edited.â€
- If the user later tries to re-translate the same language using AI:
o Aconfirmation warning is displayed:
â€œThis will override your manually edited content. Continue?â€
o If confirmed, translation is re-executed via AI.

o If declined, the existing content is preserved.

6. Functions of the AI icon on the content detail screen:

- Each language tab includes an AI icon with two main functions:

a. Manual translation trigger:
If automatic AI translation was not enabled in the â€œAdd Languageâ€ screen, users can click

the icon to manually initiate AI translation per language.

b. Outdated content indicator:
When the source language content is updated, translations in other languages become
outdated.
- The Al icon changes state (e.g., yellow) to indicate this.
- Tooltip/message example:
â€œContent has been updated in the source language. Click to update translation.â€
7. When the source language content is updated:
- The system does not automatically re-translate other languages.
- The Al icons for other language cards change to the â€œoutdatedâ€ state.

- Users can manually click the icons to update the translations.
8. AI Translation Checkbox Behavior (Global Control):
In the â€œAdd Languageâ€ screen:

- If the checkbox is selected, all added languages are auto-translated.

In the content screen:

- If the AI checkbox is enabled, AI translation will be the default option for the next
language additions.
9. In case of an AI service error:

- The following message is shown:
â€œTranslation failed. Please try again.â€

- The content field remains empty.
- The user can retry the translation.

- Errors are logged in the developer console.

Reason for Development:

While creating On-Site campaigns, users select a campaign priority under the delivery
settings during the creation steps. There are three options available in this field: â€œlowâ€,
â€œmediumâ€, and â€œhighâ€. However, campaigns with the same priority are currently ranked based
on their creation time. For example, if Campaign A was created at 15:00 with "high" priority,
and Campaign B was created at 15:05 with the same "high" priority, Campaign B is displayed
as having higher priority.

The customer wants to manually adjust the priorities of all their campaigns and sort them

accordingly.

Proposed Solution:

General Flow:

- While creating an Onsite campaign, the user will not see the â€œCampaign Priorityâ€
dropdown in the delivery control step. Instead, only the limit-adding function will be
present.

Â« When the user clicks â€œNextâ€, they will proceed to the â€œSummaryâ€ step, and the delivery
control modal in this step will no longer display the priority explanation:

Screenshot

When the user clicks the â€œSaveâ€ button on the Summary screen to save the campaign, a
pop-up message will appear at the top of the screen indicating that the campaign has
been successfully created, along with its current position in the priority hierarchy. This

pop-up will also include a direct link to the "Priority" tab to edit the campaign's hierarchy.

Pop-up info text:
â€œYour campaign is currently ranked 4th. If you want to change the ranking, you can update it
from the Priority (link) page.â€

real-time and flow campaigns.

o Flow Campaigns: In the campaign report of the relevant node, button click counts,
button name, and iOS & Android URLs will be available.

o Real-Time Campaigns: In the campaign listing page, users can access the reporting
screen by clicking the analytics icon on the far right, where button click counts, button

name, and iOS & Android URLs can be viewed.

## Page 30

Adding Column Length Information to the Automated Job Screen

Automated Job screen, within the Data Export Node and Incremental Logs section, when
a template is selected, the columns and their data types are displayed, but the column
lengths are missing.

Adding column length information to this screen will provide users with the following
advantages:

1. Customization and Table Mapping: Displaying column lengths along with the column
names will allow customers to create a table on their side and map the data correctly. This

ensures consistency between the exported data and their internal structure.

2. Easier Error Diagnosis: If the job encounters an error like "value too long," users will be

able to quickly check the column lengths on the screen and diagnose the issue.

Column Details

Suggested Changes:

## Page 31

1. New Column for Length Information: A new column will be added to display the length

information. This column will show the length for each column.

2. Storing Length Information in the Database: Column lengths will be stored in the
database, and these values will be fetched and displayed on the front-end.

Column Name and Unit Analysis:

- New Column Name: The name for the new column displaying length information could be
"Column Length".

- Unit for Different Data Types:
o Integer: n/a
o String: For string columns, the unit will be the maximum character length of the column
(e.g., "255" for a string with a maximum length of 255 characters).

o Boolean: n/a
Error Message: "Value Too Long"

This error message is triggered when the length of data in a column exceeds the predefined
length in the database. For example, if a string column has a maximum length of 7 characters
and an attempt is made to insert a value with 8 characters, the database will reject the data
and show an error message.

Error Message Details:
- Message Title: Value Too Long
- Message Description:

o This error indicates that the value entered for the specified column exceeds the defined
length for that column.

Adding Contact Key to Email, Push, and SMS Event Logs

The customer is currently able to report based on contact_key by correlating the id or
msg_id from Email Send Targets with the id or msg_id from Email Events. However, the

customer wants to see the contact_key directly in the Email Events logs, and at this point,

contact_key is not available. Therefore, the customer has requested the addition of

contact_key in the logs for Email Events, Push Events, and SMS Events. With this

development, the customer will be able to directly access contact_key across all channels

(Email, Push, SMS), making data tracking and reporting processes more manageable. This

will enhance data accessibility and consistency while providing users with more flexible

## Page 33

Push Inbox - Delete and Mark All Notifications as Read Functionality

Dengage Push Inbox - Delete and Mark All Notifications as Read Functionality Analysis

1. Purpose The goal is to add bulk delete and mark-as-read functionalities to the Push Inbox
feature in Dengage. With this enhancement, users will be able to delete all notifications at

once or mark them as read in their inbox.
2. Scope

The backend team will develop two new endpoints:

o Delete All Notifications Endpoint
o Mark All Notifications as Read Endpoint
- These endpoint details will be provided to the SDK team for integration.

The frontend will include UI components to enable users to utilize these functions.

3. Technical Details

- Backend Development:
o Requests will be processed on a per-user basis.
o The delete operation will be permanent and irreversible.
o The mark-as-read operation will update all unread notifications of the user to "read"
status.
- SDK Integration:
o The SDK team will receive endpoint details and required parameters.

o The SDK will use these endpoints to support delete and mark-as-read operations.
4. User Scenarios

- The user presses the "Delete All" button in the Push Inbox screen, the system sends a
request to the backend, and all notifications are deleted.
- The user presses the "Mark All as Read" button, a request is sent to the backend, and all

notifications are marked as read.

5. Test Scenarios

Verify that all notifications are successfully deleted.

Verify that all notifications are successfully marked as read.

- Test user authorization controls.

- Check data synchronization in multi-device scenarios.

Purpose of the Requirement:

Our customers were previously able to send WhatsApp content through third-party
applications such as CM and Karix integrated into our site. At this point, there is a need for
this development for users who do not have CM or Karix accounts or who want to perform

these sends directly through Dengage.

Solution:

After this development, Dengage users willbe able to goto Settings > 3rd Party

Integrations > WhatsApp and select â€œNew WSPâ€ to access the modal for the
WhatsApp Business API, fill in the required configuration fields, and add their target audience

information (sender name) to complete the integration.
Once the integration is complete, users will be able to create WhatsApp content directly from

Dengage without needing third-party integrations such as CM or Karix, by accessing

Content > Messaging > WhatsApp from the main menu.

Approved content by Meta can be used for campaign sends similar to other content types
(SMS/Email).

Development Stages:

1. PRE-REQ:

a. If it is a flag-based development, the flag must be enabled.
b. The customer must be a WhatsApp Business API member. This can be done via Meta
Developer. Details can be found at:

Â© Become a Tech Provider
This link and explanation should be placed in the info section and be clickable.

2. INTEGRATION:

## Page 57

Superset Analytics Authorization Rules

This document defines the authorization structure and access control rules for users of the

Superset Analytics product within the Dengage platform.

Authorization Model Overview

- All built-in dashboards, charts, and datasets will be automatically created and managed by
a Dengage Admin account.

- These assets will be owned by the Dengage Admin account.

- Authorization is enforced based on ownership. Users cannot edit objects they do not own.

Customer User Access Rules
Roles

- Write Permission

- Read Permission

Restrictions

- Customer users, even with write permissions, cannot edit the dashboards, charts, or
datasets owned by the Dengage Admin.

- These built-in assets will be read-only to all non-owner accounts.

- Users can only duplicate dashboards or charts using the â€œSave Asâ€ feature to create their
own copies.

SQL Lab Access

- Users with write access will have access to SQL Lab, enabling them to create virtual
datasets from queries.

- However, their access will be restricted to specific tables only. They will not have access to
the full schema.
Custom Metrics & Calculations

- If a user wants to create and save a new metric at dataset level, they must submit a
request to Dengage.

- Users can perform temporary calculations within chart visualizations.

- These calculations cannot be saved globally or reused across multiple charts.

## Page 63

AppsFlyer Integration

This document outlines the proposed one-way integration between AppsFlyer and Dengage

to ingest attribution metadata such as Media_Source , Campaign,
af_channel , and install_time into Dengage contact profiles. The goal is to

enable customers to create meaningful segments and launch personalized campaigns based
on user acquisition data.

This integration is possible to support two models:

1. Pull-based integration (via scheduled backend API calls)
2. Push-based integration (pending AppsFlyer partner status)
Customers want to leverage mobile attribution data to:

- Identify which ad network or campaign brought in each user
- Create dynamic segments (e.g., "Facebook-acquired users")
- Run targeted push/in-app/SMS campaigns

- Personalize journey flows based on acquisition source

Integration Scenarios

1. Pull-Based Integration

Dengage will retrieve attribution data from AppsFlyer using the Pull API.
Process:

1. The mobile app sets CUuStomer_USer_id via the AppsFlyer SDK.

2. Backend retrieves install data using:
o API:

https://hq.appsflyer.com/export/{app_id}/install_data/v
be)

3. The data includes, but is not limited to:

o customer_user_id

o media_Source -e.g., facebook, googleadwords_int
o Campaign -full campaign name

o af_channel - campaign channel (if set)

o install_time -UTC timestamp

## Page 64

o af_sub1 to af_Sub5 - optional custom tracking parameters
o appsflyer_id -device-level ID
4. Data is pushed to Dengage using the Contact API, with mapping:
o contactKey = customer_user_id
o Additional fields added as custom attributes
5. Users are dynamically segmented (e.g.. media_source = facebook )

6. Campaigns and journeys leverage this data

Notes:

- This approach depends on AppsFlyer data availability and scheduling

- Requires backend resources to data retrieval and formatting

2. Push-Based Integration (Requires Partner Status)

If Dengage becomes an official AppsFlyer partner, we can receive real-time attribution

postbacks.

Proposed Process:

1. AppsFlyer sends an HTTP postback to Dengage whenever an install occurs.

2. Postback payload includes:

o Customer_user_id, media_source , campaign, af_channel ,

install_time , etc.

3. Dengage updates the user profile using the Contact API.

4. Real-time segmentation and campaign personalization can be applied instantly.

Benefits:

- Real-time attribution sync

- No customer backend required

- Simpler setup for multi-app clients
Next Steps:

- Customer referral used to initiate partnership application
- Define postback format and endpoint with AppsFlyer

- Enable for selected accounts and scale to others

Summary

Scenario Pull-Based Push-Based

## Page 68

Winner Logic (Z-test Explanation)
Statistical Model

Model uses a two-proportion Z-test to compare the click-through rate (CTR) of each variant
to every other variant (not to control). A winner is declared only if one variant outperforms all

others with statistical significance.

Formula

Where

Â« pi = Conversion rate of Variant A = clicks_A / users_A
Â« p2 = Conversion rate of Variant B = clicks_B / users_B
Â¢ Ni, n2 = Number of users in Variant A and B
Â¢ X1, X2 = Number of clicks in Variant A and B

- p (p-hat) = Pooled conversion rate (x1+x2)/(n1+n2)

Example Calculations
1. Compare Variant A vs Variant B:

- Variant A: 200 users, 30 clicks > p, = 0.15
- Variant B: 200 users, 25 clicks > p2 = 0.125

2. Compare Variant A vs Variant C:

- Variant C: 200 users, 20 clicks > p3 = 0.10

Repeat for B vs. C if necessary.

Triggers

Overview

This document defines the complete list of triggers available for Dengage's One-to-One

on user behaviors, profile changes, system events, and external calls.

- No delivery events like "sent" or "delivered".

Special Rules for E-commerce Triggers

Cart Abandoned
- Abandonment Timing is Based on Inactivity:
o Trigger checks time since last cart activity.
o If no cart change or page action for configured timeout (1 hour customizable), it fires.
- Activity Resets the Timer:
o If user modifies cart (adds/removes products) within timeout window, the timer resets.
o If user browses product pages or site, timer resets.
- Example Timeline:
o 0:00 > User adds Product A > Timer (1 hour) starts.
o 0:40 > User adds Product B > Timer resets.
o 1:10 > User browses another product > Timer resets.
o 2:10 > No activity > Cart abandoned trigger fires.
- Important:
o Trigger only fires once after full inactivity.

o Real-time updates needed for dynamic cart reflection.

## Page 79

Purchase Not Completed - Trigger Rules
- Checkout Started:
o User clicks checkout or payment button.
o But no completed PurchaseOrder event received.

- Timeout Logic:

o Must define an acceptable completion time (30 minutes default and customizable).
- Activity Based:

o If user abandons during checkout (leaves cart during payment), trigger fires.

## Page 81

Attribution Models: Click vs. View

View-Through Attribution
- Counts conversion if message was sent, even if the user did not open or click, as long as:
o Conversion happened within attribution window (default: 72h).

o Message belongs to same journey.

Journey sends Email > user doesnâ€™t click ~ user completes purchase within 48h >

conversion is counted

Click-Through Attribution
- Counts conversion only if user clicked the message (within window).

- Preferred for performance-focused marketing.

Journey sends Push ~ user clicks the notification + user completes purchase within 48h >

conversion counts.

Attribution Window
- Each conversion goal in a journey has an attribution window (default: 72 hours).

- If the user completes the conversion within this timeframe after any message (email, push,
etc.), it counts.

- Windows are configurable per journey or per node.

Example:

- Journey A sends an email.

- Conversion goal = "Purchase Completed"
- Attribution window = 72 hours

- User purchases after 48 hours > counts as conversion.

How Dengage Handles Conversion in Multiple Journeys

If the same conversion (e.g., "Purchase Completed") is used as a goal in multiple journeys,

and a user is active in several of them, Dengage applies the following logic:

1. Attribution Priority Model (Configurable)

- Last Touch (Default): The most recent journey that sent a message within the attribution

window will get credit.
- First Touch: The first journey that sent a message after entry will take credit.

- All Journeys (Multi-Touch): All eligible journeys receive conversion attribution
independently.

## Page 82

2. Per-Journey Qualification
Each journey independently checks:

- Was a message sent from this journey?
- Was the conversion event performed within this journeyâ€™s attribution window?

- Was click/view tracking logic met?

A journey cannot claim conversion unless it sent a qualifying message, even if the same

event is configured elsewhere.

3. Scenarios

User in 3 Journeys (A, B, C). All target the same event: Purchase Completed

o Asends Email on Day 1

o B sends SMS on Day 2

o C sends Push on Day 3

o User purchases on Day 4

o â€” Journey C gets credit (last touch)

If Multi-Touch enabled:

o All three (A, B, C) get credit individually

o Each logs its own attribution tracking

If First Touch enabled:

o â€” Journey A gets credit, even if others sent messages later

Conversion and Exit Rules

Conversion Definition in Dengage:

- Aconversion is a user performing a predefined action (PurchaseOrder, EmailClick,
WishlistSave, Custom Events, or entering a segment) that is marked as a "conversion goal"
within the journey.

- Conversion events can be defined per journey and tracked globally for reporting.

Attribution Window:

## Page 97

- Users can convert within a defined timeframe after receiving a message.

- Default attribution window: 72 hours (changeable).

Exit Rules:
- Exit on Conversion: Users automatically exit the journey after conversion.
- Conditional Exit: Users can define which node or point of conversion ends the flow.

- No Exit: Users can continue in the journey after conversion (optional toggle).

Capping & Reentry

To avoid spamming and over-automation, Dengage will implement journey participation
control logic:

Supported Settings per Journey:

- Single Entry Only (default): Users enter once only, based on trigger match.
- Re-entry after X time: E.g., a user can re-enter 7 days after previous exit.

- Re-entry only if conversion not met: Block re-entry if converted in last run.

- Limit by count: Max entries per user (e.g., 3 times per month).

Advanced Options:
- Allow re-entry on different event type (e.g., AddToBasket vs ProductView)

- Segment filter for suppression: â€œUsers already in journey Xâ€

Reporting
Create a dedicated reporting screen for One-to-One Journeys that includes:

- Total Entrants

- Channel Engagement

- Exit Rate

- Conversion

- Node-Level Entry & Completion Stats

- Funnel Drop-off Visualization

User-Level Journey Reporting

Feature Overview:

- Enables marketers to search for a specific contact/user and view a timeline-style
visualization of their journey participation.

- Displays when a user entered the journey, which nodes were triggered, where they

dropped off or converted, and any messages sent or actions taken.

- Journey timeline view showing sequential actions with timestamps.

- Each journey instance shows:

o Entry event and time

o All triggered nodes and status (completed, skipped, waiting)

o Conversion event (if applicable)

o Exit reason or completion time

## Page 110

Push - Custom Parameters

The Custom Parameters feature in Push Notifications allows you to add extra data to your
push messages beyond the standard fields (title, message, etc.). These parameters are sent

along with the push and can be used by your application for custom behaviors.

With Custom Parameters, you can:

- Pass additional information (e.g., how to open a link).

- Customize how the push is displayed by handling it yourself in your app (instead of letting
the SDK render it).

- Track specific events or attributes for analytics.

- Send design or functionality details (e.g., background color, image URL, button behavior)
that your app can interpret.

The SDK only delivers these parameters. What happens next is completely decided by your
appâ€™s development team.

How to Access

1. Navigate to:
Content > Mobile/Web Push > New.

2. On the Content screen, scroll to the section called Custom Parameters.

How to Configure Custom Parameters

Step 1: Define Custom Parameters in Settings

1. Go to Settings > Campaign Configurations > Push Custom Parameters.
2. Click Add to define a parameter.

3. Enter:

o Key > The name of the parameter.
o Default Value > A default value to appear when creating new pushes.

4. Click Add to save, or Cancel to discard.

These parameters will then appear by default whenever you create a new push message.

Step 2: Add or Edit Custom Parameters in a Push

1. When creating a new push (Content > Mobile/Web Push > New), go to the Custom

Parameters section.

## Page 111

2. You will see the predefined parameters (from settings) already listed.

3. You can:
o Edit default values for this push.
o Add new parameters that are specific to this campaign.

o Remove parameters if not needed.

Example Use Cases
- Custom Rendering: If you donâ€™t want the SDK to show the push, you can handle it
yourself. For example, define a parameter like:
o background_color = #FFOOOO
o image_url = https://example.com/banner.png
Then, your app will display the push with that background and image.
- Button Behavior: Add a parameter like:
0 Open_type = browser (open in external browser)
0 Open_type = in_app (open inside the app)

- Tracking: Pass custom event data that your app will log for analytics.

Custom Parameters are defined in Settings and appear automatically in new push
campaigns. They allow you to send extra data with a push. Your app decides what to do with
these parameters (custom rendering, analytics, logic, etc.). Default parameters can be

predefined, and additional ones can be added or removed per campaign.

This feature gives flexibility to developers who want to customize the push notification
experience beyond the standard SDK rendering.

Developer Assistance Needed

Implementing these parameters requires developer assistance to ensure the custom data is
properly handled and triggers the intended actions.

Content Display Rules

Content is displayed based on the following priority order:

language.

language.

Preventing Reuse of Last 3 Passwords

To help protect your account, the system now prevents the reuse of your last three

passwords. This policy encourages stronger password practices and reduces security risks.

How It Works
Password Change Validation
When you try to set a new password:

1. Your new password is securely encrypted and compared with the protected versions of
your last three passwords.

2. The password change request is:

o Approved if your new password has not been used recently.

o Rejected if it matches any of your last 3 passwords.
Password History Management

After a successful password change:

1. The encrypted version of your new password is added to your history.

2. If more than 3 passwords are stored, the oldest one is removed to keep only the most
recent three.

This enhanced password policy is designed to protect your account from unauthorized
access and promote better security habits. Keeping your passwords fresh and unique helps

ensure your information stays safe and secure.

## Page 139

Adding Column Length Information to the Automated Job Screen - User
Guide

To improve data accuracy and make troubleshooting easier, the Automated Flows screen
now includes column length information alongside column names and data types. This
update applies to the Data Export Node and Incremental Logs and helps users correctly
map their tables and quickly identify errors like "Value Too Long."

Adding column length information to this screen provides the following advantages:

- Customization and Table Mapping: Displaying column lengths with the column names
allows users to build tables on their side and ensure accurate mapping. This helps maintain

consistency between the exported data and their internal structure.

- Easier Error Diagnosis: If a job fails due to a "value too long" error, users can easily

check the column lengths on the screen to diagnose the issue.

How to Access

1. Go to Data Space.

2. Navigate to the Automated Flows Screen.
3. Select the Data Export Node section.

4. Click on Incremental Logs.

5. Choose a template from the list.

Once a template is selected, the system will display the column details, including:
- Column Name

- Column Type

- Column Length (new field added)

Session Termination After Password Change - User Guide

To enhance account security and protect user data, the system now terminates all active
sessions when a user changes their password. This means that after updating the
password, the user will be logged out of all sessions and must re-login using the new
password. This update is an important step in preventing unauthorized access and

maintaining account integrity.

How to Access
Settings > My Profile > Change Password

- Navigate to Settings.

Â« Click on My Profile.

- Select Change Password.

- Enter the new desired password.

- Confirm the new password and save changes.

Once the password change is confirmed, the system will automatically log the user out of
all active sessions. The user must sign in again using the new password to continue using

the system.

This change ensures that any unauthorized access using previous sessions is immediately

cut off after a password update, helping to keep your account secure.

Roles and Permissions â€” Manage Table without PII

Previously, when assigning the Manage Table permission under Roles & Permissions, the
system automatically required enabling Show PII Data permission as well. With this update,
the dependency between these two permissions has been removed. You can now grant
users access to manage data tables without giving them access to view Personally
Identifiable Information (PII).

- This allows more flexible role creation by separating data management capabilities from
sensitive data visibility.

unless Show PII Data is explicitly granted.

Adding a Second Phone Number Under the Same Application in the Platform

When a new phone number is selected from the From dropdown in the API Setup, both the Phone Number ID and
the WhatsApp Business Account ID (WABA ID) will change based on the selected number.

If you want to add an additional number to the same application via the Dengage platform, follow these steps:

1. Go to Integration > 3rd Party Integration > WhatsApp.
2. Click the "New WSP" button to add a new WhatsApp sender profile.
3. Under the WhatsApp Information section:

o Enter a Configuration Name for the new setup.

o App ID and Access Token will remain the same. You can copy these from the existing configuration and paste

them here.

o Update the Phone Number ID and the WhatsApp Business Account ID (WABA ID) fields using the values
associated with the new phone number from Meta Developers Account.

4. After filling in the required fields, click the Add Account button to complete the process.
Important Note:

If the newly created application is linked to an existing WhatsApp Business account, all phone numbers connected to
that account will automatically appear in the From dropdown under the API Setup section in the Meta Developer
Console.

As a result, all content associated with the existing phone number(s) will be visible in the Dengage WhatsApp

Content section. This is because content visibility is determined by the Phone Number.

However, when a new phone number is added and linked through the same application using the method described
above, only content tied to that specific number will be visible. In this setup, it behaves as if a different partner is

using the system, keeping content visibility limited to that number.

WhatsApp Template (Content) Listing Page

The WhatsApp Content section allows you to manage all the WhatsApp messages youâ€™ve created for your campaigns.
This includes content intended for different purposes such as marketing, transactional (utility), or authentication. You
can view important details, filter by specific criteria, and prepare your content for use in campaignsâ€”all from one

place.
How to Access

To access the WhatsApp Content section, navigate to the left-hand menu and go to Content > Messaging >
WhatsApp. This will open the WhatsApp Content listing page where all your previously created content is displayed in
a structured table.

Listing Page

The listing page displays the following columns and features:

- Name: The title of your WhatsApp message. This helps you easily identify each content item.

- Type: Indicates the category of your message: whether it is a Marketing, Utility (Transactional), or Authentication

type.

## Page 158

- Status: Displays the current status of the content. This can be:
- Approved:the content has successfully passed Metaâ€™s review and is ready to be used.
- Awaiting Approval:The content has been submitted and is currently under review by Meta.
- Rejected:
The content did not pass Metaâ€™s approval process. You can edit your content or create a new one using the "+ New"

button.

- Languages

selects the appropriate version based on the following logic: first, it checks the userâ€™s language setting; if that is not
available, it falls back to the accountâ€™s default language; and if neither is defined, it uses the first language listed in
the template. This ensures the most suitable language is used when sending messages. The Languages section
displays all the languages the message is available inâ€”if you've created the same message in multiple languages,

they will all be shown here.

Creating WhatsApp Content

To create a new WhatsApp template, navigate to the left-hand menu and go to Content > Messaging > WhatsApp.

from three template categories, depending on the purpose of your message.

May include promotions or Facilitate a specific, agreed-

Marketing: This type is suitable for messages that include promotions, special offers, back-in-stock alerts, or
invitations for customers to take action or reply. These templates are designed to encourage engagement and often

require user interaction.

Utility: Utility templates are used for transactional purposes. They are intended to fulfill a specific request or provide
an update related to a transaction the customer has already agreed toâ€”such as order confirmations, payment

receipts, shipping notifications, or appointment reminders.

Authentication: This type is used to verify users with one-time passcodes (OTP). Authentication templates are
helpful in login flows or identity verification steps, especially when users must be verified at multiple stages during

access or registration processes.

For transactional message sending, both Utility and Authentication templates are used. However, if a Utility template
contains promotional or marketing content, Meta may automatically reclassify it as a Marketing template during the
review process. This categorization is done automatically by Meta. As a result, in the WhatsApp Content listing page,

you will see the final template type as determined by Meta, regardless of the initial selection.

Select the most appropriate category for your message based on your use case. Once selected, you will proceed to
the next step, where you'll define the template name, language, and message content details.

Important Notes About WhatsApp Templates

- Approved templates can be edited, but with limits. You can make changes up to 10 times within 30 days, or only
once within a 24-hour period.

- Rejected or paused templates can be edited as many times as needed, with no restrictions.

- If you delete a template, you will not be able to reuse the same name and language combination for 4 weeks.
WhatsApp blocks the use of deleted name-language combinations during this time.

- When creating a new template, make sure the template name is clean and valid. Avoid using special characters or
unnecessary formatting. This is known as sanitizing the name.

- You can only edit a templateâ€™s category and components (like header, body, footer, buttons). However, if a template
has already been approved, you cannot change its category anymore. Also, you cannot change the name of a
template once it is created.

Additional Information
- The default language of the content will automatically match the account's current default language during

creation.

Creating Whatsapp Authentication Template

To create a new WhatsApp template for authentication purposes, navigate to the left-hand menu and go to Content
> Messaging > WhatsApp. On the WhatsApp Content page, click the + New button at the top-right corner. A modal
window will appear prompting you to choose a template category. Select Authentication.

Authentication templates are used to send one-time passcodes (OTPs) or verification codes to help users securely
log into your app or verify their identity. These templates are designed to support a smooth and secure login or

transaction flow.
Once you select the Authentication category, a new screen will open where you will configure the template.

At the top, under the General section, enter your Name and choose the WhatsApp Account you want to use. If
needed, you can change the account by clicking the Change Account button. Once you're ready, click Next to
continue to the Content section.

By default, the template language is set to English. You can add more languages by clicking the â€œ+â€ button and

selecting them from the modal. After selection, click Apply to include them.
Message Type

For Authentication templates, there are two message types available:

- Copy Code
This type allows you to send a one-time passcode or verification code along with a copy button. When the user
taps the button, the code is copied to their clipboard for easy pasting into your app.

- One-Tap Autofill
This is the recommended method for the smoothest user experience. When a customer taps the autofill button in
the message, the code is sent directly to your app without requiring manual input.
If Zero-Tap is enabled in your system, the code can be sent automatically, without requiring the user to tap
anything.

If autofill is not possible, the system will automatically fall back to sending a Copy Code message instead.

Each message type is optimized to provide secure and user-friendly authentication, and you can choose the one that
best fits your appâ€™s login flow.

The rest of the content configurationâ€”including variables, buttons, and optional footerâ€”follows the same structure as
described in the Blank Content setup. These components allow for personalized messages and interaction, which will
be covered in detail in the next sections.

Copy Code

After selecting Copy Code as the message type in your Authentication template, you will configure the OTP delivery
settings and message structure. This message type is ideal for sending one-time passcodes (OTP) that users can
easily copy and paste during login or verification.

Creating Marketing Campaign Flow with WhatsApp Send Node

To send WhatsApp messages through a campaign flow, follow the steps below to set up your campaign using the
WhatsApp Send Node.

Start a New Campaign Flow

Go to the left-hand menu and navigate to Campaign > Flows. Click the + New button to create a new flow. You will be
prompted to choose the campaign type:
- One Time â€” Send the campaign once at a specific time.

- Recurring â€” Set the campaign to repeat automatically.

## Page 170

Campaign Info
Fill in the basic campaign details:

- Flow Name: Enter a name for your campaign flow.
- Folder (optional): Organize your flow under a selected folder.

- Tags (optional): Add tags to help with reporting and tracking.

Schedule Options
Choose when your One-Time campaign should run:

- Now - Launch the campaign immediately.

- Scheduled - Set a specific time and date using the calendar.

When setting up a recurring WhatsApp campaign, the Schedule Options section allows you to define how and when
the campaign should be triggered and repeated.
- Trigger Periodically: Enable this to schedule the campaign to run on a repeating basis.
- Start Date: Choose when the recurring campaign should begin. You can set it to:
o Now: Starts immediately.
o Scheduled: Choose a specific date and time from the calendar.
- End Date: Define when the recurring campaign should stop.
o Never: The campaign continues indefinitely until manually stopped.
o Scheduled: Set a specific end date.
- Recurring Periods: Click Add to define how often the campaign should repeat (e.g., daily, weekly, monthly).
- Trigger Externally: Use this option if the campaign should be triggered by a fire campaign action.
- Time Zone-Based Delivery: Enable this if you want the campaign to be delivered based on each userâ€™s local time

zone, ensuring messages are sent at appropriate times for every contact.

Click Next to proceed to the flow canvas.

Define the Audience

On the Flow Canvas, you'll start configuring your campaign by defining the audience. Double-click the Audience
node to open its settings. You'll see several options to define who should receive the WhatsApp message:

- Segment

- Predefined Segment

- Table

- Remote Segment

- Tag

After selecting your target audience, use the Calculate button to estimate how many contacts have valid WhatsApp

numbers and are eligible to receive the message.
Within the same Audience configuration panel, you'll find two additional tools: Exclude and Control Group.

The Exclude section lets you filter out specific groups to make sure certain users donâ€™t receive the campaign. You can:
- Exclude a specific Segment

- Exclude a Remote Segment from an external source

- Exclude contacts from a previous Campaign

At the bottom of the Message Details screen, you'll find the Optional Settings section. These options allow you to

fine-tune how your WhatsApp messages are delivered to your audience.

- Remove Duplicate Phone Numbers

When this option is enabled, the system will automatically detect and remove duplicate phone numbers from your

selected audience list. This ensures that each contact receives your message only once, preventing multiple sends to

the same number within the same campaign.

## Page 174

- Ignore Frequency Capping

Enabling this setting allows WhatsApp messages to be sent even if a contact has reached their daily, weekly, or
monthly messaging limit. Normally, frequency capping prevents over-sending by limiting how often a user can
receive messages. By choosing to ignore frequency caps, the system will bypass these restrictions and send the

message regardless of past send activity.

Use this option with care, particularly in promotional campaigns, to avoid overwhelming users with excessive

messages.

These optional controls are helpful when you need to ensure delivery for specific use cases, exceptions, or time-

sensitive campaigns.

Approval screen. This step allows you to double-check your content, language versions, and dynamic field mappings

to ensure everything is correct.

## Page 178

GDPR User Guide

Dengage GDPR

The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is a comprehensive data protection law
enforced across the European Union (EU) that gives individuals greater control over their
personal data. It outlines specific rights for individuals and applies to all organizations that

operate in the EU or handle the personal data of EU residents.

A key operational component of GDPR is the Data Subject Request (DSR)â€”an action taken
by individuals (data subjects) to exercise their rights under data protection laws. These rights

include accessing, correcting, deleting, or transferring their personal data.

This user guide explains how to comply with GDPR requirements within our platform. It
provides practical steps for addressing Data Subject Requests (DSRs), such as data access,

deletion, and outlines how to configure platform features to align with GDPR standards.

Understanding GDPR Roles in Your Dengage Integration

This guide explains how the key roles defined under the General Data Protection Regulation
(GDPR)â€”Data Subject, Data Controller, and Data Processorâ€”relate to your integration with
Dengage. Understanding these roles is essential for ensuring that personal data is handled
lawfully, transparently, and in line with individualsâ€™ rights, especially when responding to Data
Subject Requests (DSRs).

Data Subject

In the context of GDPR, the Data Subject refers to the individual whose personal data is
being collected and processed by your organization. This person has the right to submit
DSRs, which may include requests to access, correct, or delete their personal data. Before
any action is taken in response to such a request, it is critical that the Data Subject is

properly authenticated.

Data Controller

As the organization using Dengage, you are considered the Data Controller. This means
you are the party that decides why and how personal data should be processed. When a

Data Subject submits a DSR, it is your responsibility to receive, verify, and respond to that

## Page 179

request. Your role includes ensuring that the request is handled appropriately and that the

outcome is clearly communicated back to the individual.

Data Processor

Dengage serves as the Data Processor in this relationship. This means it processes personal
data on your behalf and according to your instructions. Dengage does not make
independent decisions regarding how data is handled. Instead, it provides the necessary
infrastructure, such as tools, APIs, or platform functionalities, to help you fulfill DSRs.
Whether it involves exporting user data, deleting specific profiles, or updating records,

Dengage assists in executing your directions in a secure and compliant manner.

Standard User Definition for DSR Handling

When managing Data Subject Requests (DSRs) under GDPR, itâ€™s essential to have a clear
and consistent definition of who qualifies as a "user"â€”also known as the data subject. In
this context, a user refers to any identifiable individual whose personal data is processed,
stored, or tracked within your systems or platforms. Proper identification and authentication
of these individuals are critical to ensuring that DSRs are handled securely and in compliance

with legal obligations.

Identifying a User

A user may be identified by one or more unique identifiers. Common identifiers include user
IDs, customer IDs, email addresses, or phone numbers. These values allow you to map

and retrieve all relevant data associated with the individual.

Scope of Data

The scope of a DSR covers all personal data linked to the identified user. This means
consolidating information from various touchpoints where the user's data might exist.

Ensuring a comprehensive scope helps maintain full compliance with GDPR requirements.

Authentication Requirements

Before fulfilling any DSR, it is essential to verify the identity of the requester.
Authentication protects against malicious attempts to access someone else's personal data.
The level of authentication should be appropriate to the sensitivity of the data and the nature

of the request.

Applicable User Types

## Page 180

Users eligible to submit DSRs are not limited to registered customers. They can include:

- Registered users who have accounts or profiles
- Anonymous visitors, if they can be identified through device IDs, cookie IDs, or similar
tracking technologies

- Mobile app users tracked via unique identifiers or analytics tools

Primary Identifiers

Different types of users are identified through different key identifiers, which serve as the

primary reference points for locating personal data:

- For registered users, common identifiers include email addresses, usernames, or user
IDs assigned by your system.

- Anonymous users may be identified using cookie IDs, IP addresses, or session IDs
collected during their interactions.

- Mobile users are typically identified via device IDs or app user tokens generated by
mobile applications.

- For customers stored in your CRM system, identifiers such as customer IDs, loyalty
program IDs, or phone numbers are used to locate data.

- In e-commerce contexts, a combination of order ID and email address is often used to

uniquely identify a user and their associated personal data.

Understanding these primary identifiers helps ensure the accurate retrieval and processing

of data when handling DSRs across platforms and user types.

Data Deletion (Right to Be Forgotten)

This feature allows users to request permanent deletion of their personal data to comply with
privacy regulations such as GDPR. When a deletion request is submitted, all personal data
related to that userâ€”including contacts, devices, and user eventsâ€”will be permanently

removed from all storage locations

Compliance

Our system supports this right by allowing you to request the permanent deletion of your

personal data.

After stopping data collection, you can submit a deletion request to permanently remove your
user profile and all related dataâ€”including contact details, device information, and user

activity logsâ€”from all our data stores.

## Page 181

What Happens When You Submit a Deletion Request?

When you submit a deletion request, the system schedules your data for permanent removal.
This includes all contact records, device information, and event data related to you. The

deletion will be completed within 30 days.

There is a 7-day cancellation window after you submit the request. During these 7 days, no
data will be deleted yet. If you change your mind, you can cancel the deletion request within

this period.

How to Submit a Deletion Request

To start deleting your data, you need to create an erasure request. This tells the system to
permanently delete the profile and all associated information.

You can do this using the CreateErasureRequest API:

- This is a POST request to
https://api.dengage.com/rest/opendsr/requests .

- It creates a new deletion request for the specified user.

How to Check the Status of a Deletion Request

You can keep track of your deletion requestâ€™s progress to see if it is still Pending or
InProgress, has been Completed, Failed or Cancelled.

Use the GetRequestStatus API:

- This is a GET request to
https://api.dengage.com/rest/opendsr/status/{subjectRequ
estId}.

- The response tells you the current status of your request.

How to Cancel a Deletion Request

If a deletion request was submitted in error, you can cancel it within 7 days from the request

date. No data will be deleted during this cancellation window.

To cancel, use the CancelErasureRequest API:

- Make a DELETE request to
https://api.dengage.com/rest/opendsr/requests/{subjectRe
questid} .

## Page 182

- Cancelling within the 7 days stops the deletion process.

If not cancelled, the deletion proceeds automatically after 7 days.

Additional Information

To learn more about the system capabilities and compliance details, you can use the

GetDiscovery API:

- Make a GET request to
https://api.dengage.com/rest/opendsr/discovery .

- This returns information about supported OpenDSR features.

Improved Login Redirection

With the new improved login redirection feature, users who access Dengage will now

experience better redirection after login.

Previously, even if a user was already logged in, clicking on the login link or being redirected
for authentication would still keep them on the /login page. Also, when a user logged out

back in, they will return to the last page they were on before logging out.

allowing users to pick up exactly where they left off.

In CRM Dynamics synchronizing with CDMP, we are synchronizing four different objects
(leads, contacts, accounts, and opportunities).

When a user starts synchronizing from the CDMP account, in the background new orders
are generated in the database. Background service will read these new coming orders
from the database.

After that, this thread will fetch the data from Shopify in the form of chunks and then store
them in the Dengage database.

There is another thread running after every 10 minutes. This gets the last sync time and
adds the interval of 10 minutes as the next sync time.

Based on the last sync time and next sync time, this thread fetches those records which
are created or updated within this period.

Users can see the history of all these synchronizations on the Sync History Page.

CRM Marketing Lists:

CDMP also supports marketing lists synchronizing with CDMP. A background service is

responsible to fetch all marketing lists from the dynamics CRM to CDMP and save them in

Dengage database. These lists get updated every day in order to synchronize with dynamics
CRM.

Targeting Onsite A/B Test User Guide

The A/B Test feature enables you to test multiple content variations in an (targeting) on-site
campaign to identify the best-performing version. By distributing your audience across
different variants and analyzing their engagement, you can optimize content effectiveness
and improve conversion rates. The system uses statistical analysis to automatically

determine the winning variant or allows manual winner selection if needed.

How to Access

How to Use

schedule, website, platform (web or mobile web), audience, and trigger time. These are

standard setup steps before enabling A/B testing.

- Toggle A/B Testing ON to test multiple content variants.

- Metric: Currently, only click-based conversion is supported.

- Control Group: The control group represents users who have not shown any content.

Used exclusively for benchmarking and excluded from winner selection.

- Evaluation Criteria:

o Each variant must reach at least 100 visitors and 25 conversions before evaluation.

## Page 216

o A variant wins if it outperforms all others with 295% confidence.
o If no winner emerges, testing continues, or you can manually select a winner.

- Auto-Close: Tests close automatically after 30 days if no winner is found.

Winner Logic
Statistical Model

The system uses a two-proportion Z-test to compare the click-through rate (CTR) of each
variant against every other variant. A winner is declared only if one variant statistically

outperforms all others.

The Z-test is a statistical method used to determine if the difference in performance
(conversion rate) between two variants is significant or if it happened by chance. In the
context of A/B testing, it helps decide whether one variant truly performs better than another

with high confidence.
Formula
Where:

Â« pi = Conversion rate of Variant A = clicks_A / users_A
Â« p2 = Conversion rate of Variant B = clicks_B / users_B
Â¢ Ni, n2 = Number of users in Variant A and B
Â¢ X1, X2 = Number of clicks in Variant A and B

- p (p-hat) = Pooled conversion rate (x1+x2)/(n1+n2)

These comparisons continue until a statistically significant winner is identified.

End Date for A/B Testing
You should define a specific end date for your A/B test:

- Use the calendar picker to select the End Date for A/B Testing.
- The test will automatically stop on this date if no winner has been declared earlier.

- If an end date is not manually set, the system will run the test for up to 30 days by default.

This allows you to control the duration of your test and ensure timely evaluation of results.

Reports

Viewing and Understanding A/B Test Results

2. Locate your campaign in the listing view.

Rule Set Information

- Status: Current state of the test (e.g., Running, Paused).

- Date: The date when the test started.

- Duration: How long the test has been running.

- Max Duration: Maximum time the test is allowed to run (auto-closes after 30 days).
- Conversion Metric: The metric being measured (currently Click).

- Winner Status: Shows if a winner has been selected automatically or manually.

Variant Performance Table
The Variant Performance Table provides a detailed breakdown of each variant's test results:

- Variation: The name of the variant being tested (e.g., Control Group, Variant A, Variant B).

- Percentage: The traffic allocation percentage assigned to the variant.

- Status: The current evaluation state of the variant (e.g., Still Collecting, Inconclusive,
Statistically Significant).

- Visitors: Total number of unique visitors who qualified for and entered this variant.

- Display: Number of times the variant content was shown to visitors.

Â« Click: Total number of clicks generated by this variant.

- Unique Clicks: Number of distinct users who clicked on the variant content.

- Click Rate (CTR): Percentage of visitors who clicked on the variant.

- Min Confidence: The statistical confidence level achieved for this variant compared to
others (aiming for [95% for winner selection).

This table helps you track engagement, traffic distribution, and statistical confidence for
each variant during the test.

## Page 218

Each variant includes a "Mark as Winner" option for manual selection if desired.

Winner Selection Logic

- The system uses a Z-Test to compare click-through rates between variants.

- A variant must outperform all others with 295% confidence to be automatically declared
the winner.

- The Control Group is excluded from winner evaluation and used for benchmarking only.

- If no variant meets the threshold, the test remains inconclusive.

Data Requirements
- Each variant must have at least 100 visitors and 25 conversions before analysis.

- Until this threshold is met, variants remain in â€œStill Collectingâ€ status.

When a Winner Is Declared
- If one variant statistically beats all others:
o It is automatically selected as the winner.

o All traffic will be redirected to the winning variant.

Manual Selection

- If no automatic winner is found, you can manually select a winner by clicking "Mark as
Winner".

- Once selected, the test is locked, and no further evaluation occurs.

Test Duration and Expiry
- Tests run for a maximum of 30 days.

- If no winner is determined within this period, the test is automatically closed as

inconclusive.

Variant Statuses

## Page 219

You may see the following statuses for each variant:

- Still Collecting > Not enough data gathered.

- Statistically Significant > Variant has beaten all others with =95% confidence.
- Not Significant > Variant did not show strong results.

- Inconclusive > No clear winner identified.

- Manual Winner > Winner selected manually by the user.

The Muted Push Notification feature allows you to send push notifications without sound.
Previously, sound settings were limited to either the default sound or a custom value. With

this update, a dropdown menu has been introduced, offering three sound options:
1. Default â€” Uses the systemâ€™s default push sound.
2. Custom â€” Allows you to define a specific sound file by entering a value.

3. Muted â€” Sends the notification without any sound.

This enhancement improves flexibility and makes it easier to configure notification sounds.

How to Access

push content:

Content > Marketing > Push > Platform Settings

How to Use

and click the New button. In the General section, you can enter a name for your notification,
add an optional description, and choose a folder if needed. Once these details are set, click

Next to move forward.

In the Select Platform step, choose your preferred platform iOS, Android, or Web. As soon
as you select a platform, the relevant platform settings will appear. Among these settings, you

will find the Sound option.

Previously, this field only allowed a default sound or a custom value. Now, it has been
replaced with a dropdown menu that provides three clear options. If you select Default, the
system sound will be used automatically. If you choose Custom, an additional Add
Customization field will appear, where you need to enter the value of your custom sound.
Finally, if you select Muted, the notification will be delivered silently, without playing any

## Page 237

Password Reset Link Validity Period by Account

This feature introduces the ability to define a custom validity period for password reset links
on a per-account basis. Previously, password reset links had a fixed expiration time, but with
this enhancement, the duration is now dynamic and depends on the configuration set for
each account.

How It Works

When a user requests to reset their password, the system generates a password reset link.
This link is only valid for the time period defined in the accountâ€™s settings. Once the specified
time elapses, the link expires automatically, and the user will no longer be able to use it. To
proceed, the user must request a new password reset link.

Configuration

The validity period is configured in minutes and can be adjusted for each account by the
support team through the back-office system. The minimum validity that can be assigned is 5
minutes, while the maximum period allowed corresponds to seven days, which equals 10,080

minutes. If no configuration is applied, the system uses the default value of 50 minutes.

## Page 238

Activating Analytics Tool Flag Per Account

The Hotjar and Google Analytics Tracking flag allows accounts to enable or disable third-
party analytics tools. For now, this flag supports Google Analytics and Hotjar only. By
default, the flag is enabled for all accounts. If an account does not want to use these
analytics tools, the support team can disable it in the back office upon request.

How It Works

The flag is managed by the support team at the account level. When the flag is enabled,
Hotjar and Google Analytics tracking remain active and continue to collect data. If the flag is
disabled, both tools stop collecting data immediately.Re-enabling the flag restores tracking

functionality.

Configuration
The flag is named Hotjar and Google Analytics Tracking in the back office.

- Default state: Enabled.

- To disable: Navigate to the back office and turn the flag off for the relevant account.

To enable again: Simply switch the flag back on in the back office.

Flow Components

Flow Components

Flow Overview

Flow is a visual campaign builder that helps you create customer journeys step by step.You
can use Flow Components to build these journeys by dragging and dropping of various flow

nodes to design complex customer interactions.

When Can You Use Flow?

Flow helps you create personalized, cross-channel customer journeys that adapt to each

userâ€™s needs. You can use Flow at any stage of the customer journey to build stronger

relationships and drive engagement. For example:

- Welcoming New Users: Send a series of helpful messages to introduce your product and
keep new users interested.

- Bringing Users Back: Reach out to users who havenâ€™t been active in a while with
personalized messages to get them re-engaged.

- Rewarding Loyalty: Send special offers or thank-you messages to loyal customers to keep

them coming back.

Advantages of Flow

Flow offers several benefits to help you engage users more effectively:

- Delivers Personalized Experiences: Use customer data to send the right message at the
right time, across multiple channels.

- Supports Omnichannel Engagement: Communicate with users through email, SMS, push
notifications, and more.

- Improves User Retention: Keep users active and interested by staying relevant and timely.

- AI-Powered Optimization: Test, learn, and improve your flows using AI to find what works

best for your audience.

Audience

Below is an explanation of each tab and when to use them:
Segment

The Segment tab displays dynamic segments that youâ€™ve already created within the
platform. For instance, if youâ€™ve created a segment for â€œUsers who viewed a product but

The Predefined Segment tab offers ready-to-use audience groups that are automatically

## Page 256

Table

The Table tab allows you to choose from your existing data tables such as the Master
Contact Table or Master Device Table to define who should receive your campaign. These
tables hold the main contact or device information in your system. Once you select a table,
you can apply additional filters to narrow your audience. This option is useful when your

targeting criteria depend directly on detailed data fields in your contact or device structure.

Remote Segment

The Remote Segment tab lists audience segments whose data resides in external SQL
databases but can be used within the platform. These segments are created by running SQL
queries on the remote database, and the resulting data can then be used as an audience in
your campaigns. This allows you to leverage external data sources directly for targeting
without manually importing them into the platform.

Tag

The Tag tab lets you target users based on specific tags that have been added to them. For
example, if someone signs up for a summer campaign or becomes a VIP customer, they
can be given a tag like â€œSummer2025â€ or â€œVIPâ€. Later, you can select this tag to send them a
special message. This is a quick and easy way to reach specific groups based on their

actions or status.

Exclusions & Control Group

Exclusions

When the Exclusions toggle is turned on, the Add Exclusion button becomes available.
Clicking this button opens a dropdown menu where you can choose from the following
options: Exclude Segment, Exclude Remote Segment, Exclude Campaign, or Exclude
Send List. This allows you to remove specific groups from your target audience. You can add

multiple exclusions to refine your audience more precisely.

Control Group

When the Control Group toggle is turned on, you can define the percentage of your
audience that will be randomly excluded from receiving the campaign. These contacts form
the control group and will be used for later evaluation of your campaignâ€™s effectiveness. By

default, the control group size is set to 10%, but you can adjust this percentage as needed.

## Page 260

Email

The Email node is used to define a step in the journey where an email message will be sent
to the contacts who reach that point. It allows you to deliver personalized, timely, and

targeted communication as part of your campaign.

This node supports the use of email templates and provides options for content selection,
audience targeting, and delivery settings.

How to Configure Email Node

To start using the Email node, go to your Flow Canvas and drag the Email node onto the
canvas after choosing your audience. Once placed, double-click the node to open its

configuration panel. The setup process consists of two main steps: Content and Settings.

Content

In the Content tab, you can rename the node to give it a clear and descriptive name that
reflects its purpose in the flow, such as Welcome Email or Cart Reminder. After naming,
select an email template from the available content list. Once the content is chosen, click
Next to proceed to the settings screen.

Settings

In the Settings tab, you can define how the email will be delivered and tracked. Here, you
will see several optional settings. The Remove Duplicate Emails option ensures that the
same email address does not receive the message more than once. The Ignore Frequency
Capping option allows the system to send the email even if the recipient has already reached
their daily, weekly, or monthly message limit, which can be useful for urgent or critical
communications. The Ignore Google Analytics option prevents GA tracking parameters
from being added to the links inside the email.

You can also configure tracking options in this tab. Enabling Open Tracking lets you monitor
if recipients open the email, while Click Tracking provides data on click interactions within
the email content.

Another important setting is the IP Pool Name. An IP pool is a group of dedicated IP
addresses used for sending your emails. By assigning your campaign to a specific IP pool
(for example, bulk-real), you can control how your emails are delivered and manage sender

reputation more effectively. If you need a new IP pool added, contact Support to set it up.

The final key option is Contact Extension, which determines which email address field will
be used when sending the message. By default, emails are sent to the contactâ€™s primary

## Page 261

(default) email address, but you can choose from the following options:

- Send to Default: Sends the message only to the contactâ€™s primary email address.

- Use Contact Extension: Sends the message to a specific extension type (e.g., Work Email
or Secondary Email) that you select from the list. Extension types must first be defined in
Settings> Campaign Configurations > Contact Extension Types. To create a new type,
you can specify a name, choose the channel (Email or SMS/MMS), and set the column
order for display.

- Send to First Available: The system checks all available email addresses for the contact
(default and extensions) and sends the message to the first valid one it finds. This ensures
delivery even if the default address is missing or invalid.

- Send to All: Sends the message to every email address stored for that contact, including
the default and all extensions. This guarantees maximum reach but may result in duplicate

communication if multiple addresses belong to the same person.

This flexibility helps you ensure your campaigns reach users effectively by targeting their
most relevant contact details. For example, business-related notifications can be routed to

the Work Email extension, while newsletters can go to the Default email.

When finished, save your configuration and connect the Email node to the next step in your

flow.

SMS/MMS

The SMS/MMS node allows you to send a text message to contacts as part of their journey
through a campaign. This channel is especially effective for delivering short, time-sensitive,
or action-driven messages such as reminders, promotional alerts, confirmations, or limited-

time offers.

By incorporating SMS into your journey, you can reach your audience quickly and directly on

their mobile devices.
How to Configure SMS/MMS Node
To start using the SMS/MMS node, go to your Flow Canvas and drag the SMS/MMS node

onto the canvas after choosing your audience. Once placed, double-click the node to open

its configuration panel. The setup process consists of two main steps: Content and Settings.

Content

In the Content tab, you can rename the node to give it a clear and descriptive name that
reflects its purpose in the flow, such as Reminder SMS or Promotion Alert. After naming,

## Page 262

select an SMS/MMS template from the available content list. Once the content is chosen,

click Next to proceed to the settings screen.
Settings

In the Settings tab, you can define how the SMS/MMS message will be delivered.

Optional Settings provide control over message delivery. The Remove Duplicate Phone
Numbers option ensures that the same phone number does not receive the message more
than once. The Ignore Frequency Capping option overrides daily, weekly, or monthly send
limits for a contact, which can be useful for urgent or critical communications. The Ignore
Google Analytics option prevents GA tracking parameters from being added to the links
inside the SMS/MMS message.

The Contact Extension setting determines which phone number field will be used when
sending the message. By default, SMS/MMS messages are sent to the contactâ€™s primary

phone number, but you can also choose:

- Send to Default: Sends the message only to the contactâ€™s primary phone number.
- Use Contact Extension: Sends the message to a specific extension type (e.g., Work
Phone or Secondary Mobile) that you select from the list. Extension types must first be

defined in Settings > Campaign Configurations > Contact Extension Types.

This flexibility ensures that messages reach the most relevant phone number for each
contact. For example, urgent delivery confirmations can be routed to the Work Phone

extension, while promotional offers may be sent to the Default Mobile number.

How to Configure Push Node

Content

Within the Content tab, you can define the message details, including the node name and the
