Next to reach the Settings tab.

Settings

The Settings tab provides additional configuration options for fine-tuning message delivery.

- Ignore frequency capping: Ensures that the message is sent even if the user has already
reached their daily, weekly, or monthly limit for receiving messages.

Only select recently used tokens of registered contacts: Restricts message delivery to
the most recently active device tokens, reducing the chance of sending messages to
inactive devices.If this option is not selected, messages will be delivered to all devices
associated with the user.

- Ignore Google Analytics: Excludes Google Analytics parameters from this message
delivery.

Expiration & Inbox Options

Further settings let you control how long the message remains valid and whether it is stored
in the push inbox.

- Expire In: Defines the time limit for message delivery. If the user is not online within the
specified time, the system retries until expiration. The maximum expiry is 28 days.

- Save to Inbox: Allows you to keep important messages accessible in the userâ€™s push
inbox.

- Remove from inbox in: Messages can be automatically removed after a set number of
days (e.g., 3 days).

- Remove from inbox on: Alternatively, you can specify an exact date and time when the
message should be removed from the inbox.

## Page 264

When finished, save your configuration and connect the push node to the next step in your

flow.

Message Expiration & Priority

eligible.

Dismiss Behavior

This section defines how the message is dismissed and if/when it can reappear.

A/B Split

This powerful tool is designed to optimize your email, push, and on-site messaging by testing
two variants of content in a single one-time campaign. Instead of continuously redirecting
traffic, A/B Split works by sending each variant to a small portion of a predefined audience,
for best results this audience should be large enough (e.g., at least 100,000 recipients). After
the initial send, the system waits for a set evaluation period to measure engagement and
conversion rates. Once the winning variant is determined, the remaining audience
automatically receives the more effective content. Whether you're fine-tuning emails,
personalizing push notifications, or enhancing on-site interactions, A/B Split enables data-

driven decisions to boost the success of your one-time campaigns.

Configuration begins by choosing the appropriate channel. Depending on the channel
selected, the configuration settings may vary slightly to accommodate specific channel

requirements.

You're preparing an email campaign to promote your new product launch, but you're not sure
which subject line will drive more opens. To find out, you use the A/B Split node in your
campaign flow. You set Variant A with the subject line â€œIntroducing Our New Collection â€”
Just Launched!â€, and Variant B with â€œYou Asked, We Delivered â€” Shop the New Arrivals!â€.

You configure the test by sending each version to 5% of your audience (5% for Variant A, 5%
for Variant B). You then set the remaining 90% to be sent to the winning variant based on
open rates. In the optimization section, you enter 120 minutes as the test duration, meaning
the system will track which subject line performs better over a two-hour period. After the test
ends, the email with the higher open rate will automatically be sent to the remaining 90% of

your audience.

This way, your campaign is optimized in real time, and most of your users receive the version

thatâ€™s proven to work better.

Selecting Content and Setting Distribution for Each Variant

each variant.

the performance and automatically send the winning variant to the rest of the audience.

Web API

A Web API (Application Programming Interface) allows different software systems to

communicate with each other over the web. It defines a set of rules and protocols for

building and interacting with software applications.

The Web API Call node allows you to to transfer data from D-Engage to your own systems or

third-party services via a defined API endpoint.

Define a Remote Target for Web API Calls

Before using the Web API Call node in your campaign flow, you must first define a Remote

Target. This tells the system where to send your API requests.

How to Define a Remote Target for Web API

Navigate to Settings

Go to Settings > Integrations > Remote Targets in the D-engage interface.

. Add a New Remote Target

Click the Add button to start the setup.

. Fill in the Required Fields

Complete the form with the following details:

Name: Enter a unique name for the remote target. This name will be used when selecting
the API target in the campaign flow.

Type: Select Web API from the connection type dropdown.

Base URL: Enter the base URL of your API, for example:

https://api.mywebsite.com/apis

Endpoint: Specify the exact endpoint you want to call, such as:

/bulkupsert

Authentication Type: Choose the appropriate authentication type.

If your API doesn't require authentication, select None (default).

For APIs that do require it, you can choose Basic.

. Save

Click Save to complete the setup. Your Remote Target is now available and can be

selected when configuring the Web API Call node in your campaign journey.

Optimize Time

This node helps you send messages at the time each user is most likely to engage. It looks at
past behavior to find the best time to deliver emails, push notifications, SMS, or web push
messages.Please note that Optimize Time is exclusively available for One-Time

Campaigns.

Optimize Time

To set up Optimize Time, start by selecting at least two time slots from the available
options: Morning, Midday, Evening, and Night. These slots represent different parts of the
day when your users are most likely to engage. You can adjust the exact hours for each time

slot in the Optimize Time and Channel settings.
Important Consideration

The time frames for this feature can be fine-tuned in the Settings > Campaign
Configurations >Time Categories by Channel. Here you can establish specific intervals that

define each time slot throughout the day.

Then, choose the channels you want to use in your campaignâ€”Email, Mobile Push, Web
Push, or SMS/MMS. For each channel, select the message content from the dropdown

menu using your pre-created content.

After choosing the content, you can configure settings to fine-tune how each message is
delivered. Once everything is set, click the Save button. The system will then automatically
create separate journey paths for each Time Slot x Channel combination, ensuring your

messages are sent at the most effective times.

Tips:

- Each piece of content will be automatically duplicated and labeled with incremental
numbers (1, 2, 3, etc.) at the end of the content name to indicate different time slots.

- You can edit the contents by double-clicking on them if modifications are necessary.

- Wait nodes within this context are not editable since Optimize Time automatically
configures the wait durations.

- Should you need to revisit your time optimization choices, you can re-enter the

configuration by double-clicking on the Optimize Time node.

## Page 279

Practical Use Case Example

Letâ€™s say you schedule a one-time campaign to start at 14:00, and youâ€™ve selected Midday
and Morning as your preferred time slots. At the campaignâ€™s start time (14:00), the system
will first send the message to users who are most active around midday. Then, instead of
sending to everyone at once, it will automatically wait until the next morning to deliver the
same message to users who are more likely to engage during morning hours. This way, each
user receives the message at a time when theyâ€™re most likely to notice and interact with it,

helping boost your overall engagement.

Optimize Channel

Optimize Channel helps you send messages through the best communication channel for
each user. It looks at past engagement dataâ€”like whether a user usually clicks on emails,

SMS, or push notificationsâ€”and picks the channel they are most likely to respond to.

If there's no history available for a user, the system will use a default channel you choose to
make sure everyone gets the message.

This feature works only with One-Time Campaigns and helps increase the chances of your

messages being seen and acted on.

Optimize by Channel

To set up Optimize Channel, start by selecting the channels you want the system to optimize
for. You can choose one or more from the available optionsâ€”Email, SMS/MMS, Mobile
Push, and Web Push. These are the channels through which your campaign message may

be sent, depending on each user's engagement history.

Next, assign content to each selected channel. You'll choose from your existing content
using the dropdown menus provided. This ensures that every channel has the right message

ready to go, tailored to suit the format of that channel.

Once your channels and content are set, you can configure settings to fine-tune your
strategy if needed. When everything is ready, click the Save button to confirm your setup.

After saving, the system will automatically create paths for each selected channel. These
paths determine which channel each user will receive the message throughâ€”based on their
past interactions or your chosen default option.

## Page 280

Imagine you're launching a promotional campaign for a new product and want to make sure

each user receives the message through the channel they prefer.

For example, you select Email, Mobile Push, and Web Push as your channels. From your past
data, you notice that some users often click on emails, others engage more with push
notifications. You assign tailored content for each:

- For Email, you select a beautifully designed product announcement.

- For Mobile Push, a short and catchy notification.

- For Web Push, a concise version of the same message.

When you launch the campaign, the system checks each user's past behavior:

- User A has consistently clicked on emails in past campaigns, so they receive the email
version.

- User B has interacted mostly with Mobile Push notifications, so they get the mobile push.

- User C is new and has no history, so the system sends the message via the default

channel you set, Email.

This way, each user gets the message through the method they are most likely to engage

with, increasing your campaign's effectiveness without manual segmentation.

The Engagement Split node helps you divide your audience based on how they interacted

with a message you sent. It must be connected directly after a Send node (such as Email,

SMS, Push, In-App, or On-Site), because it uses the engagement data from that message to

determine how to split the audience.

When you click on the Engagement Split node, you'll see options to choose how to split the

audience. These options depend on the type of send connected before it. For example:

- Delivery: Splits the audience based on whether the message was delivered.

- Open: Splits the audience based on whether the message was opened.

Â« Click: Splits the audience based on whether a link in the message was clicked.

## Page 282

To use the Engagement Split node, begin by adding a Send action to your journey. This can
be any message type such as Email, SMS, Push, In-App, or On-Site. The Engagement Split
must be connected directly after this Send node, as it relies on the engagement data

generated from the message to function correctly.

Once you have connected the Engagement Split node, click on it to open the configuration
modal. Within this interface, you will be able to select the type of interaction you want to
use to divide your audience. The options available will depend on the type of message sent.
For example, if it follows an email, you might see options like Delivery, Open, or Click. These

options allow you to define what type of engagement should determine the split.

After choosing the desired engagement type, you will see two output wires that represent
different audience paths. The green wire corresponds to contacts who have engaged
with the message in the selected way (e.g., opened or clicked), while the gray wire
represents those who have not. You can then build distinct follow-up actions for each

segment to personalize your communication based on user behavior.

## Page 283

Random Split

The Random Split node allows you to divide your audience randomly into up to three distinct
paths. This feature is useful for creating varied campaign experiences such as A/B or A/B/C
testing, experimentation, or distributing traffic across multiple strategies.

Initiating Random Split

To begin, connect the Random Split node to any available audience segment. This
connection is typically made following an action node, allowing you to distribute the

campaign audience at the onset of their journey.

Configuring Path Percentages

By default, the Random Split node divides your audience into two paths. You can adjust how
much of your audience goes into each path by entering the desired percentages (e.g., 50%
and 50%, or 70% and 30%).

If you want to divide your audience into three paths, click the Add button. This will create a
third path where you can enter a new percentage. Make sure the total of all percentages
adds up to 100%.

Once you've set the percentages, click Save.
Mapping Out the Journey

After setting your random split paths, connect each path to the next step in the journey. This

could be an Action node (like Email or SMS) or a decision node (like a wait, or end).

This way, each group of users will follow a different path based on the split, allowing you to

create unique experiences for each audience segment.
Decision Split

The Decision Split node allows you to segment your audience based on predefined rules,
such as saved segments or custom SQL queries. It helps you guide each contact down the

most relevant path.

Initiating a Decision Split

To add a Decision Split to your campaign, connect it immediately after an Action node in the

flow.

Defining Your Decision Criteria

## Page 284

Set up your decision logic by adding filters to define which contacts should continue through
this path. Once your conditions are in place, click OK to save.
For example, you can create a segment that includes users who have made a purchase

within the last thirty days.

Using Exclusion Filters

To fine-tune your audience even further, you can apply exclusion filters to remove specific

users from the segment based on additional conditions.
Establishing Pathways After the Decision Split

Once you've set your Decision Split criteria, you need to connect each outcome to the next

step in the flow:
- @ Green Wire: This path represents contacts who match the segment or criteria you
defined.

- _) Gray Wire: This path represents contacts who do not match the criteria.

Example Use Case:

In the illustration above, the Decision Split is used to check whether users completed an

order after receiving an Email Campaign:
- Users who did not complete an order are directed to receive a Push Notification as a
follow-up.

- Users who did complete an order are not sent any further messages, ending their journey

in the flow.
This setup helps ensure that only the right audience continues receiving communication
based on their behavior.
Join
The Join node is used to merge multiple paths back into a single journey flow. This is
especially helpful after using split nodes such as Engagement Split or Random Split, where

your audience is divided based on behavior or distribution logic. The Join node brings those

separate branches together, allowing the journey to continue from a common point.
How to Use â€œJoinâ€ Node in a Campaign Flow

When building a journey that includes multiple audience paths for example, one for users

who clicked a message and another for those who didnâ€™t you may want to continue with a

## Page 285

shared follow-up action, such as sending another message. To do this, place a Join node
after each of the split paths and connect all branches to it.

Once the paths converge at the Join node, you can continue building the journey from its

single output. This allows for a unified action following previously segmented logic.

Wait

The Wait node allows you to add intentional delays between steps in your campaign flow. It's
especially useful after actions like sending a message, giving your audience time to engage
before the next step occurs. By controlling the timing between nodes, you can improve the
pacing of your campaign and increase overall engagement.

To get started, drag the Wait node into your journey and place it right after the node where
you want the delay to begin. Typically, this would be after a Send node (such as Email or
Push), but it can also follow other action nodes.

When you click on the Wait node, a configuration window will appear with two options:
Duration and Wait Until.

If you choose Duration, you'll be able to set a time-based delay. First, select the time unit
from the dropdown menu minutes, hours, or days then enter the number of units you want
the system to wait for. For example, if you want a one-day delay before the next message,
select "Days" and enter "1". This creates a simple, fixed pause between nodes in your flow.
After entering your values, click the Save button.

Alternatively, if you want the journey to pause until a specific calendar date, choose the Wait
Until option. This is ideal for date-sensitive campaigns, such as events, holidays, or
promotions. Simply select the exact date and time when you want the journey to resume.

Once set, click Save to confirm.

After configuring the Wait node, you can continue building your journey by connecting it to
the next node such as another message, or an action. The system will hold each contact at
the Wait step until the defined condition is met, ensuring your messages are delivered with

optimal timing.

End

## Page 286

The End node marks the termination point of a journey path. Once a contact reaches this
node, they exit the flow entirely and no further actions will be executed for them within that

journey.
How to Use â€œEndâ€ Node in a Campaign Flow

You should use the End node at the end of each path that you do not intend to continue. For
example, if a contact does not meet a specific condition or fails to engage, you might direct
them to an End node. This ensures the flow stops cleanly and prevents further processing or

unintended actions.

In split scenarios, not every path needs to rejoin the main journey. Some branches such as
those containing disqualified or inactive users can end independently. In such cases, simply

place an End node at the end of that path to finalize it.

## Page 291

Advanced Personalization

Dev Guide

Advanced Personalization is a powerful feature in Dengage that lets you create content
that adapts to each individual user. By leveraging data from your Master Contact or Master
Device tables, you can make messages more relevant, engaging, and effective. This goes
beyond simple name personalization, your content can dynamically respond to user
attributes, behaviors, and preferences.

But it doesnâ€™t stop there. Using Query Data From Data Space, you can fetch data from any
table in your data space. This allows you to create even more advanced, personalized
experiences by including information from multiple sources and applying conditions based
on that data. The result is dynamic content that automatically changes for each recipient,

helping your campaigns feel truly personal and impactful.
How It Works
You can use JavaScript to make dynamic content in the D-engage platform.

This template system is similar to the Embedded JavaScript (EJS) template language (EJS
site).

Template System

The difference is that in D-engage, the open and close delimiters for JavaScript blocks are:

1. With {% ... %}, you can write JavaScript code directly in your template.
{% if (6Contact.name) { %}
<h2>Hello, {%= $Contact.name %}!</h2>
{% } else { %}
<h2>Hello, valued customer!</h2>
{%}%}

This code checks if the contact has a name field. If the data exists, it shows Hello, [Name]!.

If thereâ€™s no name, it shows Hello, valued customer!.

## Page 292

This approach ensures that your messages always look complete and personal, even if some
data is missing.

2.With {%= ... %}, you can insert a value so it will appear in the content.

<h2>Your order number is {%= $Current.order_id %}</h2>

If the contactâ€™s order ID is 12345, this will display: Your order number is 12345.
It inserts the actual value dynamically into your content.

This allows you to dynamically show information such as order numbers, appointment times,
or account details in your content.

3.With {%- ... %}, you can insert a value but also make sure it is HTML-escaped.

<p>City: {%- $Contact.city %}</p>

If the contactâ€™s city is saved as Milan<script>, the system will escape the unsafe code and
only show: City: Milan. This ensures your content stays safe even if the data contains HTML

or scripts.

This setup allows you to personalize your messages dynamically and safely, with appropriate

fallbacks, so that each recipient sees content that is relevant and well-formatted.

Global Variables in Templates
There are three global variables that you can use in templates:
$Contact

This object includes information about the current contact. Properties of this object are
columns from the master_contact table, such as contact_key. This object can be null in Push
sends.

$Device

This object includes information about the current device. Properties of this object are
columns from the master_device table, such as a token. This object is only available for Push
content and will be null for other channels.

## Page 293

$Current

This object contains extra columns coming from a selected audience. This can be froma
Send List Table or a SQL Segment. When sending a message using these sources,

additional columns from the table or segment can be accessed through $Current.

Example 1: Product Recommendations from a Send List

Imagine you have a send list created for product recommendations. The table has two
columns: contact_key, which identifies the contact, and recommended_product_id, which
contains the product you want to recommend. When sending content using this table,
contact_key identifies the user, and recommended_product_id becomes part of the

$Currentobject. You can access it in your content as $Current.recommended_product_id.

You can also enrich the content further by looking up additional product details, such as
title, URL, or image URL, from a product table and using them in your message. This
demonstrates both how $Current data is accessible and how it can be combined with a

lookup to enhance content.

This allows your content to dynamically personalize messages based on extra data from

the selected audience, making campaigns more relevant and engaging.

Example 2: Shopping Cart Products from a SQL Segment

Some SQL segments include extra columns, especially predefined segments related to
shopping carts. For instance, there might be columns named shopping_carts and products.
When sending content using such a segment, the $Currentobject includes a products array
containing all products in the userâ€™s cart. You can access this array directly with
$Current.products and display the items in your content either as a list, a table, or any

format that fits your message.

This allows content to dynamically include multiple items from the userâ€™s cart, providing a

personalized experience for each recipient.

Try to Show Native Permission Prompt if Browser Allows

When enabled, the SDK will first try to display the browserâ€™s native notification prompt. If
the native prompt isnâ€™t available, the custom prompt will be shown instead.Push notifications
often involve a two-step process, first the custom prompt, then the native browser prompt.
The browserâ€™s native permission is required for push notifications to be granted. Even if the
custom prompt is shown and accepted, the user isnâ€™t officially subscribed until the native

prompt is approved.

## Page 309

Show Permission Prompt on Page Load
Enable this option to automatically display the permission prompt when the page loads.

When this option is turned on, the SDK automatically manages how and when permission

prompts are shown based on the rules you define below.

If this option is turned off, you can choose to display the permission prompt manually
whenever you prefer.For example, by using the Show Native Prompt or Show Custom

Prompt methods.
- Show Permission Prompt X Seconds After Page Load:
Set a delay (in seconds) before showing the permission prompt after the page has loaded.

At Least X Sessions Required to Show Permission Prompt:

Define the minimum number of user sessions before the prompt appears.

Wait at Least X Hours/Days Before Showing Again (Ignored):

Set how long to wait before showing the prompt again if the user ignored it.(took no
action)

Wait at Least X Hours/Days Before Showing Again (Denied):

Set how long to wait before showing the prompt again if the user denied it.(clicked a â€œNo

Thanksâ€ or similar button).

Show Information Popup if Notifications Are Blocked

Enable this option to display an information popup when the user has blocked notifications
in their browser. This popup only informs the user that notifications are currently disabled, it
cannot request permission again.

Its purpose is to remind users who previously denied permission and guide them to re-

enable notifications manually from their browser settings.

You can adjust its behavior with the following settings:
- Show Information Popup X Seconds After Page Load:
Set a delay (in seconds) before showing the popup after the page loads.
- Wait at Least X Hours/Days Before Showing Again:
Define how long to wait before showing the popup again after it has been displayed.
- Show Information Popup at Most X Times:

Limit the total number of times the popup is shown to the same user.

4. Advanced Settings

The Advanced Settings section provides options to customize and control how the SDK
behaves on your website. These settings are generally for specific use cases or advanced
configurations, allowing you to track additional data, manage SDK initialization, control
navigation events, and handle device-to-contact mapping.

Use Site Variables

The Site Variables feature allows tracking important data from your website, such as the
total price or number of items in a shopping basket. You can select the data source from the
dropdown menu, such as the Google Tag Manager Data Layer or custom JavaScript code.
For each variable, you can add a descriptive name or text to clarify what it tracks.

For example, on an e-commerce site, you might track the total basket amount or the
number of items in the basket. These values can be read using a variable from Google Tag
Manager or a custom JavaScript code. While this feature is useful for tracking basket data or
similar metrics, it is less commonly used with the newer SetCart feature, which is an

advanced version of this functionality.

Custom JavaScript Code

This option allows adding custom JavaScript that runs once every time the SDK is installed.
Clicking Edit opens a code editor where the code can be entered. This can be used to run
specific codes on each SDK load or to implement custom behaviors tied to the SDK. This
feature is not generally recommended, as it can be difficult to manage and control, and is

rarely needed. It should be used only for very specific custom requirements.

Print to Browser Console

This option controls how much logging information is displayed in the browser console.

The SDK records logs related to different events and states during operation.

From the dropdown menu, you can choose how detailed the console output should be:

- All: Shows all logs.

## Page 312

- Errors & Warnings: Shows only errors and warning messages.
- Errors: Shows only error messages.

- No Log: Disables all console logging.
The default setting is Errors.
Initialize SDK on Install

The SDK starts in three main steps when it runs on a page:

1. Injection: The SDK code is inserted into your website. This loads the required scripts that
allow it to function properly.

2. Install: The SDK installs its components and prepares the environment.

3. Initialize: The SDK begins its actual operations, such as displaying on-site messages or
requesting push notification permissions.

When Initialize SDK on Install is enabled, the SDK automatically performs these steps and
starts working as soon as the page loads. This is the default and recommended option for

most users.

If this option is disabled, the SDK will not initialize automatically. This is useful if you prefer to
control when it starts working, for example, after a user action or at a specific point in your
website flow. In that case, you can manually start it using the provided initialize method.

Tip:

- Keep this enabled if you want the SDK to initialize automatically when the SDK is installed.
- Disable it only if you plan to manage when the SDK initialize manually.

Trigger Navigation on Initialize

Enable this option to automatically trigger a navigation event when the SDK initializes.

In this context, a navigation represents a userâ€™s activity on the website, such as opening a

page or clicking a link to move to another section. Many SDK features (like showing on-site

messages or requesting push permissions) depend on these navigation events to start.

When Trigger Navigation on Initialize is turned on, the SDK automatically assumes that a
navigation has occurred when it initalizes and triggers related actions internally.

If your setup already uses the public method setNavigation to manage navigation events
manually, you should keep this option disabled to avoid duplicate triggers.
If you do not use setNavigation, you should enable this option so that the SDK can handle

navigation triggers automatically.

In short:

- Enabled: The SDK automatically triggers navigation events after initialization.

## Page 313

- Disabled: You control navigation events manually using setNavigation.

Allow Connecting Multiple Contacts to Single Device

This setting determines whether a single device can be linked to multiple contacts. Normally,
when you visit a website, the SDK generates a Device ID to identify you anonymously. If you
log in with an email, a Contact Key is assigned to that Device ID. In the old system (V1),
logging out and then logging in with a different email would link the new contact to the same
Device ID. In the newer system (V2), each Contact Key gets a separate Device ID, so

logging in with a different email after logout generates a new Device ID.

Enabling this option allows a single Device ID to be connected to multiple contacts. By
default, it is disabled to ensure more accurate event and session data, but it can be

enabled if required for integrations or specific workflows.

Contact Extension

The Contact Extension feature enables you to store and manage multiple email addresses

or phone numbers for a single contact.

By default, the master contact table holds only one email address and one phone number
per contact, along with their related permissions and subscription statuses (such as email
and GSM consent).

In some cases, however, you may need to manage more than one email address or phone
number for the same userâ€”for example, when a customer has both personal and work

contact details.

alternative contact details for each user. This flexibility allows you to decide which contact
information to use in your campaigns, ensuring more precise targeting and better campaign

performance.

## Page 321

Each record in the master_contact_extension table includes several key fields that

determine how contact extensions are stored and managed.

The first four fields, contact_key, name, channel, and address, are mandatory and must
always be provided. The contact_key uniquely identifies each contact and links the
extension record to the corresponding entry in the master contact table. The name field
specifies the defined Contact Extension Type, such as Personal Email or Work Phone. The
channel field indicates the communication channel this extension belongs to, either Email or
SMS/MMS. The address field holds the actual contact details, such as the email address or

phone number, depending on the selected channel.

In addition to these required fields, the table can also include several optional ones that
provide permission and status information. The permission field indicates whether the
contact has granted consent for communication and permission_reason can be used for
adding additional information about that consent. Status and status_reason fields updated

by the system but if you want you can override it.

Step 3: Use Contact Extensions in Campaigns

Once the Contact Extension Types are defined and the related data has been imported, you

can start using these extensions in your campaign flows.

When creating a campaign in the Flow screen, select an Email or SMS/MMS node. In the
nodeâ€™s Settings tab, you will find a field named Contact Extension. This field determines
whether the campaign message will be sent to the default contact information or to the

defined extensions.
Contact Extension Options

Send to defaultlIf this option is selected, the campaign works as usual and sends the
message to the default address stored in the master contact table. The default address must
always exist in the master contact record and correspond to the contactâ€™s primary email

address or phone number depending on the selected channel.

Use contact extensionlf this option is selected, the system uses the extensions defined
earlier under Settings > Campaign Configurations > Contact Extension Types for the

selected channel.

When you select Use contact extension, two additional options become available:

- Send to first available: Sends the message to the first available address based on the

Column Order priority defined in the Contact Extension Types configuration. The system

## Page 322

starts from the highest priority (for example, order 1) and continues until it finds an

available address.

- Send to all: Sends the message to all available contact extensions defined for that

channel.

## Page 334

Al Split

The AI Split Node is an advanced feature specifically designed for recurring campaign flows.
This node works on a campaign basis and utilizes AI to determine the most effective

communication channel.

Key Features:
- Campaign-Based Functionality: The AI Split Node is tailored for recurring campaign flows,
ensuring consistent optimization over time.

- Metric Selection:

After adding the AI Split Node to your workflow, you must select the metric that will be used
to determine the winning channel. The available metrics are:
- Opens: Measures the count of recipients who open the campaign messages.

- Clicks: Measures the counts of recipients who click on links within the campaign

messages.
- Conversion Rate: Measures the percentage of recipients who complete a purchase.

- Channel Testing Period:

When you split the campaign by channels (e.g., Email, SMS), the AI Split Node sends the

campaign to each channel for a duration of up to one week.

- Winner Selection:
After up to one-week testing period, the AI analyzes the selected metric (Open, Click,
Conversion Rate) to determine the most effective channel. Subsequent campaign messages

are then sent exclusively through the winning channel, maximizing engagement and

effectiveness.

Summary

The AI Split Node ensures that your recurring campaigns are continuously optimized for

maximum engagement and effectiveness.

WhatsApp Unsubscribe

The WhatsApp Unsubscribe feature allows you to automatically unsubscribe contacts from
WhatsApp communications when they send predefined keywords. This provides a simple

and seamless way for users to stop receiving WhatsApp messages whenever they choose.

This feature is available only for WhatsApp Business API integrations. It enables you to
manage unsubscribe behavior directly within Dengage, without relying on any third-party

tools.

How to Access Unsubscribe Settings

The Unsubscribe section can be accessed through the WhatsApp Business API integration
settings, applicable to both existing and new integrations. Here's how to access the

unsubscribe settings for both cases:

For Existing WhatsApp Business API Integrations
To manage unsubscribe settings for an existing WhatsApp Business API integration:
1. Navigate to Settings > Integrations > 3rd Party > WhatsApp.

2. Open your WhatsApp Business API integration.
3. Go to Step 3: Unsubscribe.

For New WhatsApp Integration Setup

To configure unsubscribe settings when setting up a new WhatsApp Business API
integration:

1. Go to Settings > Integrations > 3rd Party > WhatsApp.

2. Select New WhatsApp (New WSP).

3. Choose WhatsApp Business API as the integration type.

4. Proceed to Step 3: Unsubscribe.

Unsubscribe Configuration

The Unsubscribe section lets you add keywords that users can reply with if they no longer
want to receive WhatsApp messages. When a user sends one of these keywords in response
to your WhatsApp message, Dengage automatically stops sending WhatsApp messages to

that contact.

Setting Up Unsubscribe Keywords

This configuration is optional. If you do not define any unsubscribe keywords, users will not
be automatically unsubscribed when they reply to your messages.

You can add up to 10 keywords that users may send as a response to your WhatsApp

messages.

How the Unsubscribe Flow Works
Once a contact sends a defined unsubscribe keyword, the following flow takes place:

1. A WhatsApp message is sent through the WhatsApp Business API using Dengage.
2. The contact replies with one of the predefined unsubscribe keywords.

3. Dengage automatically detects the keyword.

4. The contact is unsubscribed from all future WhatsApp communications.

5. No further WhatsApp messages are sent to the contact unless they re-subscribe.

This flow is fully automated, ensuring that the opt-out process is seamless and efficient.

Viewing WhatsApp Permission History for a Contact

You can view a contactâ€™s WhatsApp permission history directly from their contact profile.

To access this information:

1. Go to Audiences > Profiles > Contacts.
2. Select the contact you want to review.

3. Open the Permission History tab.

In this tab, you can see the contactâ€™s WhatsApp permission status and any changes made

over time.

## Page 362

Smartlag with ZekiAI

Smart Tags is an Al-powered feature that helps you create meaningful tags automatically by
using your existing business and product data. Instead of defining all tags manually, the
system analyzes your data and suggests ready-to-use tags that can later be assigned to

users based on their behaviors.

Smart Tags can be created in multiple ways: you can use Al-suggested tags as they are, edit

them to fit your needs, or create completely new tags from scratch.

What is a Smart Tag?

A Smart Tag is a tag generated with AI support. The system looks at your products,

categories, then suggests tags that represent customer interests or purchasing tendencies.

These tags help you better understand your audience and build more accurate segments for

campaigns.

What You Can Do with Smart Tags
With Smart Tags, you can:

- See AlI-generated tag recommendations
- Edit recommended tags before using them
- Activate recommended tags

- Create completely new smart tags on your own

How to Access Smart Tags

To start using Smart Tags, go to Audience > Tags from the main menu. On the Tags page,

you will see multiple tabs. Open the Smart Tags tab to view and manage Al-supported tags.

This page is designed to clearly separate the tags you are already using from the tags that
are suggested by AI. This helps you review recommendations safely before deciding to use

them.

The first area shows the Smart Tags that are currently active in your account. These are the
tags you have already chosen to use. The second area shows Smart Tags that are

recommended by AI but are not active yet.

Actively Used Smart Tags

The Actively Used Smart Tags section displays all Smart Tags that are actively used in your

account. These tags can already be used in segmentation and campaigns.

For each Smart Tag, you can see its name, a short description explaining what the tag
represents, and the tag values that define its structure. This makes it easy to understand

Next to each tag, there is a three-dots menu. From this menu, you can edit the tag if you
want to update its name, description, or values. You can also delete the tag if it is no longer

needed.

Recommended Smart Tags

The Recommended Smart Tags section shows tags that are suggested by AI based on your

accountâ€™s data and overall business structure. These tags are not active by default.

Each recommended tag comes with a suggested name, a description, and example values.
Before using a recommended tag, you can review it carefully to see whether it fits your

business needs.

If needed, you can edit the recommended tag to better match your use case. Once you are
ready, you can click Edit and Use to activate the tag. After activation, the tag will move to the
Actively Used Smart Tags section and become available across the platform.

Creating a New Smart Tag

You can also create a Smart Tag manually if you want full control from the beginning.

To start, click the New button and choose Smart Tag as the tag type. This opens the Smart
Tag creation screen, where you define how the tag should look and behave.

Defining Smart Tag Details

When creating a Smart Tag, you are asked to provide a few basic details. These fields ensure

that the tag is clear, usable, and consistent across your account.

The Tag Name must be unique within your account. It should clearly describe what the tag
represents so that other users can easily understand its purpose.After a tag is published, the
Tag Name cannot be changed.

The Description explains the meaning of the tag in more detail. It should briefly describe

how or why the tag is used.

Smart Tags use a categorical structure, but the tag values are not predefined. Instead, Zeki
AI analyzes the accountâ€™s data and generates a list of recommended tag values dynamically.
These recommendations vary by account and are based on calculated insights. Users can
then review and use the suggested tag values as needed.

You must define at least two tag values. These values represent the possible states or

categories of the tag, such as different preferences or characteristics.

## Page 365

For each value, you enter a label that users can easily recognize and a value that is stored by
the system. You can add more values if needed by clicking Add Tag. The label supports up to

200 characters, and an optional description can be added with up to 500 characters.

After completing all required fields, click Save. Once saved, the Smart Tag becomes active
and appears in the Actively Used Smart Tags section.
Using Smart Tags in Segmentation

After creating Smart Tags, they can be used to build audiences in segmentation.

To create a segment, go to Audience > Segments and click New. Choose Interactive as the

segment type, then enter a segment name and description.
Once the segment is created, click Add Inclusion Filter. Select the condition:
Users that have [any / all] of the [..] tags

In this step, you can choose whether users should match any of the selected tags or all of

them. The [tags...] field is a multi-select dropdown that lists all available Smart Tags.
After selecting the tags, define the value condition:
[Tag] is one of [tag values...]

The [Tag] dropdown shows only the tags you selected in the previous step. The [tag
values...] dropdown displays the predefined values of the selected tag and supports multi-

selection.

Save the segment to include users who match the selected Smart Tag conditions.

Using Smart Tags in Practice

Smart Tags help you move from rule-based targeting to behavior-driven understanding of
your audience. Instead of manually defining complex conditions, Smart Tags continuously

group users based on how they interact with your products and content.

Understanding Customer Intent and Preferences

Smart Tags make it easier to understand why users interact with certain products. For
example, users who frequently browse high-priced items, premium materials, and limited
collections can be automatically grouped under a tag such as price_positioning: Premium,
while users who focus on discounted items and sale categories can be grouped under
price_positioning: Budget. This allows you to identify price sensitivity and shopping intent

across your audience without analyzing each interaction individually.

## Page 366

This insight can be used to tailor product recommendations, adjust campaign messaging,

and optimize merchandising strategies.

Personalizing Campaign Content at Scale

Smart Tags enable more relevant messaging by reflecting user preferences directly in
segmentation. Users tagged with financial_interest: Saving can receive campaigns focused
on budgeting tools and savings accounts, while users tagged with financial_interest:

Investing can be targeted with market insights and investment opportunities.

This approach improves engagement by aligning content with individual goals rather than

broad assumptions.

Building Dynamic Segments Without Manual Rules

Instead of creating multiple filters for destinations searched, accommodation types, and stay
duration, Smart Tags consolidate these signals into a single, reusable attribute. A segment
built using travel_type: City Break automatically includes users whose behavior indicates
short urban trips, while a segment built using travel_type: Leisure & Relaxation includes
users browsing resorts, villas, and longer stays. These segments remain accurate even as

destinations and travel dates change.

This reduces the need for constant segment maintenance while keeping audiences up to
date.

Create Completely New Smart Tags on Your Own

You can also create Smart Tags manually when AI recommendations do not cover a specific
business need. For example, you can create a tag such as shopping_motivation with values
Planned Purchase and Impulse Purchase to distinguish between users who research

products in detail and users who convert quickly.

Manually created Smart Tags work the same way as AlI-generated ones and can be used
directly in segmentation and campaigns.

The product_variant table is optional and should be used only when you need to define
variations of a single product. Variants represent different versions of the same product. For

example, different colors, sizes, or configurations.

Each variant is linked to a product through the product_id, which is the common reference

key between the two tables.

This table becomes necessary only in advanced use cases, where variant-level details must
be managed or tracked individually.

confidently set tracking windows for time-sensitive campaigns.

## Page 406

Segment Permissions â€” Select Segments Without Data View Access

This feature improves access control in segments by allowing users to select and use

existing segments without giving access to full data-level details.

Users who work on segmentation often need to include existing segments while creating
new ones, but they do not need to see raw data or detailed data information. With this
update, users can now select existing segments in the segment screen without requiring
the View Data permission. This means they can focus on segmentation tasks without being
exposed to data they do not need or should not access.

As a result, roles can be defined more flexibly while still maintaining strong data privacy and

security.
How to Access and Configure

Permissions are managed from the Roles & Permissions settings.

Navigate to Settings > Identity & Access Management > Roles & Permissions. From the
roles listing page, you can open an existing role or create a new one. In the role details
screen, scroll down to the Data Space section.

The Data Space section includes multiple permissions. For this feature, two specific

permissions are relevant.

View Segment/Table allows users to see and select existing segments and tables. View
Data controls access to detailed data information and raw data content. These permissions

work independently, so you can allow segment selection without granting data-level visibility.

The Select Segments Without Data View Access feature enables safer and more precise
role definitions. It improves usability for segmentation-focused users, protects sensitive data,

and supports scalable segmentation workflows without unnecessary data exposure.

Transactional Email Preview & Test Smart JSON Generation

Transactional Email Preview & Test - Smart JSON Generation automatically identifies
dynamic variables used in transactional email templates and generates a structured JSON

payload for testing and preview purposes.

With this feature, you no longer need to manually prepare test data from scratch. All required
variables are shown automatically, so you can easily see what needs to be filled in. This
makes testing faster, reduces mistakes, and helps you preview even complex transactional

emails with confidence.

How It Works

When you click Preview & Test, the system checks your transactional email template and

detects all dynamic variables used in the content, such as names, order details, or IDs.

clear which values you can change for testing.

You can freely edit this JSON:

- Add new fields if you want to test extra data

- Remove fields you do not need

Any changes you make stay available during your session, so you can easily update values

and preview again.

Segment Versioning for Interactive and SQL Segments - User Guide

Segment Versioning allows you to view and inspect historical versions of Interactive and SQL
segments directly from the segment detail screen.

This helps you understand which segment logic was active at a specific point in time,
making it easier to analyze past campaigns and flows that were triggered based on that

segment.

By default, only the current version is editable. Previous versions are preserved and
displayed in read-only mode for reference.

How Segment Versioning Works

On the segment detail page, a version selector is displayed near the header. By default, the
Current Version is shown. When you select a historical version, the segment definition
updates to reflect the selected version and opens in read-only mode. For each version, the

creation date and time is displayed to help you identify when that version was active.

How to Access
1. Navigate to Audience from the main menu
2. Click Segments

3. From the segment list, select an Interactive or SQL segment

Viewing Segment Versions

Multi-Segment Selection in Campaign Target Audience

Multi-Segment Selection in Campaign Target Audience allows you to select and combine
multiple existing segments directly while creating a campaign, without creating a new

segment.

This helps you build flexible target audiences faster, avoid unnecessary segment duplication,
and keep your segment list clean and easy to manage. Segment combinations are applied

only within the campaign and do not create permanent segment entities.

How to Access

You can access Multi-Segment Selection from the Target Audience node while creating or

editing a Flow Campaign.
Campaigns > Flows > Create New Campaign Flow > Target Audience node

Open the campaign flow and double-click the Target Audience node to open the Segment

Selection modal.

How to Use

1. While creating or editing a Flow Campaign, double-click the Audience node in the flow
canvas.

2. The Segment Selection modal opens.

3. Select multiple existing segments from the segment list.

4. Choose how the selected segments should be combined:
o AND - users must belong to all selected segments

o OR - users must belong to at least one selected segment

5. Review the combined audience under Selected Segments.

## Page 430

In-App: Clickable Image Support

Clickable Image Support allows you to assign a click action directly to images in In-App

templates. With this feature, images are no longer limited to being visual elements.

This capability gives you the flexibility to use both clickable images and buttons within the
same In-App message, each with its own destination. As a result, you can design more
engaging layouts, guide users through multiple actions, and create richer interaction
experiences without changing your existing template structure.

How to Access

To use Clickable Image Support, navigate to the In-App creation from the content area.

Content > Marketing > In-App
Create New and select Visual Editor

Choose any template that includes an image or image + text templates.

Once the template is opened in the editor, scroll to the Action section. The Clickable Image

toggle is located within this section.

How to Use
Enable Clickable Image

In the Action section, turn the Clickable Image toggle on. When the toggle is enabled, the
image in the template becomes clickable and can trigger its own action independently from
buttons.

@) Clickable Image

iOS URL Android URL

<> >

Open on App Browser

Retrieve Link on Same Screen

If the toggle remains off, the image will stay non-clickable, and only buttons will trigger user

actions.

Configure Image Click Actions

## Page 431

After enabling the Clickable Image toggle, additional configuration fields become visible. You
can enter separate destination URLs for iOS and Android platforms. You can also choose
whether the link opens in the app browser and whether the link should be retrieved on the

same screen.

These settings apply only to the image and do not affect any button configurations in the

template.
Configure Buttons Independently

Buttons in the same template can be configured as usual and remain completely independent
from the image. You can assign different destinations to buttons, or you can choose to send
users to the same destination as the image.

Both images and buttons support Web URLs, Deep Links, and Custom Actions.

Use Cases

Clickable Image Support enables a wide range of design and interaction scenarios. For
example, you can direct users to a product detail page by clicking the image, while using a
button to add the product to the cart. This helps shorten the path to purchase while still
offering clear call-to-action buttons.

You can also use the image to open content such as an article or campaign landing page,
while buttons allow users to save, share, or take secondary actions. In cases where you
want to increase the clickable area, both the image and buttons can lead to the same

destination, making the experience more accessible.

Clickable Image Support allows images and buttons to work together in the same In-App
message. This feature gives you greater control over user journeys,and enables more flexible
design choices.

## Page 432

Role-Based Access for Settings

Role-Based Access is a security feature that allows you to control who can see and edit
different areas of the platform. Instead of giving broad access to all users, you can now

define permissions in detail and assign them through roles.

This helps you protect sensitive settings, avoid accidental changes, and give each user
access only to what they need. Users see a cleaner interface, and administrators gain better

control over access across the platform.

How to Access

This feature works in two steps. First, roles and their permissions must be configured.
Navigate to Settings > Identity & Access Management > Roles and Permissions to create

a new role or edit an existing one by selecting the appropriate permissions.

After roles are configured, they can be assigned to users. Go to Settings > Identity &
Access Management > Users and click on the userâ€™s name to open the user details modal.
From there, select a role from the User Role dropdown. The dropdown lists the roles defined

in the Roles and Permissions section.

How to Use

When creating or editing a role, go to the General permission section. The following

permissions are newly added and provide more detailed access control:

If a user does not have permission, the related section will not be visible to them.

Some features may require additional permissions to function properly. If access is
restricted, you can check the related page to see which specific permission is required and
update the role accordingly.

Use Case

You may want to give a marketing manager access to view campaign configurations, but
prevent them from changing account settings or integrations.

In this case, you can enable Campaign Configurations View so they can review settings like
Blackout periods or Channel Optimization rules, while keeping Campaign Configurations
Edit, Integrations Edit, and Change Account Settings disabled. This ensures they can

monitor and plan campaigns confidently without risking accidental configuration changes.

The new General permissions provide stronger security and clearer responsibility control. By
configuring roles carefully, you can protect sensitive settings while giving each team member
the exact access they need.

## Page 460

Last 5 password cannot be use
Current System Behavior

The system currently prevents the user from reusing their most recently used password.
When the user sets a new password that is different from the current one, the change is

successful, and the new password is compared against the previous one for validation.

Updated Requirements

According to the new requirement, the system must prevent the reuse of the last three
passwords. If a user attempts to set a password that matches any of their previous three

passwords, the system will reject it.

Password Change Validation Mechanism

When the user sets a new password:

- The new password is hashed.

- It is compared against the stored password history.

- If the new password matches any of the last 3 passwords, the change is rejected.

- If there is no match, the password change is allowed.

Updating Password History

After a successful password change:

- The new password is added to the password history list.
- If the list contains more than 3 passwords, the oldest one is removed, and the list is

updated accordingly.

## Page 461

Idle Timeout Management with Backoffice Flag
Current Situation:
User session management is handled through access and refresh tokens:

- Access Token: Has a default expiration time of 15 minutes.

- Refresh Token: Automatically activates when the access token expires to obtain a new

access token, Keeping the session active without requiring the user to log in again.

In the current setup, even if the user is inactive on the screen, the session remains active due

to the refresh token being triggered in the background.

Objective:

Some clients request that users be automatically logged out of the system if they remain
inactive (idle) for a certain period. Instead of disabling the refresh token mechanism
altogether, an idle-time-based session termination feature will be developed. This feature

will be controlled via a flag configurable per client in the backoffice panel.

Scope:
- Anew flag named â€œIdle Time Logout Enabledâ€ will be added to the client settings section
in the backoffice panel.
- When this flag is enabled:
o If the user does not perform any actions or API calls within a specific time period (e.g.,
15 minutes), their session will be terminated, and they will be redirected to the login
screen.
- When the flag is disabled:
o The current behavior will remain, allowing the session to be automatically refreshed in
the background via the refresh token.

- The idle timeout period will initially be fixed at 15 minutes.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The â€œIdle Time Logout Enabledâ€ flag should be visible and editable on the client detail
screen in the backoffice panel.

- If the flag is enabled and the user remains inactive for the defined idle time, the session

should be terminated and the user should be redirected to the login screen.

## Page 462

- If the flag is disabled, the refresh token mechanism should continue to renew the access

token in the background without logging out the user.

- The default value for the flag will be disabled .

USER GUIDE
Making Public ID (Content id) Visible in the Transactional Content Interface

To improve the management of transactional content, especially for accounts with large
amounts of content, a new enhancement has been introduced. This allows users to view and

search Public ID information directly in the Content interface.

Previously, users could not easily identify which Content ID corresponds to the Public ID in
the Content interface. This led to difficulties when managing changes to content. To address

this, the following improvements were made:

Public ID Column Added: A new column for Public IDs has been added to the Content

interface.

Shortened Public ID Display: The Public ID is now displayed in a shortened format, showing

the first two characters and the last two characters (e.g., 32...91) for easier viewing.

Hover to View Full Public ID: When you hover the cursor over the shortened Public ID, the
entire Public ID is shown without needing to click. The full Public ID will appear as something
like 22684ba1-08a8-4a57-abf1-5039ff3553591.

## Page 470

Searchable by Public ID: You can now use the search box to search by Public ID to quickly

locate specific content based on its Public ID.

Detailed View in Content: When accessing the details of any content through the interface,
the entire Public ID will be visible. Additionally, an info button will be available next to the

Public ID, providing an explanation of what the Public ID represents and how it can be used.

How to Use the Feature:
1. Viewing Public ID in the Content Interface:
o In the Content interface, the Public ID will now appear in a new column.
o The Public ID will be shortened to display only the first two and last two characters (e.g.,
32...91).
o Hover to Reveal Full Public ID: Simply place your cursor over the shortened Public ID

without clicking, and the entire Public ID will appear.

## Page 471

Silent Push Test Sends

There are pushes sent to determine whether the user has deleted the application. Normally,
in order to understand whether the user has deleted the application, we send this feature
once a day and for a certain time, if the customer wishes to turn it on. However, some of the
customers stated that they could not test this and therefore could not understand whether

the pushes were sent or not.

For this purpose, an improvement will be made so that the customer can send silent push via
the app he wants.

"Silent push" are push notifications sent in mobile applications to perform data update or
synchronization operations in the background without showing any notification (sound,
vibration or visual alert) to the user. The user cannot see these notifications, but the party

that sends the push notification can perform test requests and updates.
Here, users can send their messages via iOS, Android and Huawei apps. (not on the web)

settings - app â€” select any app (other than web) - in the top bar on the right

User Guide

The Silent Push Send Test feature allows users to send silent push notifications to test
whether the application is still installed on users' devices. Normally, silent push notifications
are sent once a day at night when Uninstall Tracking is enabled. However, some customers

were unable to verify whether the silent pushes were being sent.
With this enhancement, users can now manually send a Silent Push Test for verification.

What is a Silent Push?

Silent push notifications are background push messages that update or synchronize data in
mobile applications without triggering any visible notifications (no sound, vibration, or visual
alert). The user does not see these notifications, but the sender can track responses to

confirm if the app is still installed.

How to Access and Use the Silent Push Send Test

1: Navigate to Application Settings

- Go to Settings > Integrations > Applications.

How Silent Push Works

- When Uninstall Tracking is enabled under Push Notifications, a silent push is
automatically sent at night.
- During the nightly calculation, devices that have uninstalled the app are detected, and their

statuses are updated accordingly.

- The Silent Push Send Test allows users to manually trigger this process for testing
purposes.

## Page 475

Email Builder Autosave

When clicked to the "back to concent" on the content preparation page through the email
builder, it is automatically saved and redirected to the content page. However, there are
concerns about customer requests that this may be confusing and may result in logout when

left on the screen for a long time.

At this point, if the user somehow logs out and tries to log in again and create a new email
content, he will see his old and unsaved work and will be asked if he wants to continue his
old work. If the user wants to continue his old work, he will be able to continue working with

the last changes he made.

USER GUIDE

The Email Builder Autosave feature ensures that your work is automatically saved when
working on email content. If a user closes their browser, logs out, or accidentally exits the

page, their unsaved progress will be retained and restored upon returning.

How to Access

1. Navigate to Content > Email.

2. Click on the New button.

3. Select Email Builder as the content type.

4. Choose a template or start with Blank Content.

5. Enter a Name and select a Folder for your content.

6. Click Next to proceed to the Email Builder.

Autosave and Recovery Process
- If you accidentally close your browser or lose your session, the system will retain an
unsaved draft of your last work.

- Upon creating a new email content via email builder, you will see a notice:

"Unsaved Template Available" "You have an unsaved draft template. Would you like to

continue editing?"
o No - Discard the draft and start a new email.

o Yes â€” Resume editing from the last saved state.

Automatic Save When Returning to Content Page

- If you click Back to Content while working in the Email Builder, your progress is

automatically saved, and you are redirected to the email builder.

Restoring Work After Logout

- If a user logs out and then logs in again, they will see their last unsaved email content upon
attempting to create new content.

- The system will prompt whether they want to continue from their previous session.

- If confirmed, they can continue working with their most recent changes preserved.

This feature ensures that users do not lose progress due to accidental closures or session
timeouts, enhancing workflow efficiency.

## Page 477

Moving Gray Log Errors into Automated Flow
Dalnet - THY

The customer uses automated job with file drop trigger by dropping files to FTP. They do two
types of work in flows. Automatic table creation and flow triggering. During these operations,
they receive graylog level errors that are not reflected in the interface. The scenarios and

errors received are explained below.

1- With Automated Sendable Contact Import, they leave files and create automatic tables. In
this scenario, they sometimes transmit CSV files that have Turkish characters in their names,
markups that we do not support, or very long names. In this case, the name of the CSV file
may not be suitable for us to use in table names. For this reason, the table cannot be created,
data cannot be transferred and an error is received.

2- In normal flows, they send us a zip file with a file drop trigger, write it to a table and trigger
the campaign. From time to time, errors occur in the zip files they send to us, and we receive
an error that the zip could not be read. Again, the flow cannot be triggered at all.

The following situation occurs in all of these errors. Since the flows are never triggered, no
error occurs in the history field. In fact, there is no reaction in the flows as if no data was left.
However, they can find out about this by opening a ticket with us. We can also see the details
from the graylog.

The customer wants these errors to appear in the flow in the interface so that they can follow
them.

Errors received accordingly will also be shown on the listing screens. In this way, items 1 and

2 above will be resolved.

USER GUIDE

This feature ensures that Gray Log errors appear within the automated flow interface, making
them easier to track. Errors received will also be displayed on listing screens for better
visibility.

How to Access

1. Navigate to Data Space.

2. Go to Automated Flows.

3. Click on one of the flows you want to inspect.

## Page 478

4.In the flow screen, select the Job History tab.
5. Click on one of the errors to view details.
6. Hover over an error to see a modal with error details.

7. The red modal that appears will contain detailed information about the error.

This feature helps users monitor errors efficiently and take appropriate action when needed.

## Page 480

Using Table's Allowed Columns in SQL Segment

Within the scope of this development, creating segments of some columns (columns with
segmentEnabled: false) is not allowed in the Master Device and Master Contact Tables. At
this point, an improvement has been made to show these unusable columns in error
messages and to prevent them when trying to create a segment with these columns.

This development was carried out for two different areas:

1. For SQL: These columns cannot be validated as SQL query and will return an error

message.

Error massage: â€œThe â€˜column nameâ€™ column you are trying to use is not able to set up or
allowed to be used in this context for creating segments.â€
2. For Interactive Segment: These columns do not show contact fields or device fields drop-

down list.
Columns that cannot be used in tables are listed below:
For Master Device: is_device_active, created_by, update_by, wp_subscription, install_date

For Main Contact: created_by, updated_by, contact_id

User Guide

To ensure data integrity and prevent unauthorized segmentation, certain columns in the
Master Device and Master Contact tables cannot be used when creating segments. This

update enhances error handling by:

- Preventing the use of restricted columns in SQL queries.
- Displaying error messages when attempting to create a segment with these columns.

- Hiding restricted columns from the dropdown lists in Interactive Segment creation.

Restricted Columns
The following columns cannot be used for segment creation:
Table Restricted Columns

Master Device is_device_active, created_by, updated_by,

wp_subscription, install_date

Master Contact created_by, updated_by, contact_id

## Page 481

1. SQL Segment Creation
- If arestricted column is used in an SQL segment, an error message is displayed:

o Error: â€œThe â€˜column nameâ€™ column you are trying to use is not able to be set up or
allowed to be used in this context for creating segments.â€

- The segment cannot be created until the restricted column is removed.

2. Interactive Segment Creation
- Restricted columns do not appear in the Contact Fields or Device Fields dropdown lists.

- Users can only select allowed columns for segmentation.

This update ensures that restricted columns cannot be used in segment creation, improving
data security and query accuracy. Error messages and dropdown filters provide a

seamless user experience while enforcing column restrictions.

## Page 502

InApp - Screen Name in Test
Feature Explanation:

The "Screen Name" field has been added to the InApp test screens to test the inapp ona
specific screen. This helps in identifying and tracking inapp across different screens more
effectively.

How to Use It: Screen Name Field:
Each test screen now includes a "Screen Name" field.

This field indicates the name of the screen being tested, making it easier to identify and
manage inapps on different screens. Api structure: As the inapps are coming in the

getMessages endpoint. These inapps contain every filters including screen name.there
would be no change in the api structure.Same endpoint would be used to fetch the test

screen name inapps.Example Scenario:
In an e-commerce application:

When a user views the "Product Detail" page, the screenName parameter will include
"ProductDetail" in the API call.

The user will call function set navigation("productDetail") in order to get this inapp visible to
the user.Summary:

This new feature helps in better tracking and testing of InApp screens by specifying the
screen name in the screen name filter. This makes it easier for developers and testers to

understand which screens are being tested and how users are interacting with them.
USER GUIDE

The "Screen Name" field has been added to the InApp test screens to allow testing of in-app
messages on a specific screen. This enhancement helps users track and identify in-app

messages across different screens more effectively.

How to Access
1. Navigate to the InApp Test Screens section in the platform.
2. Select the test screen where you want to test an in-app message.

3. Locate the Screen Name field in the test screen interface.

## Page 519

Tokenized Send

This new feature allows to clients who prefer not to store personally identifiable information
data like name, surname, email and phone numbers etc. outside their own systems. The

client utilize the encoded data on Email and Sms sendings.

Prerequisites
1. The client can not merge identified and tokenized data in one account.
a. Tokenized Send feature flag must be enabled on Back Office.

2. The API implementation must be defined to utilize this feature. Settings > Tokenazation
API Definition
a. 2 types of APIs are supported.
i. JSON

ii. GZip (Recommended)
sâ‚¬ Technical Documents
Tokenized Sending API Definition

Tokenized Sending Development Guide

1 b. The API supports HTTP Basic Auth or API Key authorization.
2

o If the â€œBASIC AUTHâ€ type is selected, API URL, username, and password must be

provided. The clients can utilize SSL connection to encrypt username or password.

o If â€œAPI KEYâ€ type is selected, Key and Value must be passed through the request
header.

o If the â€œGZipâ€ format (recommended) is used, the request and response should be

developed in accordance with GZip as follows:

For the request and response:
= Set the header "Content-Encoding" to "gzip".

= Set the header "Content-Type" to â€œapplication/octet-stream".

This ensures that both the request and response are properly encoded and decoded using
gzip compression.

within 90 seconds.

## Page 545

TB - Moving Gray Log Errors into Automated Flow
Sprint 24

Team Blue

Dalnet - THY

The customer uses automated job with file drop trigger by dropping files to FTP. They do two
types of work in flows. Automatic table creation and flow triggering. During these operations,
they receive graylog level errors that are not reflected in the interface. The scenarios and

errors received are explained below.

1- With Automated Sendable Contact Import, they leave files and create automatic tables. In
this scenario, they sometimes transmit CSV files that have Turkish characters in their names,
markups that we do not support, or very long names. In this case, the name of the CSV file

may not be suitable for us to use in table names. For this reason, the table cannot be created,

data cannot be transferred and an error is received.

2- In normal flows, they send us a zip file with a file drop trigger, write it to a table and trigger
the campaign. From time to time, errors occur in the zip files they send to us, and we receive

an error that the zip could not be read. Again, the flow cannot be triggered at all.

The following situation occurs in all of these errors. Since the flows are never triggered, no
error occurs in the history field. In fact, there is no reaction in the flows as if no data was left.
However, they can find out about this by opening a ticket with us. We can also see the details

from the graylog.

The customer wants these errors to appear in the flow in the interface so that they can follow

them.

Errors received accordingly will also be shown on the listing screens. In this way, items 1 and
2 above will be resolved.

## Page 550

TB - Silent Push Test Sends

Team Blue
Sprint 24

There are pushes sent to determine whether the user has deleted the application. Normally,
in order to understand whether the user has deleted the application, we send this feature
once a day and for a certain time, if the customer wishes to turn it on. However, some of the
customers stated that they could not test this and therefore could not understand whether
the pushes were sent or not.

For this purpose, an improvement will be made so that the customer can send silent push via

the app he wants.

"Silent push" are push notifications sent in mobile applications to perform data update or
synchronization operations in the background without showing any notification (sound,
vibration or visual alert) to the user. The user cannot see these notifications, but the party
that sends the push notification can perform test requests and updates.

GDPR Kapsaminda Bireylerin Haklar1

GDPR, bireylere kisisel verileri uzerinde genis kapsamli haklar tanir:

1. Bilgilendirme Hakki (Right to Informed)

Bilgilendirilme hakki, genellikle bir gizlilik bildirimi araciligiyla saglanan "adil isleme bilgisi
sunma yukumluldgdnuzu kapsar. Bu hak, kisisel verileri nasil kullandiginiz konusunda

seffaf olma gerekliligini vurgular.

2. Erisim Hakki (Right to Access)
a. Veri Koruma Yasalar! kapsaminda, veri sahipleri asagidaki haklara sahip olabilir:
i. Kisisel verilerinin islenip islenmedigine dair onay alma,
ii. Kigisel verilerine erisim saglama,
iii. Gegerli Veri Koruma Yasasi tarafindan belirlenen diger ek bilgilere ulasma.

b. Kisiler, Kendileri hakkinda hangi verilerin islendigini 6grenebilir.

3. Duizeltme Hakki (Right to Rectification)
a. Yanlis veya eksik verilerin dUzeltilmesini talep edebilirler.

Bireyler, kisisel verilerinin yanlis veya eksik olmasi durumunda duzeltilmesini talep etme
hakkina sahiptir.
Eger soz konusu kisisel verileri GgUncU taraflarla paylastiysaniz, mUmkUn oldugunda

duzeltme hakkinda onlari bilgilendirmeniz gerekebilir.

4. Silme Hakki (Right to Erasure - "Unutulma Hakk")

a. Bireyler, belirli durumlarda verilerinin silinmesini talep edebilir.

Silme hakki, ayni Zamanda â€œunutulma hakki" veya "silinme hakki" olarak da bilinir.

4. islemeyi Kisitlama Hakki (Right to Restrict Processing)
o Verilerin islenmesini belirli Kosullarda sinirlandirabilirler.

5. Veri Tasinabilirligi Hakki (Right to Data Portability)

## Page 572

o Bireyler, kendi verilerini farkli bir servis saglayiciya tagsima hakkina sahiptir.

6. itiraz Hakki (Right to Object)

o Kisiler, belirli veri isleme faaliyetlerine itiraz edebilir (6rnegin, pazarlama amacli veri
kullanimi).

Otomatik Karar Almaya Kars! Cikma Hakki

o Otomatik sistemler tarafindan alinan kKararlarin insan g6zetimi olmadan yapilmasina itiraz
