Rights of Individuals Under GDPR

GDPR grants individuals extensive rights over their personal data:

Right to Be Informed
This right covers your obligation to provide â€œfair processing information,â€ typically via a
privacy notice. It emphasizes the need for transparency about how personal data is used.

Right of Access

Under data protection laws, data subjects have the right to:

- Obtain confirmation of whether their personal data is being processed,
- Gain access to their personal data,

- Obtain other supplementary information as specified by the applicable data protection

legislation.

Individuals can learn what data is being processed about them.

## Page 575

Right to Rectification

Individuals can request correction of inaccurate or incomplete data.

If personal data is shared with third parties, those parties may need to be informed of the

corrections, where possible.

Right to Erasure (Right to Be Forgotten)

Individuals can request deletion of their data under certain circumstances.

Also Known as the â€œright to be forgottenâ€ or â€œright to deletion.â€

Right to Restrict Processing

Individuals can restrict the processing of their data under certain conditions.

Right to Data Portability

Individuals have the right to transfer their personal data to another service provider.

Right to Object

Individuals may object to certain types of data processing (e.g., for marketing purposes).

Rights Related to Automated Decision-Making
Individuals have the right to object to decisions made solely through automated processing

without human involvement.

Email Tracking Under GDPR: Open & Click Tracking

Under GDPR, tracking opens and clicks in emails may require separate consent. This is

because such tracking techniques are considered personal data processing.

Email Subscription and Data Processing Consent

Asking users, â€œWould you like to subscribe to our email list?â€ is sufficient for sending emails,

but may not be enough for tracking technologies.

GDPR requires explicit and specific consent. In other words, users must be clearly informed:

â€œWe will track whether you open our emails and which links you click.â€

## Page 576

Does Open & Click Tracking Require Separate Consent?

Yes, in most cases, separate consent is required.

This is because email opens and link clicks are considered behavioral data and thus personal
data under GDPR.

If no consent is obtained for such tracking, it may constitute a GDPR violation.

How Should Consent Be Collected?
There should be a clear statement in the email subscription form. For example:
â€œWe will track whether you open our emails and click the links inside. Do you agree to this?â€

Users should be given the option to refuse tracking (e.g., an alternative email without

tracking).

Alternative Methods
If tracking is intended without separate consent, legitimate interest may apply in specific

Cases.

However, you must conduct a Legitimate Interest Assessment (LIA) and provide an easy
opt-out option to users.

Conclusion
- General consent for email sending is not sufficient for open & click tracking.
- Separate consent is typically required for such tracking.

- If tracking is done without consent, a legitimate interest test must be completed and users

must be able to opt out.

- Because this is a sensitive area under GDPR, the safest route is to obtain explicit consent.

Question:

Letâ€™s say we provide users with an option to accept or reject tracking. If a user chooses â€œYou
may send me emails, but I do not want to be tracked,â€ what should we do? Should we avoid
placing any tracking links and open tags in the email? Or can we include them but process
the signals anonymously?

Answer:

If a user selects the option â€œYou may send me emails, but I do not want to be tracked,â€ then

there are two GDPR-compliant approaches to consider:

## Page 577

1. Do Not Use Any Tracking Technologies (The Safest Option)

- Do not include any open tracking pixels or tracked links in the email.
- Links should be direct, non-tracked URLs (e.g., https://site.com/campaign).

- No data is collected, and full respect is given to the userâ€™s preference.

Pros:

Most secure option in terms of GDPR compliance.

Cons:

You will not receive any open or click data.

2. Include Tracking But Anonymize the Data (Risky and Debatable)

In this approach:

- You may include open tracking pixels and tracked links.
- However, signals are not tied to identifiable user data (e.g., email, IP address, device info).

- Instead, data is analyzed in aggregate form (e.g., â€œThis campaign has a 30% open rateâ€).

Important Note:

This enters a gray area under GDPR:
- If the data is fully anonymized (i.e., cannot be traced back to a person), it may fall outside
GDPRâ€™s scope.

- However, if any indirect identifiers remain (e.g., IP addresses or browser fingerprints),
there is still a risk of GDPR violation.

Pros:

Allows for general performance analysis of the campaign.

Cons:

If anonymization is not strong enough, it could result ina GDPR breach.

Final Recommendation:

To ensure full GDPR compliance, the safest option is to completely avoid tracking for users
who opt out.

If you consider anonymized tracking, make sure your system truly anonymizes the data in an
irreversible and non-identifiable way. You should assess this based on your organizationâ€™s
risk tolerance, but the lowest-risk option is to simply avoid any tracking for those users.

Requester: Beymen

Request Details:

1. Duplicate Existing Automated Flow
Beymen requests the ability to duplicate an existing automated flow.
For example, they want to create a new automated flow that is similar to an existing one,
but instead of building it from scratch, they would like to duplicate the existing flow and
continue editing from there.

. Editing Start Date and End Date After Initial Setup

Currently, during the initial setup of a new automated flow (on the "New Automated Flow"

page), Start Date and End Date are defined. However, once saved, there is no available
screen to update these dates later on.
They request the ability to edit the Start and End Date after saving the flow.

(Screenshot related to this issue has been shared as an attachment.)

RP Review and Comments:
- The ability to update Start and End Date already exists. It can be accessed via the bar
that opens when the "i" icon is clicked.

- Duplicating an existing flow is feasible and can be implemented.

To-Do Implementation Plan:

- Users will be able to duplicate an existing flow by clicking the â€œ...â€ icon at the end of the

corresponding row and selecting the option: â€œDuplicate the campaignâ€

## Page 601

(Screenshot)

Duplication Flow:

The user will first land on the â€œGeneralâ€ page where all basic flow information is pre-filled,
identical to the original flow.

The only difference will be the name field, which will include â€œCopy 1â€ next to the original
name.

(If this is a second duplicate, it will display â€œCopy 2â€, and so on.)

The user can proceed without changing anything on the General page.

The new screen will look like the edit screen of an existing flow, although the flow hasn't
been saved yet:

Screenshot

(Because the flow is not saved yet, the General configuration bar will remain visible at the
top.)

Once all necessary modifications are made, the user can proceed by clicking â€œNext.â€

The flow will then continue as usual, with â€œSaveâ€ or â€œBackâ€ options:

Screenshot

After clicking â€œSave,â€ the user is redirected to the standard flow detail page, where further
changes can be made as with any existing campaign:

Screenshot

5-RealTime Segment Sync

RP-562: Ostrovok I RU, EU Cloud IWarning for disabling real-time segments (REtERsED)

Description

Add a warning alert when a user disables Real-Time Segment Sync.

EU, RU

Account

ostrovok, b2b-ostrovok, rate_hawk, roundtrip

What is the clientâ€™s problem? (please, explain in-depth)

Users sometimes disable Real-Time Segment Sync without realizing that the affected
segment is still being actively used in multiple campaigns. Since there can be many
campaigns running simultaneously, it's easy to forget which segments are linked where. This

can lead to unintended campaign behavior or targeting issues.

Describe the cost of not doing this request:

- Campaigns may continue running with outdated or incorrect segment data.
- Risk of sending irrelevant messages to the wrong audience.
- Operational inefficiencies due to the lack of visibility on segment usage.

- Increased support inquiries due to unexpected campaign behavior.

Additional Information

Suggested behavior:

When a user attempts to disable Real-Time Segment Sync, display a *warning popup*
indicating that the segment is currently used in active campaigns, and list or link to those
campaigns if possible. This will help prevent accidental disruptions and improve user

awareness.

Conversion Calculation Rules

## Page 615

The account's conversion tracking attribution model can be based on either message

"delivery", "open or click", or "only click". This configuration is applied across all

campaigns. It is not possible to be defined per-campaign basis.

The conversion calculation is based on the conversion deadline defined in the campaign
settings and account's configured attribution mode.

Event Prioritization in Conversion Calculation:

If the account's conversion attribution is configured as "Delivery", then event prioritization for conversion calculation will
be as follows:

- The Click events from the sends always get the highest priority.
- If there is no Click event, the message with an Open event is counted.
- If neither Click nor Open events are present, the conversion calculation is made for the

message's Delivered event.

If the account's conversion attribution is configured as "Open or Click", then event prioritization for conversion calculation
will be as follows:

- The Click events from the sends always get the highest priority.

- If there is no Click event, the message with an Open event is counted for conversion.

If the account's conversion attribution is configured as "Only Click", then only Click events

will be counted for calculating conversion of the send.

## Page 621

Appsflyer Partner Integration - Phase 1
Overview
What is AppsFlyer?

AppsFlyer is a mobile marketing attribution and deep linking platform used by mobile
marketers, product teams, and developers. It helps companies:

Attribute mobile app installs to specific ad campaigns, partners, and channels.

Track in-app events (e.g., purchases, sign-ups, trial starts) with real-time reporting.

Understand user journeys and optimize advertising spend across networks like Meta,
Google Ads, TikTok, and more.

Enable deferred deep linking to send users to specific app content even after install via a
single OneLink URL.

Manage audience segmentation and re-engagement through push, email, or ad networks.
AppsFlyer acts as a critical analytics and campaign attribution layer in the mobile
ecosystem, especially for performance-driven and multi-channel marketing teams.

1. Why This Is Needed

- Customer Demand:

o Ostrovok and another key mobile-first customer have requested AppsFlyer integration to
enhance campaign targeting and visibility.

- Market Expectation:

o Competitors like MoEngage, WebEngage, CleverTap, and Braze already offer this
integration.

o Customers expect install source tracking, journey attribution, and deep-link consistency
in mobile campaigns.

Failing to offer this could lead to churn or lost opportunities with mobile-centric clients.
2. Objective

Develop and deploy a two-way integration between Dengage and AppsFlyer, covering:

Â« Inbound Postbacks: Receive install and event attribution from AppsFlyer.
- Outbound Events: Send re-engagement or conversion events back to AppsFlyer.

- Enable customers to activate this integration from the Dengage dashboard.

3. Competitor Comparison

## Page 626

WhatsApp Channel â€” Unsubscribe Messages and Block Scenarios
Reason for Development

Following the WhatsApp (WP) Channel enhancement, our users can now create WhatsApp
templates and prepare them for sending directly from the Dengage panel. However, unlike
SMS and email scenarios, unsubscribe [{{unsubscribe-link}}] functionality is not currently
available for WhatsApp messages.

It is essential that users are also able to send unsubscribe links in this message type.
Additionally, when a recipient blocks the sending number, this action should be detected on
our side, and the WhatsApp permission for the relevant contact in the target audience should

be automatically updated in the permissions section.
Planned Enhancements
1 - Unsubscribe Messaging

The structure and process here will be very similar to the unsubscribe flows used in SMS and
email. This way, an unsubscribe link will be sent in WhatsApp messages, and when clicked,
the user will be redirected to a page where they can complete the unsubscribe process, just

like in SMS and email messages.

1.1- WhatsApp Customized Unsubscribe Page

First, a new configuration area will be added to the Settings > Campaign Configurations >
Customized Unsubscribe Page section specifically for WhatsApp, in addition to the existing
configurations for SMS and email.

The configuration layout will be exactly the same as the others, and users will be able to
configure the following settings within this section:

General Font Family
General Font Color
Logo

Logo Width

Logo Align

Title

Button Text Font Size

Button BG Color

Button Text Color

After completing the configurations, they will click the Save button and see a confirmation

pop-up saying: "WhatsApp unsubscribe page saved successfully."

1.2 - Unsubscribe Link Sending

When users create WhatsApp templates via Content > Messaging > WhatsApp, they will
add a variable in the message section by clicking â€œAdd Variableâ€ in the pop-up input area,
giving it any desired name.

Unlike other setups, the customization of the variable added here will be done later on the

flow screens during the sending process.

After this plugin is added, they will complete and save the other message configurations.

For sending, they will need to customize the template on the flow screens. While customizing
variables here ( 4 Screenshot ), they will proceed by selecting {{unsSubscribe-

1ink}} through the Customization Selector.

By proceeding this way, an unsubscribe link will be included in their messages, and when
recipients click this link, they will be redirected to the previously prepared WhatsApp

Customized Unsubscribe Page.

2 - Updating Contact Permissions When the Sender Number Is Blocked

Another scenario is when users individually block the WhatsApp sender number before
receiving an unsubscribe message. In this case, if the sending continues, the user may be
blocked by Meta.

As a precaution, we need to detect that the contact has blocked the sender number and

automatically update the sending permissions accordingly.

Based on Anilâ€™s feedback, the required improvement here is to automatically disable
WhatsApp sending permissions in the permission tables for contacts that are marked as
BOUNCED in WhatsApp sends.

Other details will be discussed during the pre-grooming.

## Page 667

Gdpr kapsaminda kullanicilarin verilerini anonim olarak takip edebilir miyim?

Evet,
GDPR (Genel Veri Koruma TuziUgii) kapsaminda anonimlestirilmis verileri kullanmak ve
takip etmek genellikle mumkUndur. Ancak burada cok Onemli bir ayrim var: verilerin

gercekten anonimlestirilmis olmasi gerekir.

GDPR'a Gore Anonim Veri Nedir?

Anonim veri, kimligi belirlenebilecek bir kisiye ait hicbir bilginin, dogrudan ya da dolayl
sekilde, geri allinamaz bigimde icermedigi verilerdir. Yani bu verilerden, kimin oldugunu asla
tahmin edemezsiniz â€” geri dondurulemez olmalidir.

Anonim Veri Takibi Mumkun:

Â« Kullanici davranislarini (Ornegin: sayfa gezinme, buton tiklama) kimlik bilgisi olmadan
toplarsaniz.

- IP adresi, cerez IDâ€™si, e-posta gibi kisisel veri igermiyorsa.

- Toplanan verilerden birey tanimlanamiyorsa ya da tanimlanamaz hale getirildiyse.

Anonimlestirme Degilse (Sadece "pseudonymization"):

- Eger veriler sifrelenmis, maskelenmis, ya da kullanict IDâ€™si gibi dolayli tanimlayicilar

iceriyorsa, bu veriler hala kisisel veri sayilir ve GDPRâ€™a tabidir.

- Yani pseudonymization (takma adlandirma), anonimlestirme ile ayni sey degildir. Bu tur

In-App Content Bug - Swipeable Popups

Task Name: ZenHotels I In-App Content Bug - Swipeable Popups

JIRA Ticket: @https://dengage.atlassian.net/browse/TM-46 Can't find link

Issue Summary:

ZenHotels' in-app popups were swipeable, allowing users to scroll them when they should

remain static. This was unintended behavior and affected user experience.

Current Behavior:
- Users were able to swipe up or down on in-app popups, making them scrollable.
- This caused unexpected movement in the UI.

- The issue was present across multiple devices and platforms.

Expected Behavior:

- In-app popups should remain static and should not be swipeable.

Resolution:
- The issue has been identified and fixed.
- Popups now remain static and are no longer swipeable.

- The fix has been successfully tested and confirmed.

even when no image URL is provided.

## Page 678

Push Custom Buttons

JIRA Ticket: @https://dengage.atlassian.net/browse/TM-5 Can't find link

Issue Overview:

Rich Push notifications allow users to interact through custom action buttons. Each button is

expected to redirect users to a specific URL when clicked.

Current Problem:
- The first button works correctly, directing users to the right URL.

- The second and subsequent buttons do not work correctly, redirecting users to the wrong
URLs.

Expected Behavior:
- Every custom button should redirect users to its assigned URL.

- The system should handle multiple buttons correctly, ensuring each one functions

independently.

Fix Implemented:

- Corrected button indexing to ensure proper URL assignment.

- Updated notification logic to manage multiple buttons separately.
- Re-tested on various devices to confirm the fix.

- Verified successful redirection for all buttons.

Post-Fix Results:
- All buttons now redirect correctly to their respective URLs.

- The issue is fully resolved, and Rich Push notifications work as expected.

## Page 679

Other Option Input Field Issue in In-App Feedback

Jira Ticket: @ https://dengage.atlassian.net/browse/TM-27 Can't find link
Issue Overview:

The input field for the "Other" option in the in-app feedback form was not appearing
consistently on Android and iOS devices. This caused users to be unable to enter custom
feedback when selecting "Other."

Current Behavior:
- When users clicked the "Other" option, the input field did not always appear.
- The issue was observed on both Android and iOS platforms.

- This prevented users from providing custom feedback.

Expected Behavior:
- When users select the "Other" option, the input field should always appear.

- Users should be able to enter and submit their custom feedback without any issues.

Fix Implemented:

1. Updated UI Logic: Ensured the input field is always present in the background and
becomes visible when "Other" is selected.

2. Improved Event Handling: Fixed the trigger so that selecting "Other" always displays the
input field.

3. Tested on Multiple Devices: Verified the fix works across different Android and iOS

versions.

- Message: e.g. â€œUse this code within 15 minutes!â€ , â€œoffer valid for 15 mins onlyâ€œ

3. Conditional Copy Coupon Code Button
- If the revealed reward is a coupon code:

o Display a "Copy Code" button below the code.

o On click: code is copied to clipboard with tooltip feedback (e.g., "Code Copied!").
- If the reward is not a coupon code (e.g., a discount message or special offer):

4. CTA Button
- Below the revealed result, a button links to the relevant landing page or product.

- Required if no coupon code is involved.

2. Scratches to reveal a reward.

6. User clicks to copy or redirect.

Market Gap Analysis & Problem Statements
Explainability

Only Insider provides comprehensive reasoning for AI decisions. Most platforms offer

"magic" without transparency, reducing user trust and adoption.

All-or-Nothing Problem

Competitors either overwhelm users with complete generation (Insider) or provide minimal

AI assistance (WebEngage). No platform offers progressive enhancement.

Workflow Fragmentation Issue

Every platform forces context-switching between separate modules for segments, flows, and

content. No unified canvas experience exists.

Generic Content Problem

Al-generated content lacks brand authenticity and requires heavy editing across all
platforms.

Problems

- Blank-canvas paralysis wastes hours.

What is Fine-Tuning?

Fine-Tuning = Teaching the AI your brandâ€™s tone and style.

Instead of starting from scratch, we take an already smart AI and retrain it
on your own data â€” like your past email subject lines, SMS messages,

campaign data, industry terms, etc.

toneâ€, â€œkeep SMS under 160

charsâ€)

What is RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)?

RAG = AI + Search Engine

Instead of training the LLM on everything from scratch, you keep your
campaign data in a searchable database, and when a user enters a

prompt, the system:

1. Searches for relevant info (e.g., top-performing subject lines for this brand)
2. Feeds that info into the AI model

3. AI uses that context to generate smarter content
This way, the LLM writes as if it remembers your history â€” without retraining.

Use RAG + Light Fine-Tuning on Open-Source Model (e.g., Mistral 7B)

Combine Retrieval-Augmented Generation (for brand-specific context) +

lightweight fine-tuning (for tone, industry patterns).

Why RAG?
Because we are dealing with:

Â« Many clients
- Need for brand + performance + industry context

- Want to keep costs controlled (vs. full fine-tune every time)

A vector database stores your campaign data in a way that AI can understand and search â€”

not as exact text, but as â€œmeanings.â€
Imagine storing:

- Brand tone data

## Page 712

Session Termination After Password Change

To enhance account security and protect user data, the system now terminates all active
sessions when a user changes their password. This means that after updating the
password, the user will be logged out of all sessions and must re-login using the new
password. This update is an important step in preventing unauthorized access and

maintaining account integrity.

How to Access
Settings > My Profile > Change Password

- Navigate to Settings.

Â« Click on My Profile.

- Select Change Password.

- Enter the new desired password.

- Confirm the new password and save changes.

Once the password change is confirmed, the system will automatically log the user out of
all active sessions. The user must sign in again using the new password to continue using

the system.

This change ensures that any unauthorized access using previous sessions is immediately

cut off after a password update, helping to keep your account secure.

## Page 724

Realtime/Flow Page URL Filters/Conditions Redesign

Flowda Operator ve Deger alinarak yapillyor. Ornek CONTAINS /women/

Realtineda Operator ve Deger alinarak yapillyor ama operator bilgisi SDKâ€™ya akmiyor.

Operator ve deger ile bir Regex Uretiliyor.

Her ikisi de sadece protocol ve domain kism! haricindeki kism! inceliyor. Yani path + query +
hash butunune baktyor.
URL 5 parcadan olusur:

1. Protocol: Bizi pek ilgilendirmiyor. CUnkU miusterilerin tamami zaten https://. Ornek: ftp://
http:// https://

. Domain: Genellikle SDK tek sitede calisacak sekilde ayarlaniyor ama bazi musteriler farkl

subdomainleri igin tek SDK kullanmak istiyor. Bu nedenle URL kurali koyulurken domain
bazli yapilmasina izin vermeliyiz. Ornek: www.dengage.com dev.dengage.com,

dengage.com

. Path: Su an destekliyoruz desteklemeye devam edecediz. /category/electronics
/product/55121 /about.html /blog/how_to_make_pancakes.php

4. Query: Su an destekliyoruz desteklemeye devam edecegiz. Query iÂ¢ginde parametreler key

value pair olarak yer alir ve sirasi degisebilmektedir. Bu nedenle queryâ€™ler icin key value

bazili segenek sunmallyiz. ?utm_medium=email&pageSize=50&page=3

. Hash: Su an destekliyoruz desteklemeye devam edecegiz #Address #payment
#/product/55552323

Yeni yapida URL filtreleri 6 tipte olacak

1. Full URL: URL pargalarina bakilmaksizin browser adres cubugundaki degere g6re
filtreleme. Text/String bazli operator secimi ve free text input ile filtre degeri alinacak.
Ornek: Starts with https://somedomain.com/category?page=5

2. Domain: Sadece domain kismina gore filtreleme. Text/String bazli operator secimi ve free
text input ile filtre degeri alinacak. Ornek: starts with blog.

3. Path: Sadece path kismina gore filtreleme. Text/String bazli operator secimi ve free text
input ile filtre degeri alinacak. Ornek: Does not contain /about/

4. Query String: Sadece query string degerine gore filtreleme. Text/String bazli operator
secimi ve free text input ile filtre degeri alinacak. Ornek: Does not start with ?s0me_key=

5. Query Parameter: Query icindeki her bir key value pairâ€™e gore filtreleme. Free text input ile

key, Text/String bazli operator secimi ve free text ile value filtresi degeri alinacak. Ornek:

## Page 725

page_type equals category, brand_filter equals samsung
6. Hash: Sadece hash kismina gore filtreleme. Text/String bazli operator secimi ve free text
input ile filtre degeri alinacak. Ornek: page_type equals category, brand_filter equals

samsung

Her bir URL kurali Realtime Onsite kurallari gibi Gruplanabilir ve AND/OR operatorleri ile

baglanabilir olacak.

## Page 726

Realtime Onsite Triggers

Mevcutta olanlar:

- On Page Load

- On Scroll

- On Exit Intent

- On GTM Data Layer event

Mevcutta olmayan ama altyapisi hazir olanlar:

- On Dengage Event: SDK event requesti attiginda atilan isim ve mUmkUnse attributelara
gore tetikleme

- On Window Event: Browser window objesine atilan event

Bu isi yaparken sadece yeni eklemeleri yapmayacadgiz. Delay ile ilgili karisikligi da gidermis

olacagiz.

Toplamda 4 ana tip olacak

1. On Event:

a. Dengage Event: Event: requesti tetikleyen tum eventlerdir. Arayuzde bir dropdown ile
eventler secilir. Secilen evente gore attributelar listelenir. Key value olarak eklenir.
operator kurallart eklenebilir. Attributesuz sadece eventin varliginin yeterli olmas!
secenegdi sunulabilir

b. GTM Data Layer Event: dataLayer a event key ile basilan entitylere bakar. SDK ayaga
kalmadan Once olan eventleri al alma dzelligi eklenebilir. Event name freetext yazilir.
Attributelar da key value pair olarak eklenebilir. Operator kurallar! eklenebilir. Attributesuz
sadece eventin varliginin yeterli olmasi segenegi sunulabilir

c. Window Event: Browser window objesine atilan eventlerdir. Event name freetext yazilir
Attributelar da key value pair olarak eklenebilir. operator kurallari eklenebilir. Attributelar
event.data icinde aranir. Attributesuz sadece eventin varliginin yeterli olmasi segenedi
sunulabilir

2. On Page Load: SDK setNavigation tetiklenince calisir. Scroll ve Delay'den arindirilacak.

3. On Exit Intent: As is kalacak. Bunun kucuk de olsa bir hassasiyet ayari var ama cok zor fark
ediliyor. Kullaniciya bunu sectirebiliriz ama farkini anlamak gergekten zor. Bence
sectirmeyelim.

4. On Scroll: SDK agisindan ayni sekilde calisir. Birden fazla scroll trigger oldugunda ne
yapilacag! Tartisilsin

## Page 727

Mevcutta On Page Load altindaki Delay ayrica belirlenebilir olmali. Show/Run X Seconds after

trigger fired gibi bir label ile alinmall.

Bir kampanyanin birden fazla trigger ile calisabilmesinin OnU acilabilir. Gruplama ve AND/OR

ile sartlandirabilir.

## Page 753

Whatsapp Contact Extension
1. Purpose and Objective

Purpose: To enable multi-address management for each contact across communication
channels (Email, SMS, WhatsApp), ensuring that during message delivery, the system can
select one or multiple addresses per contact based on configurable rules. The goal is to
extend the existing serviceâ€”currently supporting Email (E) and SMS (S)â€”with WhatsApp
(W) channel support.

Objectives:

- To store multiple communication addresses per contact in a unified data model.
Â« To enhance the API and UI to support WhatsApp addresses in addition to Email and SMS.

- To provide flexible address selection logic at the time of message delivery (manual,

automatic, multi-address, or fallback).

2. Current Situation

Currently, the system stores one email and one GSM number per contact in the main contact
table. Additional email addresses and GSM numbers are stored in an extension table. During
campaign delivery, users can select which email(s) or phone number(s) should receive the

message. Multiple selections are supported.

However, WhatsApp is not yet supported. To align WhatsApp with the same logic, the

extension table and related services must be enhanced to handle this third channel type.

Story 1- Add WhatsApp Extension in Settings

Description:

A user should be able to add a WhatsApp extension record from the Settings screen. This
record includes the WhatsApp number, label, and consent information. List should be
searchable

UATs:

- UAT-1.1: User opens Settings > Contact Extension Types and sees â€œAddâ€ option. When the

user adds a new WhatsApp number and saves, the record is successfully created.

Â« UAT-1.2: Validation prevents saving invalid WhatsApp numbers or empty required fields.

## Page 754

- UAT-1.3: After saving, the new record automatically appears in the WhatsApp extension
list.

Story 2 â€”- API Support for WhatsApp Extensions

Description:
The existing Extension API must acceptanew Channel = "W" parameter to handle
WhatsApp extensions in addition to Email (E) and SMS (S).

5-BulkUpsertExtensions
UATs:

~ UAT-2.1: API call with "Channel": "W" successfully creates a new WhatsApp
extension linked to that contact.

Â« UAT-2.2: API returns validation errors for invalid WhatsApp numbers or missing consent.

Story 3 - WhatsApp Extension Auto-Listing in Table

Description:
Once a WhatsApp extension is created, it should automatically be displayed in the extension
table.

UATs:

## Page 758

Remote Segment Columns to Customization
Purpose and Description
Problem:

Currently, when a remote segment is defined via a remote source connection, the SQL
query written for that remote source returns columns correctly, but these columns are not
stored during the segment creation process.

As a result, when users try to create dynamic content (email, onsite, in-app, WhatsApp, etc.),
remote segment columns are not available as variable placeholders â€” unlike standard

SQL-based or table columns
Need / Objective:

To ensure remote source segment columns can be used as dynamic variables in content
creation modules, by storing the column metadata during segment creation and exposing it

in the variable selection modal.

Expected Outcome:
- Remote source segment SQL result columns are saved along with the segment definition.

- When creating a content or campaign linked to that segment, users can view and insert
these columns as variables within the editor modal.

Story 1- Store Remote Source Segment Columns

Description:

When a user defines a remote segment based on a remote source SQL, the system should
extract all column names and data types from the query result and persist them during the
save operation. These columns will later be exposed to the content and campaign modules

as selectable variables.

Acceptance Criteria:

1. When saving a remote segment, the system should automatically detect and store SQL
result column metadata (name + type).

2. Editing a remote segment should update the column list accordingly

3. Remote segment kolonlari d6ndugunde alphanumeric ve alt cizgi (_) karakterler igeren

kolonlar disindakiler alinmayacak. Sistem hata vermeyecek, kolonlari dahil etmeden diger
kolonlarla islem devam edecek.

## Page 759

Story 2 - Display Remote Segment Variables in Content Builder and Flow

Description:
When creating content (email, onsite, in-app, WhatsApp), users should be able to select

variables from remote source segment columns through the variable insertion modal.

Acceptance Criteria:

1. If a selected segment is remote-source based, its columns should appear in the
Customization Modal under a â€œColumns from Remote Segment Variablesâ€ section.
2. Each column should be selectable and inserted into the content

3. Inserting variables should work across all channel editors (email, onsite, in-app,
WhatsApp).

Story 3 - Display Remote Segment Variable Values in Preview

Description:

When previewing a content or campaign that uses a remote segment, the system should

display data from the segment query result, based on the selected segment and its columns.

Acceptance Criteria:

1. When â€œPreviewâ€ is clicked, system should fetch sample row data from the segment result

2. Each placeholder in the content should be replaced with the corresponding sample value.

3. Preview should dynamically change when another segment is selected.

4. For the campaign if remote segment is chosen customization should be seen with remote

segment variables ? (whatsapp)

## Page 768

Purpose

Currently, geofence locations are created by selecting them one by one on the map.
When a user wants to mark, for example, all shopping malls across a country, they must
manually create each geofence individually. This process is time-consuming and prone to

user errors.

Within the scope of this work, it is aimed to develop a CSV upload mechanism that allows
users to create geofences in bulk.

Reference: @https://dengage.atlassian.net/browse/TP-1544 Can't find link

Scope
The following items are included in the scope of this development:

- A Bulk Upload (CSV Import) option is added to the Cluster creation screen.

- Asample CSV file is provided for users.

After a cluster is created, the user can either upload a CSV file or add geofences manually.

The CSV file is expected to contain the following columns:

o Geofence Name

o Longitude

o Latitude

o Radius

o Measure (km / mile)

- Acolumn mapping screen is displayed; if column names match exactly, the system
performs automatic column mapping.

- Geofences are created based on the rows in the CSV file and displayed on the map.

- After the user confirms the map preview, the cluster content is saved.

- The cluster becomes selectable in campaign deliveries.

- If the total number of geofences exceeds 100, an error message is shown on the import

preview screen, and the user is required to edit the CSV file.

different transactional push which
send by tags

Â« Analyze click trends by tag or a

date range

Feature Flag bulk instant push

Prerequisites

Bulk Instant Push â€” Date & Tag Based Metrics

1. Purpose & Description

Bulk Instant Push page currently lists individual push send records and displays limited
metrics per send (e.g. sent, delivered).

However, users are unable to view aggregated performance metrics for Bulk Instant Push
sends based on a selected date range or tag, and cannot evaluate overall delivery and

engagement performance for transactional or bulk use cases.

This feature extends the existing Bulk Instant Push page by introducing:

- Date-rangeâ€”based total metrics

- Tag-based filtering via manual text input

## Page 779

- Aricher total metrics summary aligned with Push Send Reports

The solution reuses existing aggregated push send tables, ensuring metric consistency and

avoiding additional processing.

2. Scope and Objective

Scope
- Enhance Bulk Instant Push page with aggregated total metrics
- Add Date Range filter affecting both list and totals
- Add Tag filter as a manual text input field
- Extend existing totals to include:
o Sent
o Delivered
o Open
o Click
o Bounce
o Error
- Use existing aggregated send tables where sent counts and related metrics are already
calculated
- Ensure totals reflect:
o Selected date range

o Entered tag(s)

Objective

- Allow users to understand overall Bulk Instant Push performance within a specific time
period

- Enable analysis of Bulk Instant Push sends by operational or functional tags

- Keep reporting behavior consistent with Push Send Reports

- Preserve existing per-send list behavior while adding aggregated insights

35. Acceptance Criteria
AC-01- Date Range Based Totals

When the user selects a date range on the Bulk Instant Push page,
Then all total metrics must be recalculated based on Bulk Instant Push sends within the

selected date range.

## Page 780

AC-02 - Tag Filter Availability

When the user views the Bulk Instant Push page,

Then a Tag filter field must be available as a manual text input.

AC-03 - Tag-Based Metric Filtering
When the user enters one or more tag values in the Tag filter field,

Then total metrics must reflect only Bulk Instant Push sends associated with the entered

tag(s).

AC-04 - Metric Accuracy

When Date Range and/or Tag filters are applied,
Then Sent, Delivered, Open, Click, Bounce, and Error totals
Must match values calculated from the existing aggregated push send table

And must be consistent with underlying send records.

AC-05 - List and Totals Consistency

When filters are applied,
Then the aggregated totals and the listed Bulk Instant Push sends

Must be derived from the same filtered dataset.

1. Purpose and Definition
Purpose

The purpose of this feature is to allow accounts to manage multi-language content delivery in a controlled, scalable,
and standards-compliant way by using BCP-47 locale codes, while also supporting limited custom locale definitions
for advanced use cases.

Definition
Localization settings enable an account to:
- Select supported locales from a predefined BCP-47-compliant dropdown list

- Configure default and fallback rules for language and region resolution

- Ensure deterministic and accurate language selection during content delivery

2. Scope and Objective
Scope
In Scope
- Selecting supported locales from a predefined dropdown list
- Adding up to 5 custom locale codes per account
- Validating and normalizing all locale codes according to BCP-47
- Defining:
o Global Default Locale
o Language-level Default Locale mappings (e.g. pt > pt-BR)
- Send-time locale resolution logic

- UI for managing enabled locales and previewing resolution behavior

Out of Scope

Â« Unlimited custom locale creation
- Free-text, unvalidated locale input
Â« Automatic content translation

- Geo-IP based language inference

## Page 783

Objectives

- Prevent incorrect or ambiguous language configuration

Â« Support regional language variants (e.g. pt-BR vs pt-PT )
- Maintain high data quality by limiting custom locale usage

- Balance flexibility for enterprise use cases with UX simplicity

- Align with industry standards and best practices

3. Acceptance Criteria

Locale Selection
- Users can add locales using a searchable dropdown populated with predefined BCP-47 locales

- Each selected locale is stored in normalized BCP-47 format (e.g. pt-br > pt-BR)

Default Locale Rules
- A Global Default Locale must be selected

- If multiple locales exist for the same language, a Language-level Default Locale must be defined

Example

1) Enabled locales: pt-BR, pt-PT
2I Default for pt: pt-BR
3

Send-Time Locale Resolution

When sending content, the system resolves locale in the following order:

1. Exact match between user locale and enabled locale
2. Language-level default locale

3. Global default locale

The resolved locale must be:

- Logged per send

- Consistent across all channels

UX & Feedback

- The system must proactively warn users when:
o A language has multiple variants but no default is selected
o A custom locale limit is reached

- Resolution behavior must be testable via a preview/tester interface

Notification Center â€” Business Analysis Document

1. Definition and Purpose

Definition

Notification Center is a central notification management area that presents notifications

generated from system-wide events to users in a tag-based, prioritized, filterable, and

actionable way.

Purpose

- Ensure users receive immediate alerts about relevant events

## Page 816

Enable notifications to prompt user actions
Provide mute/subscribe mechanisms to control notification volume
Create a flexible, scalable tag model independent of categories

Allow users to personalize notification experience in future phases

2. Scope and Objectives

2.1 Scope

Notification Display & Management (Phase-1)
Notifications appear in Notification Center in real time
Notifications are:

o Listed newest first

o Displayed in a scrollable modal
Unread count is:

o Shown on header icon

o Displays â€œ9+â€ after a threshold
Notification actions:

o Single/multiple selection

o Mark as read

o Delete

List filters:

o All notifications

o Unread notifications
Search

o Users can search within notifications.

Coupon Code Upload Feature (Phase 1)
1. Overview

Dengage provides a self-service Coupon List Upload feature, allowing users to import and
manage coupon code lists via CSV, REST API, or FTP.

2. Competitors

Platform CSV API FTP Alerts Snippe Flow Appen
Upload t Node d

Braze Yes No No Yes Yes No No

MoEngag Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes No Yes

WebEnga_ Partial No No No No No No

CleverTap No No No No No No No

Dengage Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes

Braze relies on snippet-based assignment with {% promotion('key') %} used
inside Canvas. It does not support conditional assignment or fallback through a dedicated

node.

MoEngage supports snippets via Jinja, but coupon distribution occurs when the message is

rendered. There is no node to separate assignment logic from message sending.

WebEngage allows partial CSV upload but lacks proper coupon lifecycle management.

Coupons are treated more like user data.
CleverTap does not support any coupon code upload.

Dengage will be the only platform to support a dedicated Coupon Assignment Node in
automation flows, enabling precise assignment timing, fallback logic, and campaign-level
tracking.

5. Upload Methods

We will support three coupon code import methods:

## Page 857

Add it to Content

Snippet {{ coupon('LIST_NAME') }} should be inserted into the message by a

personalization token.

Add â€œAssign Coupon Codeâ€ Node

While building a campaign flow:
- Drag the Coupon Code node into the flow and open it
- Choose the existing coupon list from the dropdown

- If no list exists, they should create a new list by modal or redirecting

Node Behaviour
- One unassigned code is fetched from the list
- Code is marked as ASSIGNED to the contact

- Code is inserted into the message content

- If a user is eligible to receive a code through multiple channels, they should receive the
same code. For example, if a user gets two messages through two channels, they'll only
receive one code. The same applies for reporting purposes. One code will be sent, and the

user will receive it through both channels.
Handle Send Failures
If no codes are available:
- Campaign send is paused

- Error logged in campaign logs

- Alert sent to configured emails

Sample for UI: @ Add Coupons to MoEngage

Sample for UI: Â© Promotion Codes

Listing Page

- Lists all created/imported coupon lists

- Columns: List Name, Snippet, Remaining Codes, Expiry, Status, Created Date, Actions

. Filters: Active/Expired/Archived, Date Range, Search by Name

Actions on Listing Page:
- View Details: See description, expiry, threshold, and import history
- Edit : Update name, description, expiry, alert settings
- Append CSV: Upload additional codes to same list

- Archive: Mark list inactive, disable further use in campaigns

## Page 858

- Export: Download remaining or all codes as CSV

- Displays total, assigned, redeemed, and remaining codes

- Warning badges for low stock or upcoming expiry

How Users Use the Codes

- In campaign creation (Email/SMS/In-App/Onsite/Whatsapp), user adds the snippet: {+
coupon('LIST_KEY') }}

- Dengage injects one unassigned code per recipient

- Code is marked as "ASSIGNED" and tied to that contact

- If no codes are available:
o The campaign send is paused with an error log

o Admin is notified via email/alerts

5. System Behavior
Max Codes per List: 20 million
File Size Limit: 100 MB

- Duplicate codes detected and flagged

- Multiple uploads allowed (append mode)

- Code statuses: UNASSIGNED , ASSIGNED

- Campaign nodes prevents reuse; each recipient gets a unique code

## Page 859

Appsflyer Partner Integration

What is AppsFlyer?

AppsFlyer is a mobile marketing attribution and deep linking platform used by mobile
marketers, product teams, and developers. It helps companies:

- Attribute mobile app installs to specific ad campaigns, partners, and channels.

- Track in-app events (e.g., purchases, sign-ups, trial starts) with real-time reporting.

- Understand user journeys and optimize advertising spend across networks like Meta,
Google Ads, TikTok, and more.

- Enable deferred deep linking to send users to specific app content even after install via a
single OneLink URL.

- Manage audience segmentation and re-engagement through push, email, or ad networks.
AppsFlyer acts as a critical analytics and campaign attribution layer in the mobile ecosystem,
especially for performance-driven and multi-channel marketing teams.

1. Why This Is Needed
- Customer Demand:

o Ostrovok and another key mobile-first customer have requested AppsFlyer integration to
enhance campaign targeting and visibility.

- Market Expectation:

o Competitors like MoEngage, WebEngage, CleverTap, and Braze already offer this
integration.

o Customers expect install source tracking, journey attribution, and deep-link consistency
in mobile campaigns.

Failing to offer this could lead to churn or lost opportunities with mobile-centric clients.
2. Objective

Develop and deploy a two-way integration between Dengage and AppsFlyer, covering:

- Inbound Postbacks: Receive install and event attribution from AppsFlyer.
- Outbound Events: Send re-engagement or conversion events back to AppsFlyer.

- Enable customers to activate this integration from the Dengage dashboard.

3. Competitor Comparison

4. User Flow

Inbound Data (AppsFlyer > Dengage):

1. User installs app via a campaign.

2. AppsFlyer attributes the install and sends postback to Dengage.
3. Dengage logs the event and enriches user profile.

4. Dengage triggers onboarding or engagement journeys.

Outbound Data (Dengage > AppsFlyer):

1. Dengage sends a push/email/in-app notification.
2. User clicks and opens the app.

3. Dengage sends re-engagement data to AppsFlyer.

4. AppsFlyer attributes session to Dengage's campaign.

2. Select Your App

## Page 863

3. Go to Partner Marketplace and search for Dengage
4. Click Activate Partner
5. Paste Customer ID / Workspace ID from Dengage
6. Enable:

o Send Install Postbacks

o Send In-App Events

o Accept Re-engagement Events
7. Choose Region (EU, Global, etc.)

8. Save and test the connection with AppsFlyer's tools

Step 2: Setup in Dengage Dashboard
1. Login to Dengage Panel
2. Go to Settings > Integrations > AppsFlyer
3. Click Connect AppsFlyer
4. Input:
o AppsFlyer App ID
o Developer Key
o Optional: Security Token for incoming postbacks
5. Toggle and configure:
o Receive Install Events
o Receive In-App Events (signup, purchase, etc.)
o Send Re-engagement Events (push click, email open)

6. Save & Enable Integration

Shopify/Mag etc Plugin Integration - Developer & User Guide (FAQ)

This document provides a comprehensive FAQ for Dengage's integration with Shopify,
Magento, and custom e-commerce platforms. It is intended for developers, QA testers, and
project managers implementing or maintaining Dengage plugins.

h2. 1. Integration Setup

Q1: What are the components of a Dengage plugin integration?
Â« SDK Script

Â« Cron job or API sync mechanism

- Push Notifications configuration

- Onsite messaging setup

- Custom events

Q2: What data does the plugin sync?

- Customer data (contacts)

- Order data

- Product catalog

- Event tracking (pageview, add-to-cart, checkout, etc.)
Q3: What platforms are supported?

Â« Shopify

- Magento 2

- Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC)

Q4: How are integrations deployed?

- Via plugin packages (ZIP or GitHub)
- Requires API key setup and CDMP access

- Recommended: deploy first on staging/sandbox

h2. 2. Data Syncing & Cron Jobs

Q5: How is data synced?

## Page 869

- Push-based (real-time via API or SDK)

- Cron-based (scheduled syncs)

Q6: Can sync frequency be changed?

- Yes, at the code level (not via UI)

- Default is every 15 minutes

Q7: What causes missing data?

Â«- API token expired or blocked
- IP not whitelisted in CDMP
- Incorrect plugin version

- Errors in logs (validate cron or API calls)

Q8: What to check if product image is missing?

- Parent product may not have image; fallback to variant image

- Sync config may need adjustment

h2. 3. Event Tracking

Q9: What events are tracked by default?
- Homepage View

- Category Page View

- Product Page View

- Add to Cart / Remove from Cart

- Begin Checkout

- Order Completed

Q10: How are events tracked?

- Via the JavaScript SDK loaded on the website
- Data passed to Dengage via event objects
QT1: Can custom events be added?

- Yes, via SDK or API

- Examples: wishlist added, filter used, click tracking

Q12: What causes web events to not appear?
- SDK not loaded
Â« Domain mismatch

- Ad blockers or CSP restrictions

## Page 870

h2. 4. Web Push & Onsite Messaging

Q13: How is Web Push enabled?

- SDK installed

- VAPID key configured in CDMP

- Permission requested by browser

Q14: Why does push say ' 2 Salesforce: The #1 AI CRM ' or wrong domain?
- Staging domain used for SDK

Â« Root domain mismatch

Q15: Can push be triggered on order completion?

- Only if a campaign is configured to listen to that event
- Not default behavior from backend sync

Q16: How to validate push functionality?

- Accept push permission

- Inspect console logs for token registration

Â« Check in CDMP > Channels > Web Push Tokens

Q17: Is push the same as onsite messaging?

- No, onsite is rendered directly on page

- Push requires browser permission

h2. 5. Debugging & Logs
Q18: Where are logs stored in Magento?
- Typically in /var/log/dengage_sync.1log

Q19: What to do if contact is not created?

- Check sync logs

Â« Confirm email is set (used as contact key)
- Ensure IP is not blocked

Q20: What causes duplicate contacts?

- Missing deduplication logic

- Inconsistent use of contact key (email vs phone)

Q21: How to split name & surname in contact sync?

## Page 871

Â« Modify plugin mapping logic
- Separate fields before sending to Dengage
Q22: What to do if new registrations donâ€™t sync?

- Wait for cron to run or trigger it manually

- Check logs for error or delay

h2. 6. Testing & QA Best Practices

Q23: How to test event tracking?

- Use browser console to inspect SDK

- Trigger events manually

- Use GTM to simulate events if needed
Q24: What is needed for full QA validation?
- Product sync verification

- Order and contact appearance in CDMP
- Web push token registration

- Triggered push or onsite display

Q25: Can QA test while data is syncing?

- Yes, events will still trigger via SDK

- Full data sync may lag slightly behind
Q26: How to confirm wishlist or cart event sync?

- Use developer tools > Network > look for event payload

- Check event logs in CDMP

h2. 7. Plugin Deployment & Maintenance

Q27: How are plugin versions tracked?

Â« GitHub repo shared with client (access controlled)
- Changelogs and release notes published

Q28: How to switch plugin versions?

- Remove old code
- Upload and configure new plugin

- Always test on staging first

## Page 872

Q29: Can clients request a central changelog?

- Yes, hosted on GitHub or shared Google Drive

Q30: What should be shared with client post-deployment?
Â¢ Plugin zip

- Version changelog

- Test plan document

- Access to repo (GitHub or drive)

h2. 8. Known Issues & Fixes

Q31: Product image not showing?

- Use first variant image if parent missing

Q32: Add-to-cart slows down site?

- Switch to batch sync

- Avoid real-time event overload

Q33: Cron job not running?

- Check server cron logs

- Validate cron schedule in Magento config
Q34: Push not showing after order?

- No campaign is tied to order_complete event

Q35: Sync failed due to token issue?

- Ensure IP is whitelisted

- Regenerate API token if expired

Q36: Error fetching API token?

- Invalid credentials

Â« Missing IP whitelist

Q37: Event appears but no data in table?

- Field mismatch in mapping

- Event triggered before product sync

h2. 9. Admin & Configuration

Q38: How to whitelist IPs in CDMP?

## Page 873

- Login to CDMP > Project Settings > IP Whitelist

Q39: Can cron schedule be changed by client?

- Only via code

- Dengage team can customize and deliver updated plugin
Q40: Can plugin be installed on multiple stores?

- Yes, as long as each store uses unique API credentials

## Page 878

Recommendation Engine

The Dengage Recommendation Engine enables marketers to deliver personalised, context-

aware product recommendations across all communication channels (email, SMS, push, in-

app, onsite, WhatsApp). It combines behavioural data, catalogue attributes, and business

rules to maximise relevance and conversion.

This document contains:

Recommendation types Dengage supports
Events required to power them
Example scenarios of usage

Fallback strategies for cold start or missing data

1. Concepts

- Catalogue: A product feed uploaded to Dengage, containing product attributes (ID, title,

category, brand, price, discount, images, stock, etc.).

. Events: User actions collected from web, app, or backend systems ( product_view ,

purchase , add_to_cart ).

- Recommendation Models: Algorithms combining event/user/session data and catalogue

attributes to generate suggestions.

- Fallbacks: Predefined rules ensuring recommendations are always served even if

personalised data is missing.

5. Fallback Strategy Principles

- Always serve content, even with no user history (optional: user can choose not to show
anything)

- Use popularity (trending/bestsellers) as a universal fallback

- Use category or brand-level defaults when context exists but behaviour is missing

- Curated or campaign-driven sets can override algorithmic fallbacks when needed

4. Next Steps
- Define API endpoints for each recommendation type

- Create marketer-facing UI for selecting models, setting fallback rules, and previewing

results

- Enable analytics dashboards (CTR, CVR, revenue uplift per recommendation type)

## Page 888

Dengage Recommendation Models Specification (Phase 1)

1. Overview

Phase 1 of Dengageâ€™s Recommendation Engine focuses on non-session-based
recommendation algorithms built from existing event and catalog data. The goal is to provide
customers with scalable and flexible product recommendation logic that can be used across
all Dengage channels. Each recommendation model can be created once and reused in any
channel or campaign through widgets or API calls.

Key Terms

Input (Seed)

This is the data point that drives the recommendation. It can be a product, category, or user-
level attribute, derived from static selections or event attributes.

Possible sources for input data:

- Static Product or Category ID: Customer manually chooses a product or category.

- User Attribute: Derived from user profile data (e.g., last purchased category).

- Event Attribute: Derived dynamically from an event (e.g., product added to basket).
Dengage automatically interprets the input to deliver the correct recommendation logic.

Event

Events are tracked user or system activities that provide behavioral or transactional data to

the recommendation models (e.g., ProductView, AddToBasket, PurchaseOrder).
Filter

Filters allow customers to refine recommendation results (limit by category, brand, discount

range, or exclude low-stock items.)
Global Rules

Defines high-level behavioral exclusions and logic settings applied across all

recommendation outputs.
Fallback

Specifies what to show if a recommendation produces insufficient results (fallback to

Category Bestsellers if â€œFrequently Bought Togetherâ€ has no matches).

Refresh Frequency

## Page 889

Determines how often data is recalculated (real-time, hourly, or daily), depending on model

type.

5. Global Rules

Each recommendation model supports the following global settings, configurable in the
builder or via API:

1. Hide widget if not enough products: Prevent display when results fall below a minimum
threshold (e.g., <3 products).

2. Exclude recently purchased items: Exclude items purchased in the last X days (customer
defines X).

3. Exclude recently viewed products: Exclude items viewed in the last X days (customer
defines X).

4. Exclude products in cart: Prevent recommending items currently in the userâ€™s basket.

5. Show only products in stock: Display only items with available inventory; customers can

define the minimum stock level.

6. Recommendation Model Detailed Analysis

Purchase-driven Models

Top Sellers

Description: Products with highest sales volume in a defined time period.

Events Needed: PurchaseOrderItem

Input (Seed): None (global aggregation)

Calculation Method: Aggregate purchases by product_id; rank by total sales or quantity.
Filters: Category, Brand, Price, Time window

Example Scenario: Retailer highlights â€œTop 20 Bestsellersâ€ in weekly newsletter.
Refresh Frequency: Daily

Fallback: Category Bestsellers.

Category Bestsellers

Description: Bestselling items within a specific category.
Events Needed: PurchaseOrderlItem, CategoryView

Input (Seed): Category ID from event or static selection
Calculation Method: Aggregate by category; rank by quantity.
Filters: Category, Brand, Price, Time window

Example Scenario: PDP shows â€œTop Sellers in this Category.â€

## Page 893

Refresh Frequency: Daily
Fallback: Global Top Sellers.

Frequently Bought Together

Description: Products frequently purchased together.

Events Needed: PurchaseOrder, PurchaseOrderltem

Input (Seed): Product ID(s) from order or basket event

Calculation Method: Association rule mining using support, confidence, and lift.
Filters: Category, Brand

Example Scenario: PDP widget displays accessories bought with the viewed product.
Refresh Frequency: Every 12 hours

Fallback: Category Bestsellers.

Catalog-driven Models

New Arrivals

Description: Recently added catalog products.

Events Needed: Catalog (created_at)

Input (Seed): Category ID (optional)

Calculation Method: Filter items created within last N days.

Filters: Category, Brand, Price, Date range

Example Scenario: Onsite or email block highlights â€œNew Arrivals in Running Shoes.â€
Refresh Frequency: Daily

Fallback: Category Bestsellers.

Discounted Products

Description: Currently discounted products.

Events Needed: Catalog (price, original_price)

Input (Seed): Category ID or none

Calculation Method: Compute discount percentage; filter = threshold.

Filters: Category, Brand, Discount %, Price range

Example Scenario: Newsletter promotes â€œUp to 40% Offâ€ items per userâ€™s interest category.
Refresh Frequency: Every 6 hours

Fallback: Top Sellers.
Price Drop Products

Description: Products whose price recently decreased.

Events Needed: Catalog Delta

Input (Seed): Product or Category ID

Calculation Method: Detect price changes; rank by percentage drop.

Filters: Category, Brand, Price drop %

## Page 894

Example Scenario: Push notification alerts user that â€œPrice dropped on your viewed item.â€
Refresh Frequency: Real-time

Fallback: Discounted Products.

Behavior-driven Models
Last Visited Products

Description: Recently viewed products for a user.

Events Needed: ProductView

Input (Seed): User ID

Calculation Method: Deduplicate and rank by recency.

Filters: Category, Recency (days)

Example Scenario: Homepage shows â€œRecently Viewed Items.â€
Refresh Frequency: Real-time

Fallback: Category Bestsellers.

Alerts

Price Drop Alert

Description: Alerts users when tracked products decrease in price.
Events Needed: Catalog Delta, WishList, AddToBasket

Input (Seed): Product ID from WishList/AddToBasket

Calculation Method: Detect price changes above threshold.
Filters: Category, Brand, Price drop %

Example Scenario: Email: â€œA product you liked is now 20% off.â€
Refresh Frequency: Real-time

Fallback: Discounted Products.
Back in Stock Alert

Description: Alerts when previously unavailable products return.

Events Needed: [nventoryUpdate, WishList, AddToBasket

Input (Seed): Product ID from WishList/AddToBasket

Calculation Method: Detect inventory change from 0 to positive.

Filters: Category, Brand, Minimum stock

Example Scenario: Notify user via push when their wishlisted product is back in stock.
Refresh Frequency: Real-time

Fallback: None.

Low Stock Alert

Description: Alerts users when products are nearly out of stock.
Events Needed: InventoryUpdate
Input (Seed): Product ID (from userâ€™s WishList, Basket, or ProductView)

## Page 895

Calculation Method: Trigger when stock < threshold.
Filters: Category, Brand, Stock threshold

Example Scenario: Display â€œOnly 3 leftâ€ onsite or via push.
Refresh Frequency: Real-time

Fallback: None.

Notes

This document defines all Phase 1 algorithms and data models. These models are channel-

agnostic and can be used in any Dengage campaign or personalisation experience.

The following models were evaluated but excluded from Phase 1 and may be added later:

- Basket Affinity

- Products by Brand

- Products by Price Range
- Last Purchased Products
- Wishlist-Based

- Cross-Sell

- Upsell

A separate Recommendation Builder UI/UX Specification document will define the

configuration experience for customers.

## Page 909

Allow Custom Column Creation for Product and Order Tables

Overview

This request aims to allow customers to extend Product and Order tables by adding custom
columns via both UI and API. The core table structure must remain fully protected. Only

customer-created custom columns can be updated (e.g. name change), while system-
defined columns cannot be modified in any way.

Problem Product and Order tables currently have a fixed
schema. Customers cannot store additional

business-specific attributes.
Customer Name -
Request Link -

Link
Feature Flag No

Prerequisites -

1. Purpose and Definition

- Enable controlled schema extensibility by allowing customers to add custom columns to
Product and Order tables.

- Critical Constraint:
o Core (system-defined) table structure must not be altered.
o Only custom-added columns are manageable by users.

- Why Dengage needs this:

o Preserves data integrity and backward compatibility.
o Prevents accidental breaking of existing data flows.

o Provides flexibility without compromising platform stability.

2. Scope and Objectives

In Scope

## Page 910

- Adding, updating, and deleting custom columns to Product tables via UI and API. (5- Upser

tProduct )

- Adding, updating, and deleting custom columns to Order tables via UI and API. (5- Upsert

Orders )

- Updating metadata (e.g. column name) of custom columns only.

- UI availability controlled by an existing frontend parameter.

- Backend enforcement of system vs custom column separation.

Out of Scope

- Any modification of system/default columns.

- Deleting system columns.

- Changing data types of existing columns.

- Structural changes to Product or Order base schemas.

Key Objectives

- Protect core Product and Order table structures.

- Allow safe and controlled schema extension.

- Ensure identical rules across UI and API.

- Prevent misuse that could break existing data pipelines.

Dependencies and Required Components

- Settings Page Changes:

UI must clearly distinguish system columns from custom columns.

- APIs:

o Create custom column

o Update custom column metadata

## Page 915

Segment Versioning for Interactive and SQL Segments

Overview

Problem Clients can view only the latest version of a segment
in the panel. Historical segment definitions are not
accessible via the UI. This creates a significant gap
when analyzing why a campaign or flow was

triggered for a specific audience in the past.

Client Name All Clients

Request Link RP-708: ALL I ALL DC (Cloud & OnPrem) I Segme
nt Versiyonlarinin Panel Uzerinden Goriintlenebilme
si lcin Gelistirme Talebi quseram

Figma Link -

Technical Analysis = -

Link

Feature Flag No

Prerequisites -

1. Purpose and Definition

Currently, users can only view the latest version of a segment from the panel. Historical
segment definitions are not accessible via the UI. This creates a significant gap when

analyzing why a campaign or flow was triggered for a specific audience in the past.

When an unexpected delivery occurs, the support team must identify which segment logic
was active at send time. Today, this is only possible by manually querying the
sys_panel_audit_log table in the database.

This process:
- Requires technical expertise
- Is time-consuming

- Increases operational and support workload

- Delays root cause analysis and customer communication

## Page 916

The lack of UI-level segment version history prevents clear visibility into historical targeting

logic and makes post-send analysis inefficient.

This feature introduces segment versioning and historical access, aligned with existing
versioning behavior for Content and Automated Flows, enabling users to inspect past
segment logic directly from the panel.

2. Scope and Objectives

In Scope
- Versioning for:
o Interactive Segments
o SQL Segments

This task enables Shopify merchants to select which custom Product and Order columns
should be synced to Dengage. A new configuration screen will be added to the Dengage
Shopify application settings. The Shopify app will first ensure selected custom columns exist
in Dengage (via API) and then start sending data for those columns. This feature is

dependent on the completion of Custom Column Support for Product & Order Tables.

Problem After enabling custom columns in Dengage Product
and Order tables, Shopify merchants need control
over which Shopify custom fields are synced.
Automatically syncing all fields can cause
unnecessary data load.

1. Purpose and Definition
Â« Enable controlled schema extensibility by allowing customers to add custom columns to
Product and Order tables.
- Critical Constraint:
o Core (system-defined) table structure must not be altered.
o Only custom-added columns are manageable by users.
- Why Dengage needs this:
o Preserves data integrity and backward compatibility.

o Prevents accidental breaking of existing data flows.

o Provides flexibility without compromising platform stability.

In Scope
- Shopify App UI
o Add anew configuration screen (or section) under existing Application Settings.
o Display available custom Product and Order fields detected from Shopify.
o Allow merchants to select which custom fields should be synced.
- Sync Logic
o For each selected field:

missing).

completed and available.

- Separation

Out of Scope

- Editing or deleting custom columns from this screen.

- Give merchants explicit control over synced custom fields.

- Ensure Dengage schema is extended only when needed.

- Maintain a clear and predictable sync process.

Generative AI Content Creation
Overview

This development enables users to generate and optimize marketing content across Email, SMS/MMS, Push, WhatsApp, In-
App, and Onsite channels using generative AI.

The system learns from Brand Kits, AI Personas, and optionally from previous campaign data (text + images) to maintain
brand consistency and creative quality.

Objectives

1. Reduce campaign content creation time.

2. Deliver brand-consistent, multilingual (connect with AI translate), and tone-accurate content.
3. Enable scalable creative automation across all communication channels.

4. Gradually evolve from element-level assistance > full content generation > campaign creation > Creative Agent > Action
Agent

Core Foundation (Under Settings)
1. Brand Kit
A centralized repository defining visual and stylistic identity. Not just for AI, but also useful for manual content creation.

Fields:

- Brand Name

- Primary / Secondary Colors
- Font Families

- Logo Upload

- CTA

- Header/Footer templates

- Design patterns or layout presets

Usage:
Brand Kit automatically applies to every generated image or layout suggestion.

When AI generates visuals or complete templates, it adheres to these brand parameters.
2. AI Brand Persona

A configuration defining brand tone, communication style, and voice.

Fields:

- Business Model (Explaining what the users brand does etc.)

- Prompt(Optional)

- Positive Keywords

- Negative Keywords

- Tone (Friendly, Professional, Playful etc.)

- Voice (Formal, Conversational, Luxury, etc.)

- Target Audience Keywords (Gen Z, Tech-Savvy, Fashion)

- Style Prompts (from MoEngage-like prompt schema: â€œUse emojis,â€ â€œSound like a luxury brand,â€ â€œFocus on conversion,â€ etc.)
- Default Language

- Option to associate a Brand Kit

Optional Switches:

Use accountâ€™s previous content for AI training (text + image)

Acceptance Criteria for AI Brand Persona

Users can list, create, duplicate, edit, and delete multiple AI Brand Personas.

Users can set a default persona that automatically applies to all new Al-generated content.
Each persona includes configurable fields: Persona Name, Linked Brand Kit, Prompt,
Include/Exclude Keywords, Target Audience, Tone, Writing Style, Output Language, and AI
Training.

Users can link each persona to a specific Brand Kit to maintain visual and tonal
consistency.

If AI Training is enabled, the persona learns tone and phrasing patterns from past and
future campaigns.

The default persona is applied to all new content unless the user manually selects another
one.

Deleting a persona removes it from all selection lists but does not affect previously
generated content.

Validation prevents saving personas without required fields (Persona Name, Brand Kit,
Target Audience, Tone, Writing Style, and Output Language).

All persona fields include tooltips providing brief explanations for easier setup.

## Page 952

Coupon Code Generation for Shopify

This document outlines how Dengage will manage unique coupon code generation through Shopify's Admin API. It
covers Shopify's API rate limits, performance across plan tiers, implementation strategies, supported coupon types,
and the recommended architecture for scalable, reliable code generation.

1. Shopify API Limits & Cost System

What Is a Leaky Bucket Algorithm? w Leaky bucket

Shopify uses a leaky bucket algorithm to manage API traffic and prevent overloading their systems. Think of it like a
bucket with a small hole at the bottom:

Â« The bucket size is the maximum burst capacity (1,000 cost units).
- Water (API calls) is added when you send a request.

- Water leaks out at a fixed rate (50 cost units/second).

If you try to pour too much water too quickly (send too many requests), the bucket overflows and Shopify returns a

429 Too Many Requests error.

Shopify uses it to throttle API usage on its GraphQL Admin API. Understanding this system is crucial to designing a
reliable and scalable coupon-generation feature.

Key Rate Limiting Concepts

Term Value

Bucket Size 1,000 cost units

Refill Rate 50 cost units per second

Max Cost/Query 1,000 units (hard cap)

Typical Coupon Call ~50 units per 250 codes (bulk
mutation)

Max Array Input 250 items per GraphQL call

Example:
- 1request = 250 codes = ~50 units
- You can safely make 1 request per second (matching refill rate)

- Bursting: You can send ~20 requests instantly (1,000 / 50), then wait for refill (which is a risky way to manage)

## Page 953

Rate limits

Total Unique Code Limit

Â« Shopify enforces a hard cap of 20 million discount codes per store. This includes:

o Active codes
o Expired codes

o Disabled codes

- Deleted codes do NOT count toward the limit.

Limiting Warnings

- Track the total codes generated per store via metadata

- Block or warn users when approaching the 20M cap

Â« Show a warning banner at 18 million codes:

"Your store is nearing the 20 million coupon code limit enforced by Shopify. Please delete expired or unused

codes to free space."
- We can introduce features like:

o Archive + delete old codes

o Auto-delete expired codes after a configurable duration.

6. Refill Model (Rolling Pool Generation)

For flows, Dengage will adopt a refill model similar to Klaviyo.

Logic:
- System keeps a buffer pool of unique codes (e.g., 600 codes)
- If available drops below threshold (e.g., 400), Dengage automatically creates a new batch

- For relative expirations (e.g., 3 days after send), generate fresh codes daily

UI Indicators:

- "Low inventory" badge if code pool < threshold
- "Generating more codes..." progress state

- Admin is alerted if refills fail or inventory is empty

## Page 959

Sticky Bar Improvement
Overview

This document outlines a proposed enhancement to Dengage's sticky bar feature, enabling a
new optional behavior for top-positioned bars to appear as a banner on page load and
become sticky upon scroll. This update is based on client feedback regarding mobile

usability conflicts (e.g., overlapping login buttons).

Problem Statement

Clients using the sticky bar on mobile have reported UX issues where the bar, fixed at the top
of the screen, interferes with critical UI components (e.g., login or register buttons). Current
positioning options are limited to top or bottom, without scroll behavior or margin

offset.
Objective

Introduce a scroll-triggered behavior that allows the sticky bar to initially appear in a non-
fixed position (like a banner), and then become sticky (fixed) after the user starts scrolling.
This improves usability, particularly on mobile, while preserving visibility and conversion
potential.

Proposed Behavior

State Behavior

Page Load Sticky bar is placed statically at the

top of the page (before content).

On Scroll Sticky bar becomes fixed and

remains visible.

Optional Controlled via new toggle: Stick

on Scroll.

For Position: Bottom

Â« No change in behavior.
. Always position: fixed; bottom: Q;

- "Sticky on Scroll" setting is disabled or hidden for this case.

## Page 961

MAU Report

1. Overview

The MAU Report provides a consolidated view of user, contact, and device activity over a
rolling 50-day period.

The report is placed under Analytics > Reports and becomes visible only for accounts where
the MAU billing feature flag is enabled.

The design attached in this PRD is a mockup and illustrates the intended layout and user

experience.

2. Objective

- Allow customers to view how many users, contacts, and devices were active at least once
in the last 30 days.

- Provide transparency for MAU-based billing.
- Offer day-by-day visibility through a line chart showing the historical trend of all three

metrics.
3. Definitions
Total Active User

Info Tooltip: A user is counted as active if they have at least one session within the last 30

days. (Active Contact + Active Device = Total Active User)

Active Contact

Info Tooltip: A contact that has had at least one session within the last 30 days.
Active Device

Info Tooltip: A device that has had at least one session within the last 30 days.

All three values are calculated using a rolling 30-day window, not a calendar month.
Blue Infobox

â€œThe values shown in Total Active Users, Active Contacts, and Active Devices are all based
on activity from the last 30 days. Each metric reflects how many users, contacts, or devices

were active at least once during this 50-day period.â€
