Multi-Segment Selection in Target Audience for Campaigns

Overview

Problem

Customer Name

Request Link

Figma Link

Technical Analysis
Link

Feature Flag

Prerequisites

1. Purpose and Definition

Currently, n11 creates multiple new segments for
each campaign by combining existing segments
externally using logical AND / OR conditions. Each
campaign-specific combination results in a new
segment, leading to excessive segment proliferation
and increased operational overhead. Over time, this
leads to poor segment manageability, reduced

clarity, and a higher risk of misconfiguration.
N11

RP-444: n11 I Segmenti Kampanya Alaninda Olust
Ura GNISPRINT)

The customer requests the ability to select multiple existing segments directly within the

campaign Target Audience selection and logically combine them using AND / OR, without

creating a new persistent segment entity.

The objective is to:

- Eliminate unnecessary segment duplication.

- Reduce campaign setup time and operational workload.

- Keep segment management clean while preserving campaign flexibility.

This enhancement impacts both Flow campaigns (Audience node) and Quick Campaign

audience selection, ensuring functional consistency across campaign types.

Competitor Analysis (High-Level)

## Page 965

MoEngage: Allows advanced audience filters within campaigns but typically encourages
saving combined audiences as reusable segments.

WebEngage: Supports multiple conditions in campaign audience selection; segment reuse
is emphasized, but campaign-level logical grouping exists.

Braze: Enables multiple segment selection with boolean logic directly in campaign
targeting, without forcing segment creation.

CleverTap: Allows real-time logical combinations during campaign setup; segments can
be ephemeral or saved.

Insider: Supports campaign-level audience composition with AND/OR logic across
multiple segments.

Emarsys: Relies more on predefined segments; limited flexibility at campaign-level without

creating new segments.

2. Scope and Objectives

In Scope

Ability to select multiple segments in:

o Flow Campaign > Audience node

0 Quick Campaign > Target Audience selection
Logical operators:

o AND

o OR

Correct audience calculation with:

o User deduplication

o Deterministic calculation results
Campaign-level audience definition without creating a new saved segment
Logging of:

o Selected segment IDs

o Logical operator used

Backward compatibility with existing single-segment behavior

Out of Scope

Persisting combined segments as reusable standalone segments
Nested logical grouping (e.g., (A AND B) OR C)
Changes to segment builder UI

Historical recalculation of past campaigns

Key Objectives

## Page 966

- Reduce segment clutter.
- Simplify campaign setup.
Â« Maintain calculation accuracy and performance.

- Preserve auditability and campaign-to-audience traceability.

Dependencies and Required Components
- Audience calculation service

- Campaign execution engine

- Logging and reporting services

APIs

- Extend existing audience calculation API to accept:
o Multiple segment IDs

o Logical operator parameter

35. Acceptance Criteria

Criteria Code Description

AC-01 The user must be able to select more than

one segment in the Flow Campaign Audience

node.

AC-02 The user must be able to define the logical
operator (AND / OR) between the selected
segments.

AC-03 When AND is selected, the system must

calculate the target audience as the

intersection of the selected segments.

AC-04 When OR is selected, the system must
calculate the target audience as the union of
the selected segments and remove duplicate

users.

AC-05 If a user exists in multiple selected segments,
the user must appear only once in the final

Campaign audience.

AC-06 The audience calculation must be triggered
and behave consistently with the existing

Calculate mechanism.

## Page 967

AC-07 When the campaign is saved, the system

must not create a new persistent segment;
the segment combination must be stored only

at the campaign level.

AC-08 Campaign logs and campaign details must

clearly display all selected segment IDs and

the applied logical operator.

AC-09 Existing campaigns using a single segment

must continue to work without any behavioral

or calculation changes.

AC-10 The multi-segment audience selection must

be available in both Flow Campaigns and

Quick Campaigns.

AC-11 The campaign must not be allowed to start

unless the audience calculation is

successfully completed.

AC-12 For campaigns using multiple segments, the

Ccampaign-to-audience relationship must
remain traceable through logs for

retrospective analysis.

. Design

User opens Flow Campaign or Quick Campaign.

User double-clicks Target Audience / Audience node.

Segment selection modal opens.

User selects multiple segments from the list.

User selects logical operator (OR).

System displays calculation option as usual.

On calculate:

o Backend computes audience based on selected logic.

o Overlapping users are deduplicated where applicable.

Campaign saves audience configuration as a campaign-level definition.
Execution and reporting reference this composed audience definition.

Logs and insights associate campaign with multiple segment IDs and operator, not a new

segment entity.

1. Purpose and Definition

Problem: Today, whenever a user selects a customization tag, it is immediately inserted into
the active editor. This behavior creates inconsistent, error-prone personalization because
users cannot define fallback behavior at insertion time and must manually craft fallback logic

(or accept blank values).

Requested change: The improvement must be available everywhere customization is
available (all editors/areas where the customization selector is used), not only a single

channel/editor.

2. Scope and Objectives

In Scope

Whenever a user selects a customization tag, it is
immediately inserted into the active editor. This
behavior creates inconsistent, error-prone
personalization because users cannot define
fallback behavior at insertion time and must

manually craft fallback logic (or accept blank values).

Wizz Air

selecting a customization tag in all surfaces that expose customization, including but not

limited to:

o Email editor(s)

## Page 970

o Push / Web Push message editor(s)

o In-App message editor(s)

o SMS / WhatsApp message editor(s)

o Any other builder/editor where the â€œCustomization Selectorâ€ component is used
- Support fallback strategies (context-aware):

o No fallback

o Replace text (requires fallback value)

o Do not send (only if supported for the relevant channel/runtime; otherwise, disabled with

explanation)

- Auto-insert:

o the selected placeholder/tag, and

o an if/else logic snippet compatible with the relevant editor/runtime

Out of Scope

- Introducing new runtime personalization engines if none exist for a channel.

- Defining brand-new â€œskip sendâ€ semantics; we only reuse what is already supported,
otherwise the option must be disabled.

Â« Reworking existing content rendering pipelines beyond what is necessary to support the

inserted output safely.

Oracle is missing support for Segment, Table, and SQL Editor export capabilities that are

available for comparable database Remote Targets (Microsoft SQL, PostgreSQL, ODBC).

## Page 974

Why Dengage Needs This

1. Feature Parity: Oracle should have the same export capabilities as Microsoft SQL and
PostgreSQL, which are comparable relational database targets.

2. Enterprise Customer Demand: Oracle is the dominant database in enterprise environments
(insurance, banking, telecommunications). Limited Oracle export support restricts
Dengage's ability to serve these customers.

3. Data Symmetry: Customers expect bidirectional data flow. If they can import from Oracle,
they should be able to export to Oracle.

4. Product Positioning: Completing Oracle export support strengthens Dengage's position as

an enterprise-grade CDP.

2. Scope and Objectives
Functional Requirements:
1. Segment Export to Oracle
o Export segment results to a specified Oracle table
o Support via Automated Flows (scheduled) and manual export
o Column mapping between segment fields and Oracle columns
2. Table Export to Oracle
o Export any Dengage Data Space table to Oracle
o Support full export (truncate + insert) and incremental (upsert)
o Configurable primary key for incremental mode

3. SQL Editor Export to Oracle
o Export SQL query results directly to an Oracle table

o Maintain existing SQL Editor interface, add Oracle as a destination option

## Page 1027

Master Contact Extensions Reporting Enhancement
Overview

This document outlines proposed enhancements to Dengage's reporting and history features
to properly display Master Contact Extensions data. Currently, when users utilize the Master
Contact Extensions feature to communicate via alternative email addresses or phone
numbers, all reporting and history records default to the master contact's primary
email/phone rather than the actual recipient used for communication. This creates confusion
and prevents clients from accurately tracking which contact method was used for each

campaign.

Problem Statement
Clients using the Master Contact Extensions feature report the following issues:

1. Campaign Canvas Reports: When a campaign is sent to an extension email (not the
master contact's primary email), the campaign canvas shows the master contact email

instead of the actual recipient email used for delivery.

2. Contact Card Campaign History: There is no indication of which specific email address
received the campaign when viewing a contact's campaign history, making it impossible to
distinguish between sends to primary vs. extension emails.

3. Permission History Gaps: Permission history logs do not include actions related to
extension emails and phone numbers, creating incomplete audit trails.

These limitations prevent clients from:

- Accurately reporting on multi-email/phone communication strategies

- Understanding which contact method is most effective

- Maintaining complete permission and compliance records

Objective

Enhance reporting and history features to accurately reflect the actual email address or
phone number used for each communication, rather than defaulting to the master contact's
primary identifiers. This will enable clients to:

- Track campaign performance by specific contact methods

Â« Maintain accurate communication histories

- Ensure complete permission and compliance logging

Proposed Changes

## Page 1030

Additional Security Feature - Role based access
Overview

This document outlines a comprehensive permission system enhancement for Dengage's Settings page. Currently,
users with "Account Settings" permission can edit all settings items. The proposed system introduces granular, role-
based permissions at both category and individual item levels, with three permission types (View, Edit, No Access)
and automatic UI visibility control based on permissions.

Problem Statement
The current permission system has several limitations:

1. All-or-Nothing Access: Users with "Account Settings" permission can edit all settings, creating security and
operational risks.
2. No View-Only Access: There's no way to give users view-only access to settings for audit or reference purposes.

3. Visibility Issues: Users see settings they cannot access, leading to confusion and unnecessary support requests.

These limitations prevent clients from:

- Implementing principle of least privilege
- Providing audit access without edit rights

- Maintaining proper separation of duties

Objective
Implement a hierarchical, granular permission system that:

- Allows role-based permission assignment at both category and item levels
- Supports three permission types: View, Edit, and No Access

- Automatically hides UI elements based on permissions

- Maintains backward compatibility with existing roles

Â« Enables flexible role creation for diverse organizational needs

## Page 1033

Gmail Promotions Tab Integration for Email Service
Overview

This document outlines the integration of Gmail Promotions Tab features into Dengage's email service. Gmail's
Promotions Tab allows marketers to enhance their promotional emails with rich annotations including product
images, discount offers, expiration dates, and deal badges. These annotations appear directly in Gmail's Promotions
Tab, increasing email visibility and engagement without any cost. This feature is available only to consumer Gmail

users (not Google Workspace users) and uses HiSchema.org - Schema.org structured data markup.

Problem Statement

Dengage currently has a partial implementation of Gmail Promotions Tab annotations, but it suffers from several

critical issues that prevent the feature from working properly:

1. Date Format Error: The existing implementation uses an incorrect date format, causing Gmail to reject the
annotations. The current format does not comply with ISO 8601 standard required by Gmail, resulting in
annotations not being displayed.

2. Limited Annotation Types: Only 2 out of 4 available Gmail annotation types are currently supported, preventing
clients from using the full range of promotional features Gmail offers.

3. Missing Fields: Clients cannot utilize many optional fields that could enhance their email's appearance and

effectiveness in Gmail's Promotions Tab.

4. HTML Stripping Issue: When clients attempt to manually add HSchema.org - Schema.org markup to their email
HTML, the system strips it out during the save process. This prevents technically savvy users from implementing
workarounds or using advanced features not available in the UI.

5. No Validation or Error Messaging: Without proper validation, clients have no way to know why their annotations
aren't appearing in Gmail or how to fix the issues.
These issues result in:

- Wasted client effort in setting up annotations that don't work
Â« Support burden from clients reporting "Gmail annotations not showing"
- Competitive disadvantage against ESPs with working implementations

- Loss of potential engagement and conversion improvements

Objective
Fix and enhance Dengage's Gmail Promotions Tab integration to:

- Fix Date Format: Implement correct ISO 8601 date formatting to make existing annotations work

- Add Missing Annotation Types: Implement 2 missing types

- Expose All Fields: Enable all optional HSchema.org - Schema.org fields for each annotation type

- Preserve Manual Markup: Stop stripping Hi Schema.org - Schema.org markup from HTML, allowing advanced

users to add custom markup

Success criteria:

- All 4 annotation types functional and displaying correctly in Gmail

- Manual markup preserved in HTML editor

- Date format issues resolved (ISO 8601 compliance)

## Page 1048

This feature aims to improve the CSV import workflow by addressing three critical user

experience issues:

1. Unmapped Column Detection: Users currently can proceed past the mapping step
without mapping all columns, leading to import failures with unclear error messages.

2. Simplified Table Creation: Users must manually create tables and define columns in Data
Space > Tables before importing CSV files

3. Regular Table Support & Auto Column Detection: Regular Tables cannot be created from

import flow, and Send List tables don't automatically detect columns from CSV data.

The solution will provide visual indicators for unmapped columns, validation before
proceeding, automatic table creation from CSV files, Regular Table support, and automatic

column detection for all table types.

2. Scope and Objectives
Objectives:

- Prevent import failures due to unmapped columns
- Improve user experience with clear visual feedback and validation
- Enable Regular Table creation from CSV import flow

Â« Implement automatic column detection for all table types (Send List and Regular Table)

Expected Outcomes:

- 60-80% reduction in import-related support tickets

- Faster onboarding for new users uploading their first dataset

- Elimination of "Import disabled for the '' column!" errors

- Both Send List and Regular Table can be created directly from CSV import

- Columns are automatically detected and created for all table types

In Scope

Phase 1: Mapping Improvements

Â« Red border highlighting for unmapped columns

Â« Alert banner showing unmapped column count

Â« "Exclude unmapped columns" checkbox functionality
Â« Disabled Next button when unmapped columns exist

Â« Automatic Next button activation when exclusion is selected

Phase 2: Table Type Support Enhancement

## Page 1049

Â« Enable Regular Table creation from CSV import flow
- Add table type selector (Regular Table / Send List) in table configuration

- Ensure both table types support same functionality

Phase 3: Auto Table Creation & Column Detection
Â« CSV analysis and column detection

- Data type inference algorithm

Â« Table configuration preview screen

Â« Automatic column creation for all table types

Â« One-click table creation from CSV with all columns pre-configured

Phase 4: Enhanced Mapping
Â« Fuzzy matching for similar column names

Â« Suggestion system for common mappings

Â« Remember user's previous mapping choices

35. Acceptance Criteria
AC-1: Visual Indication of Unmapped Columns

Â« Unmapped columns are highlighted with red borders around the entire column card
Â« Column cards show "MAP TO ATTRIBUTE" dropdown in disabled/empty state
- Visual differentiation is clear and accessible (WCAG compliant)

- Red border provides immediate visual feedback without need for icons or tooltips

AC-2: Visual Validation and Next Button Control

- Unmapped columns are automatically highlighted with red borders
- "Next" button is disabled (not clickable) when unmapped columns exist
- An alert banner appears at the top: "X columns couldn't be mapped"
Â« Acheckbox option "Exclude unmapped columns" is displayed in the alert banner
Â« When user checks "Exclude unmapped columns":
o Unmapped columns are automatically unchecked/excluded
o "Next" button becomes enabled

- User cannot proceed without either mapping all columns or excluding unmapped ones

AC-3: Automatic Table Detection and Creation

- System analyzes uploaded CSV file (first 100 rows recommended)

- User can review and edit:

AC-5: Regular Table Creation Support

AC-6: Automatic Column Creation for All Table Types

- Columns include correct names and inferred data types

1. Purpose and Definition
Purpose:
To enable on-premise customers to configure their own Google Maps API Key through the

admin panel, eliminating the need for custom frontend builds and deployments for each

customer.

Current Behavior:

- Customer requests Geofence feature usage

- Customer provides Google Maps API Key

- Development team hardcodes the API Key into frontend code
- Separate frontend image is built and deployed X

- High operational overhead for each on-premise customer X<

Expected Behavior:

Admin users can configure Google Maps API Key via Settings > Integrations > 3rd Party

Integrations page

Google Maps integration card is visible ONLY if account has Geofence feature enabled

Card shows "Connect" button when not configured, "Connected" badge and "Disconnect"

button when configured

Clicking "Connect" or "Details" opens a modal with configuration form

For non-Geofence accounts or cloud deployments, Google Maps card should not be

visible in the list

API Key is stored securely in the database

Frontend dynamically loads Google Maps script using the configured key

No custom frontend build required for on-premise deployments

API Key can be updated without code changes or redeployment

## Page 1073

AC-01: Admin Panel Settings Page - Feature Visibility

Conditional Visibility: Google Maps API Key settings tab/section must be visible ONLY if
the account has Geofence feature enabled

System must check account's Geofence feature flag before rendering this settings section
For cloud/SaaS accounts or accounts without Geofence feature, this section must not
appear in Settings menu

For on-premise accounts with Geofence enabled, settings must appear as a tab under
Settings > Integrations

Settings page must have a dedicated "Integrations" or "Third-Party Services" section
Google Maps API Key configuration area must be visible only to users with admin role
Input field must support paste functionality and accept alphanumeric characters with
special characters (-, _)

API Key must be masked by default, showing only the last 4 characters (e.g.,
eecceceexy7123)

Show/Hide toggle button must reveal full API Key when clicked
Help text with link to Google Maps API documentation must be displayed

Save button must be disabled when no changes are made

AC-02: API Key Storage and Retrieval

API Key must be stored in database with encryption at rest

Backend must provide GET endpoint to retrieve API Key (masked for non-admin, full for
authorized requests)

Backend must provide PUT/POST endpoint to save/update API Key

API Key updates must be immediately available without application restart
Configuration must be account-specific (for multi-tenant systems) or global (for on-
premise)

API response time for fetching API Key must be under 500ms

AC-03: Dynamic Google Maps Script Loading

When Geofence page loads, frontend must fetch Google Maps API Key from backend

If API Key exists, Google Maps script must be injected dynamically into the page with the
key

Script loading must not block page rendering (async loading)

If script is already loaded with the same key, it must not be loaded again

Map component must initialize only after script loads successfully

No hardcoded API Key should exist in frontend code

AC-04: Missing or Invalid API Key Handling

If no API Key is configured, Geofence page must display a user-friendly error message

## Page 1074

Error message must state: "Google Maps API Key is not configured. Please contact your

administrator to enable Geofence features."

For admin users, error message must include a direct link to Settings page

Map container must show a placeholder UI (not a blank error page)

No JavaScript console errors related to missing API Key should occur

If API Key is invalid/expired, Google Maps error should be displayed (handled by Google)

System must remain functional; other features should not be affected

AC-05: Security, Access Control and Feature Gating

Feature Flag Check: System must verify Geofence feature is enabled for the account
before showing settings

If Geofence feature is disabled or not available, Google Maps API Key settings must not be
visible anywhere in the UI

Only users with admin role can view and modify Google Maps API Key settings (for
accounts with Geofence enabled)

Non-admin users must not see the Settings section or receive "Access Denied" error

API Key must be transmitted over HTTPS only

API Key must be encrypted in database storage

Backend API endpoints must validate both user permissions AND Geofence feature flag
before allowing access

Audit logging for API Key changes is recommended but not mandatory for MVP

AC-06: User Experience and Feedback

After saving API Key, a success notification must be displayed

Success message must state: "Google Maps API Key saved successfully. Changes are
effective immediately."

Save button must show loading state while saving (disabled with spinner)
If save fails, error notification must be displayed with retry option
Cancel button must discard changes and restore previous value

UI must be responsive and work on different screen sizes

AC-07: On-Premise Deployment Compatibility

Same frontend Docker image must work for all on-premise customers without modification
No customer-specific builds or environment variables should be required

Configuration must persist across application restarts and updates

Database migration scripts must be provided for new configuration table/fields
Deployment documentation must be updated with API Key configuration steps

Existing hardcoded solution (Kocgailem) must be migrated to dynamic solution

## Page 1075

AC-08: Backward Compatibility and Migration

- System must gracefully handle missing API Key during initial deployment

- No breaking changes to existing Geofence functionality or API contracts

- Migration script must be provided to move hardcoded key to database for existing
customers

- Feature must be tested in Tani (staging) environment with Kogailem before production

- Rollback plan must be documented in case of deployment issues

1. Purpose and Definition

Purpose:

To implement shortlink support for transactional SMS messages, ensuring consistency
between preview and actual delivery while enabling link click tracking for transactional SMS
campaigns. This will improve user experience, enable better analytics, and align transactional
SMS capabilities with bulk SMS features.

Current Behavior:

. Preview screen shows: https://short.1link/abce123 (shortlink)
- Actual SMS delivered:
https://example.com/very/long/product/url/path (original URL)

- No click tracking available for transactional SMS links
- Inconsistency causes user confusion about actual SMS content

- Transactional and bulk SMS use different tracking domains and methods
Expected Behavior:

. Preview screen shows shortlink: https://short.link/abc123

. Actual SMS delivered: https://short.link/abc123 (same shortlink)
- Shortlink redirects to original URL when clicked
- Click events are tracked and reported in analytics

- Consistent user experience between preview and delivery
Technical Context:

As per engineering team feedback: "Transactional SMS'lerde shortlink destegi mevcut
degildir. Destek olsa bile transactional ve bulk click tracking tamamen farkli domainler ve

metodiar uzerinden islenmektedir."
Implementation Methods (Based on SendTransactionalSms API):

Â¢ Payload 1 - Direct Content (use content):

## Page 1093

In-App Message: Clickable Image Support for Button Templates

Overview

Problem In button-enabled In-App
templates, images are NOT
clickable - only buttons have link
actions. In image-only templates,
images ARE clickable but buttons

Customer Misli

Request Link RP-683

1. Purpose and Definition

Purpose: Add an independent "Image URL" toggle at the bottom of the Call To Action
section that allows users to configure separate click actions for the image. When enabled,
users can set iOS and Android URLs for the image independently from button URLs. This
provides maximum flexibility - image and buttons can have different destinations, or users

can choose to keep image non-clickable.

## Page 1105

Current Behavior:

- Button-enabled templates : Image never clickable â‚¬ Only buttons trigger actions

- Image-only templates : Image is clickable (Y% But no buttons available

- Problem: Cannot have BOTH clickable image AND buttons in same template

Expected Behavior (NEW):

- "Image URL" toggle: Independent section below all button configurations

- When OFF (default): Image is NOT clickable, only buttons work
Â« When ON: iOS URL and Android URL fields appear for image
- Flexibility: Image can have DIFFERENT URL from buttons, or SAME URL, user decides

- Use Cases: (1) Image > Product page, Button > Add to cart; (2) Image > Article, Buttons

+ Share/Save; (3) Image and buttons > Same destination

- Analytics tracks click_source (image vs button) regardless of URL

- Supports all link types: Web URL, Deep Link, Custom Action

Business Context:

Misli is migrating from their backoffice system where images were clickable. By adding a

simple checkbox under each button configuration, we provide maximum control and

flexibility. This is a low-risk, high-value enhancement.

Overview

Problem The current "Preview & Test" tool
for transactional emails requires
users to manually write the

1. Purpose and Definition

Purpose:

## Page 1116

To enhance the "Preview & Test" functionality for transactional emails by implementing
automatic detection of dynamic variables used in templates and auto-generating the required
JSON structure with placeholder values. This eliminates manual JSON construction and
significantly improves testing efficiency.

Current Behavior:

- User clicks "Preview & Test" button

- Modal opens with instruction: "This template requires a Current Json for testing. Give an
example Json to be used in API call."

- User must manually type entire JSON structure from scratch

- User must remember all variable names used in template

- User must know proper nested structure (e.g., current.order.total)

- Time-consuming and prone to typos/errors K

Expected Behavior:

- User clicks "Preview & Test" button

- System automatically scans template for all dynamic variables

- System detects variables like: First_name, last_name, order_id,
order_total

- Modal opens with pre-populated JSON structure containing all detected variables

- JSON uses variable names as placeholder values (e.g., "first_name": "first_name")

- User can easily identify which field to edit and replace with actual test values

- Simple, predictable structure that user can quickly modify

Example Transformation:

Template contains:

Hello {{current.first_name}} {{current.last_name}}!
Order #{{current.order_id}}

Order Total: {{current.order_total}}
Delivery to: {{current.city}}

Auto-generated JSON:

"First_name": "first_name",
"last_name": "lLast_name",

"order_id": "order_id",

In Scope

1. User scrolls to "Ignore Frequency Capping" section

engagement experience. Users spin the reels to match 3 identical symbols and win prizes
(coupons, discounts, free shipping). Template works on both In-App and On-Site campaigns
and maintains consistency with existing Spin the Wheel infrastructure.

Competitive Advantage: Slot Machine missing from most competitors. Unique
differentiator opportunity.

Business Value: Spin the Wheel achieves 25-35% spin rate. Target similar for Slot. Braze
Snoonu: 39% order increase.

Legal Review Required: Gambling resemblance. Add disclaimers: "No purchase
necessary".

CRITICAL - No Prize Redistribution Logic: When Dynamic coupons deplete OR Static
win limit reached > probability goes to "No Prize" (NOT to other prizes). This prevents
users from getting alternate prizes they didn't actually win. Example: Prize A (30%)
depletes > No Prize increases from 25% to 55%.

Success Metrics (3 months): 30% adoption, 25-35% spin rate, +15% conversion, 3:1 ROI.

Observed Market Implementation:

- Two-stage popup approach: Game (tap challenge) + Reward Reveal (coupon code display)
- Typical setup: 20 taps in 10 seconds

- Limited social mechanics, single-use design

Dengage Coupon Integration:

- Coupon Type Selection: Generic (single code for all winners) vs Unique (one-time codes

displayed to all winners

- Unique Mode: Campaign owner uploads coupon list (CSV/Excel), system assigns unique
code per winner, tracks usage

- Coupon List Management: Upload/import interface, validation, remaining count display,
exhaustion handling

- Integration: Leverage existing Dengage coupon management system

Configurable Parameters:

- Tap Count: Adjustable (default: 20 taps, range: 5-100 taps) - enables brand customization
(Brand X: 11 taps, Brand Y: 41 taps)

- Time Limit: Adjustable (default: 10 seconds, range: 5-60 seconds)

1. Purpose and Definition

Purpose:

To provide real-time visibility into email HTML content size during the composition process,
preventing Gmail clipping issues and campaign send failures. The feature will display current
content size, warn users when approaching limits, and provide actionable recommendations

to reduce size before sending.

Current Behavior:

- User creates email content with no size visibility â‚¬

Â» Content exceeds 102 KB limit unknowingly

- Campaign send fails OR Gmail clips content (users see "[Message clipped] View entire
message") <

- Support tickets increase, customer satisfaction decreases

- No proactive prevention mechanism exists

Expected Behavior:

- Real-time content size indicator appears next to Spam Score in email editor

- Color-coded status: Green (safe), Yellow (warning 85-94 KB), Red (danger 95+ KB)
- Expandable details show size breakdown and recommendations

- Users can proactively reduce content before sending

- Campaign send failures due to size violations eliminated

Â« Gmail clipping incidents significantly reduced
Technical Context:

Gmail Clipping Threshold: 102 KB of HTML content (not including externally hosted images)
Industry Best Practice: Target 80 KB to account for ESP-added tracking parameters
Dengage Current Limit: 102 KB documented at 5-Platform Limits

5.Complete Tip Pool (All Possible Tips)

Category 1: Images (Image-related issues)

TIP-IMG-01: "Compress images"

- Priority: HIGH

- When to Show: When embedded images detected OR base64 images present
- Impact Calculation:

o High impact if: Number of <img> tags with data:image (base64) > 0

o Medium impact if: Number of <img> tags >5

- Display Text (Title): Compress images

- Display Text (Description): Use optimized formats (WebP, compressed JPEG) for
embedded images

- Badge Color: HIGH (Red: #fee2e2 / #99'1b1b)

TIP-IMG-02: "Reduce number of images"

- Priority: MEDIUM

- When to Show: When number of <img> tags > 10

- Impact Calculation:

o High impact if: Number of <img> tags > 15

o Medium impact if: Number of <img> tags > 10
- Display Text (Title): Reduce number of images

- Display Text (Description): Consider removing less important images or combining
multiple images
- Badge Color: MEDIUM (Orange: #fed7aa / #9a3412)

TIP-IMG-03: "Use CDN-hosted images instead of embedded"

- Priority: HIGH

- When to Show: When base64 encoded images detected

- Impact Calculation:
o High impact if: Number of base64 images > 2

- Display Text (Title): Use CDN-hosted images

- Display Text (Description): Replace embedded base64 images with CDN-hosted URLs to
drastically reduce size

- Badge Color: HIGH (Red: #fee2e2 / #991b1b)

Category 2: CSS/Styling (CSS-related issues)

TIP-CSS-01: "Remove inline styles"

## Page 1171

- Priority: HIGH
- When to Show: When inline Style=""' attributes detected frequently

Impact Calculation:

o High impact if: Number of inline style attributes > 50
o Medium impact if: Number of inline style attributes > 20
- Display Text (Title): Remove inline styles

- Display Text (Description): Extract repeated CSS to reduce redundancy and improve

email size
- Badge Color: HIGH (Red: #fee2e2 / #99'b1b)
TIP-CSS-02: "Simplify formatting"
- Priority: MEDIUM
- When to Show: When excessive <Span> or <font> tags with styles detected
- Impact Calculation:
o High impact if: Number of <SpPan> tags with style > 100
o Medium impact if: Number of <SPaNn> tags with style > 50
- Display Text (Title): Simplify formatting
- Display Text (Description): Remove unnecessary text formatting and use simpler styles
- Badge Color: MEDIUM (Orange: #fed7aa / #9a3412)
TIP-CSS-03: "Remove redundant CSS"
- Priority: MEDIUM
- When to Show: When <Style> tag size > 5 KB
- Impact Calculation:
o High impact if: <Style> tag content > 10 KB
o Medium impact if: <style> tag content > 5 KB
- Display Text (Title): Remove redundant CSS
- Display Text (Description): Consolidate and minify CSS rules in style blocks
- Badge Color: MEDIUM (Orange: #fed7aa / #9a3412)

Category 3: HTML Structure (Layout complexity issues)

TIP-HTML-01: "Simplify layout structureâ€

- When to Show: When nested <table> depth > 3 OR total HTML elements > 200

- Impact Calculation:

- Display Text (Title): Simplify layout structure
- Display Text (Description): Reduce nested tables and complex HTML structure

- Badge Color: MEDIUM (Orange: #fed7aa / #9a3412)

TIP-HTML-02: "Remove unnecessary HTML elements"

User Role "No Access" - Automatic Status Management

Overview

Problem

Prerequisites

1. Purpose and Definition

Purpose:

When a user's role is changed to
"No Access", the system does not
automatically update their status in
sys.account_user table to 'P'
(Passive). Similarly, when the role is
changed back to any other role
(Admin or custom roles), the
user_status is not automatically
reactivated to 'A' (Active). This
creates inconsistency where users
with "No Access" role remain active

in the system at the account level.

Internal - Subscription Management
/ User Management

Internal discussion with Product

team

N/A - Backend logic enhancement
(UI already exists)

[To be added]

Not required - Bug fix /

Enhancement

Understanding of subscription

management system

Â« User role assignment logic
(Admin, No Access, Custom
Roles)

Â« sys.account_user table structure
and user_status field

Â« Relationship between sys.user,

sys.account_user, and

sys.account tables

To automatically synchronize user status in sys.account_user table when their User Role is changed to or from "No

Access". This ensures that users without access permissions are properly marked as passive at the account level,

while users granted access are automatically activated.

Current Behavior:

## Page 1182

Â« Admin manually changes User Role to "No Access" in the user management modal

- User cannot login to the system (access is blocked)

- syS.account_user.user_status remains 'A' (Active) X

- Inconsistency: User has no functional access but appears active in account_user table

- When role is changed back to Admin or custom role, user_status must be manually updated

Expected Behavior:

- No Access Assignment: When User Role > "No Access", automatically set

sys.account_user.user_status = 'P' (&{

- Role Reactivation: When User Role > Any role other than "No Access", automatically set

sys.account_user.user_status = 'A' {J

- Account-Level Isolation: Same user can be 'P' in one account and 'A' in another account (multi-account support)

- Manual Changes Only: This logic applies only to manual role changes via user management UI, not to automatic

subscription system changes

Why sys.account_user Table?

A single user can exist in multiple accounts with different roles and statuses. For example, user@example.com might

have Admin access in Account A but No Access in Account B. Therefore, user_status must be managed at the

account_user level, not the global user level.

Assignment

Manual Role Changes

Multi-Account Support

4. Design

Backend Implementation Approach:

- Trigger Point: User role update endpoint/service (when admin saves role change)

- Logic Flow:
a. Detect role change in request

b. Check if new_role = "No Access" > Set user_status = 'P' in sys.account_user
c. Check if old_role = "No Access" AND new_role # "No Access" > Set user_status = 'A' in sys.account_user
d. Otherwise > No status change
e. Log audit entry if status was modified
- Database Updates: Single transaction to update both role and status atomically

- Error Handling: If status update fails, rollback entire role change

UI Considerations:

- No UI changes required - existing user management modal is sufficient

- Consider adding informational tooltip: "Users with 'No Access' role will be automatically set to Passive status"

1. Purpose and Definition

Purpose:

Add channel-specific sender filtering to Send Reports page, enabling customers to filter
email sends by sender profile, SMS sends by sender name, and WhatsApp sends by
configuration. This will support domain warmup tracking and sender-specific performance

analysis.

Current Behavior:

- Email Send Reports: Filterable by Email channel and "All Content" - no sender profile filter
- SMS Send Reports: Filterable by SMS channel and "All Content" - no sender name filter
- WhatsApp Send Reports: Filterable by WhatsApp channel and "All Partners" - no

configuration filter
- Customer Impact: CG cannot track individual sender profile performance during warmup

phase

Expected Behavior:

Â« Email: Add "Sender Profile" dropdown filter showing all sender profiles used by the
account

- SMS: Add "Sender Name" dropdown filter showing all sender names used by the account

- WhatsApp: Add "Configuration" dropdown filter showing all WhatsApp configurations

- Filters display available options from actual send data

- Selecting a filter updates the Send Reports metrics (Total Sent, Delivered, Open, Click,
Bounced, Error)

- Graph visualization updates to show filtered data
Business Context:

CG uses 10 different sender profiles for email sends and is in domain warmup phase. They
need to track each profile's performance separately to ensure successful warmup. Current
UI only shows aggregated metrics across all sender profiles, making profile-specific

monitoring impossible.

Customer Impact: Critical for CG (Condor Gaming) - currently blocking their domain
warmup tracking. Impacts all customers using multiple sender configurations.

Business Value: Enables proper domain warmup monitoring, improves sender-specific
performance analysis, increases customer satisfaction.

Cost of Not Doing: Risk of losing CG customer. Continued support burden for domain
warmup tracking requests.

Implementation Approach: Simple dropdown addition leveraging existing Send Reports
infrastructure - low technical risk.

Estimated Effort: 15 story points total (2-3 weeks with one backend + one frontend
developer).

Rollout Strategy: Can be rolled out immediately to all customers as it's additive
functionality with "All" default option.

Future Enhancements: (1) Add same filtering to Send Logs (Event Details) page, (2) Export

functionality, (3) Additional filter parameters (group_id, transaction_id).

Â¥& Technical Considerations

Database Schema: Verify that sender_profile (Email), sender_name (SMS), configuration
(WhatsApp) columns exist and are indexed in send_reports tables.

Query Performance: Existing Send Reports queries should handle additional WHERE
clause without significant performance impact.

Filter Options API: New endpoint needed to fetch distinct sender
profiles/names/configurations for date range - should be cached for performance.

UI Component Reuse: Leverage existing dropdown component pattern used for Channel
and Content filters.

API Backwards Compatibility: New filter parameters are optional - existing API
consumers unaffected.

Data Accuracy: Ensure sender metadata is consistently captured during send process to

populate filter options accurately.

1. Purpose and Definition

Purpose:

Implement proactive warning messages on the login page that inform users when they are
approaching the account lock threshold (5 failed attempts). Display countdown warnings
after the 2nd failed attempt, giving users the opportunity to reset their password before being
locked out.

Current Behavior:
- Attempt 1-4: Generic error message "Incorrect username or password" - no indication of
remaining attempts

- Attempt 5: Account is immediately locked and user sees "User account locked. Please

contact account manager to unlock"
- User Impact: No opportunity to self-recover by resetting password before lockout occurs

- Admin Burden: Increased support tickets for account unlocking requests

Expected Behavior:

- Attempt 1: Generic error "Incorrect username or password"

- Attempt 2: Generic error "Incorrect username or password"

Attempt 3: Warning message "You have 2 attempts remaining before your account is

locked. Consider resetting your password."

Attempt 4: Critical warning "You have 1 attempt remaining before your account is locked.

We recommend resetting your password now."

Attempt 5: Account locked - "User account locked. Please contact account manager to

unlock"

- "Forgot Password?â€ Link: Emphasized in warning messages to guide users to password

reset flow
@ Why Start Warnings at Attempt 3?

Starting warnings at attempt 3 (showing "2 attempts remaining") balances security with user

experience. It prevents alert fatigue from too-early warnings while giving users sufficient

## Page 1202

opportunity to course-correct. Users who make 1-2 typos won't be alarmed, but those with

genuine password issues get meaningful warnings.

Business Benefits

Â« Reduced admin workload for account unlocking requests

- Improved user satisfaction through proactive guidance

- Maintains security while enhancing usability

- Encourages password reset self-service before lockout

- Aligns with industry standard practices (AWS, Azure, Google, etc.)

4. Design

UI/UX Design Requirements:

Visual Hierarchy & Message States:

- Attempt 1-2: Standard red error box with text "Incorrect username or password" (existing
design)

- Attempt 3: Yellow/amber warning box with A\ icon and countdown text "2 attempts
remaining"

- Attempt 4: Red critical warning box with & icon and countdown text "1 attempt
remaining"

- Attempt 5: Red error box with lock icon @ and account locked message (existing design)

Message Placement & Layout:

- Display warning message below password field and above "Login" button
- Replace generic error with warning message (don't show both simultaneously)
- Ensure sufficient vertical spacing to prevent visual clutter

- Maintain consistent message box width matching login form width

Interactive Elements:

- "reset your password" / "resetting your password now" should be styled as inline hyperlink
(blue, underlined)

- Link hover state should provide clear affordance (darker blue, cursor pointer)

Â« Link click should navigate to Forgot Password page or open modal

- Consider also visually emphasizing the existing "Forgot Password?" link in the UI during
warning states

Mobile Responsiveness:

- Warning messages must wrap appropriately on mobile viewports

- Font size remains readable (minimum 14px on mobile)

- Touch targets for links meet minimum 44x44px accessibility guidelines

## Page 1208

- Icons scale appropriately for mobile displays

Accessibility Considerations:

- Warning messages use appropriate ARIA labels (role="alert")
- Color contrast meets WCAG AA standards for both warning states
- Screen readers announce warning severity and attempt count

- Keyboard navigation works seamlessly with password reset links

Backend Design Requirements:
- API Response Enhancement: Modify login authentication endpoint to return
failed_login_attempts count in error response body

- Response Format Example: Backend should return a JSON response including the failed

attempt count

- Counter Logic: Ensure failed_login_attempts counter increments only on password

mismatch (not on non-existent username)
- Counter Reset: Reset failed_login_attempts to O on successful authentication
- Database Field: Verify failed_login_attempts column exists in user/authentication table

- Security: Ensure failed attempt count is user-specific and session-independent

Design mockups showing warning states at different attempt levels will be created by
Product Design team. Backend implementation should follow existing authentication patterns

with minimal disruption.

Additional Notes

Priority: Medium-High - Improves UX and reduces support burden for account unlocking
Customer Impact: All Dengage platform users across all accounts

Business Value: Reduces admin workload for unlocking accounts, improves user
satisfaction, encourages self-service password resets

Estimated Effort: 16 story points total (approximately 2 weeks with backend + frontend
collaboration)

Target Teams: Backend team (API modifications), Frontend team (UI/UX implementation),
QA team (comprehensive testing)

Dependencies: None - independent enhancement to existing authentication flow

Rollout Plan: Can be deployed immediately to production; backward compatible (adds
information, doesn't break existing behavior)

Industry Standards: Aligns with best practices used by major platforms (AWS, Azure,
Google Cloud, Salesforce) for progressive account security warnings

Future Enhancements: (1) CAPTCHA challenge before final attempt, (2) Time-based
automatic unlock after X minutes, (3) Email notification on account lock, (4) Admin

dashboard to view locked accounts and unlock remotely

J& Technical Considerations

Database Schema: Verify failed_login_attempts column exists in user/account table. If not,
add migration to create this column (INT, default 0).

Counter Increment Logic: Counter should ONLY increment on password mismatch for
valid users, not on non-existent username attempts (prevents username enumeration
attacks).

API Performance: Adding failed_login_attempts to response has negligible performance
impact (single integer field). No database query overhead as value is already retrieved

during authentication.

## Page 1214

Frontend State Management: Warning display logic should be simple conditional

rendering based on failed_login_attempts value from API response. No complex state
management required.

Backwards Compatibility: New API response field is additive - existing authentication

clients unaffected. Frontend can gracefully handle absence of field (default to old

behavior).

Security Considerations: Ensure failed attempt counter is properly isolated per user and
cannot be manipulated via API calls. Counter must be server-side only, never client-side.

Rate Limiting: Consider if additional rate limiting is needed beyond 5-attempt lock. Current

implementation relies solely on failed attempt counter, which may be sufficient for most
use cases.
- Internationalization (i18n): Warning messages should support localization. Use translation

keys for all user-facing text.

Implement an automated notification system that sends summary report emails to

designated users when one-time campaigns are published and when their sends complete.

Additionally, send daily summary emails for recurring campaigns showing aggregated

metrics from the previous 24 hours. This provides internal teams with real-time visibility into

campaign operations and performance metrics without manual monitoring.

Current Behavior:

- No automated notifications when campaigns are created/published

- No automated notifications when campaign sends complete

- No daily summary emails for recurring campaigns

- Teams must manually check platform to monitor campaign status

- No summary reports available via email

Expected Behavior:

- One-Time Campaigns - Notification 1 (Campaign Published):

o Sent immediately when flow is published

o Contains: Flow name, segment, communication types & count, creator, approver

o Email subject: "Campaign Published: [Flow Name]"

## Page 1230

- One-Time Campaigns - Notification 2 (Send Completed):

o Sent when all communications in flow complete

o Contains: All published info + targeted/delivered counts per communication

o Email subject: "Send Completed: [Flow Name]"

- Recurring Campaigns - Notification 3 (Daily Summary) [&%:

o Sent once per day at 08:00 AM (next morning, local time)

o Contains: Table of all recurring campaigns sent in previous 24 hours (yesterday)

o For each campaign: name, segment, communication types, execution count, total

targeted/delivered users

o Summary section: total campaigns, total executions, total users targeted/delivered

o Email subject: "Daily Campaign Summary - [Yesterday's Date]"

Business Context:

Beymen previously used another platform that provided "Campaign Send Summary Reports"

functionality. This feature enabled their teams to stay informed about campaign operations

without constantly monitoring the platform. They expect similar functionality in Dengage to

maintain operational visibility and team coordination. The daily recurring summary is

particularly important as recurring campaigns can send multiple times per day, making

individual notifications overwhelming and impractical. Sending the summary at 08:00 AM

(next morning) allows teams to review yesterday's campaign performance at the start of their

workday.

1. Purpose and Definition

Purpose:

Display the Super Admin contact email (with privacy masking) in the login screen warning
message when a user account is pending approval. This enables users to directly contact the

responsible Super Admin instead of contacting Dengage support, reducing support load and
accelerating user onboarding.

Current Behavior:

- Login Attempt: User enters credentials
- Warning Message: You cannot log in without your admin approving first
- User Confusion: User does not Know which admin to contact for approval

- Support Impact: Users contact Dengage support thinking Dengage needs to approve
them

- Delayed Onboarding: Support team redirects users to their Super Admin, adding
unnecessary steps

Expected Behavior:

- Enhanced Warning Message: Display Super Admin masked email in the warning

- Example: You cannot log in without your admin approving first. Please contact your Super
Admin at opa***************@ defans.com.tr for approval.

- Email Masking Format:

o Show first 5 characters of email username

o Replace remaining characters before @ with asterisks

o Show @ symbol and full domain

o Example: opasimsankara@defans.com.tr becomes opa*************** @ defans.com.tr
- User Action: Users directly contact their Super Admin for approval

- Support Reduction: Fewer unnecessary support tickets

Privacy and Data Protection:

Email masking ensures KVKK (Turkish Data Protection Law) and GDPR compliance by limiting
personal data exposure. Users can recognize their Super Admin from the first 5 characters
and domain, while full email remains protected.

Overview

Problem Current Engagement Split node only checks
engagement from the immediately preceding

sent simultaneously) or want to track

in a flow, they cannot evaluate combined

prevents customers from implementing
sophisticated engagement-based routing
logic such as "engaged with either Email OR
Push" or "engaged with all previous

communications."

1. Purpose and Definition

Purpose:

Enhance the Engagement Split node to support multi-channel engagement evaluation,
allowing users to check engagement across multiple previous send nodes with flexible
selection of specific sends, event types, and logical operators (OR/AND). This enables

sophisticated routing based on combined engagement behavior across different
communication channels.

Current Behavior:

- Single Send Limitation: Engagement Split only checks the immediately preceding send
node

- Example Scenario: Flow has Email Send > Push Send > Engagement Split

- Current Issue: Engagement Split ONLY checks Push Send engagement, cannot evaluate
Email Send engagement

- Customer Impact: Cannot track "engaged with Email OR Push" or "engaged with both
Email AND Push"

- Workaround: Customers must create multiple separate flows or use complex Decision
Split nodes with custom SQL queries

Expected Behavior (New Feature):

- "Add Content" Button: User clicks to select which previous sends to evaluate

Multi-Send Selection: Modal displays all previous send nodes in chronological order with
channel icons (De Email, 24 Push, 6) SMS, +f InApp, & Onsite)

Flexible Selection: User can select/deselect any combination of previous sends via

checkboxes

Exclude Option: User can explicitly exclude certain sends from evaluation if needed

Event Type Selection: For each selected send, user chooses ONE specific engagement
event type:

o Email: Delivery / Open / Click

o Push: Delivery / Click

o SMS: Delivery / Click

o InApp: Display / Dismiss / Click
o Onsite: Display / Dismiss / Click

## Page 1250

- Logic Operator: User selects OR logic ("engaged in ANY selected send") or AND logic

("engaged in ALL selected sends")

Business Context:

This enhancement supports modern omnichannel marketing strategies where customers

send coordinated campaigns across multiple channels. For example, a product launch might

include simultaneous Email + Push notifications, and the customer wants to route users who

engaged with EITHER channel to a follow-up nurture flow while routing non-engaged users

to a re-engagement campaign.

4. Design
UI/UX Design Requirements:

- Engagement Split Node Settings: Add "Add Content" button in node settings modal

- Modal Trigger: Clicking "Add Content" opens new modal overlay displaying send node
selection interface

- Modal Header: Title "Engagement Split" with subtitle "Configure how to evaluate user
engagement across channels"

- Source Selection (Optional for future): Three radio options:
o "Last Send Only" (current behavior, marked as "Current")
o "Specific Sends" (new functionality, marked as "New")
o "All Previous Sends" (new functionality, marked as "New")

- Send Node List: Unified vertical list showing all previous send nodes with:

## Page 1258

o Checkbox for selection
0 40x40px channel icon with colored background (5&J Email blue, Â£4 Push light blue, Â¢-)
SMS pink, *f InApp yellow, â‚¬ Onsite teal)
o Send name (bold, 14px)
o Metadata line (campaign, template info, 12px gray)
o Position badge (#1, #2, etc., right-aligned)
- Event Selection Section: Below each send when selected:
o Horizontal row of radio button cards
o Each card shows event icon (7, Â®, ~, 6) and label
o Cards have hover and selected states
o Only ONE event selectable per send (radio button behavior)
- Selection Summary: "Selected sends: X of Y" counter at top of list
- Logic Selector: Yellow background section with two radio card options:
o "OR Logic" - Engaged in ANY selected send
o "AND Logic" - Engaged in ALL selected sends
- Live Example Box: Green background box showing current configuration in plain English
- Modal Footer: Cancel button (white/gray) and OK button (blue primary)
- Responsive Design: Modal should be scrollable if send list is long (max-height with

overflow-y: auto)

Backend Design Requirements:

- Node Configuration Storage: Store selected send node IDs, event types, and logic
operator in Engagement Split node configuration JSON

- Flow Parser: Identify all send nodes that appear before Engagement Split node in flow
graph

- Engagement Data Query: Query engagement events for specified send nodes and event
types from engagement tracking tables

- Logic Evaluation Engine: Implement OR logic (ANY match) and AND logic (ALL match)
evaluation for engagement conditions

- API Response Structure: Return list of previous send nodes with metadata (channel type,
name, campaign info, position)

- Execution Performance: Optimize engagement queries to prevent flow execution delays
(use indexed queries, consider caching)

- Migration Strategy: Existing nodes without multi-send configuration continue to use "last

send only" behavior (default fallback)

1. Purpose and Definition
Purpose:
Enhance GetInAppLogs API to include eventAttr field (button_id identifier) for click events, matching the existing

functionality in GetRealtimeInAppLogs API. This enables customers to identify which specific button_id each contact
clicked and integrate real-time with call center/CRM systems for immediate follow-up actions.

Current Behavior:
. GetInAppLogs API: GET /rest/logs/inapp - Returns InApp event logs but does NOT include eventAttr
field for button tracking

GetRealtimeInAppLogs API: GET /rest/logs/realtime/inapp - ALREADY includes eventattr field
with button_id identifier
- Event Types: OP (Open), DP (Displayed), DS (Dismissed), CL (Clicked), ER (Error) events are logged

Contact Tracking: APIs return ContactKey field when user is logged in, otherwise null

- Device Tracking: APIs always return deviceld field for both logged-in and anonymous users

Inconsistency Issue: GetRealtimeInAppLogs has eventAttr, but GetInAppLogs does NOT - causing integration
complexity

SDK Support: Mobile SDKs provide button_id identifier (primary_button, secondary_button, tertiary_button)

- Business Impact: Customer cannot use GetInAppLogs for button tracking - must use GetRealtimeInAppLogs
only

- Workaround Limitations: sys table SQL queries + segment export + scheduled flows are not real-time (5-10
minute delays)

Expected Behavior:

- API Consistency: GetInAppLogs enhanced to include eventAtttr field for CL events, matching
GetRealtimeInAppLogs behavior

eventAttr Field: Contains button_id identifier (primary_button, secondary_button, tertiary_button)

- Real-Time Integration: With eventAttr + contactKey/devicelId, both APIs enable immediate call center system
integration
- Backwards Compatibility: Existing API consumers unaffected - eventAttr field added without breaking changes

- Standardization: Both APIs now return consistent button tracking data structure
Business Context - Credit Application Use Case:

Customer displays InApp message: "Would you like to apply for our new credit card offer?"
Buttons: [Yes] [No] [Maybe Later]

Current Problem: GetInAppLogs returns all InApp events but CL events don't include eventAttr field.
GetRealtimeInAppLogs has eventAttr but lacks some filtering capabilities. Customer needs consistent button
tracking across both APIs.

Desired Outcome: GetInAppLogs enhanced to return eventAttr field
(primary_button/secondary_button/tertiary_button) in CL events, matching GetRealtimeInAppLogs functionality.
Customer can use either API with consistent data structure.

Technical Note: eventAttr contains button_id identifier. Customer must maintain button_id mapping in their system
to know which position corresponds to which intent (Yes/No/Maybe).

retargeting.

cannot be met.

parameters (sendId, contactKey, eventType) to reduce data transfer, (3) Bulk export functionality for data

warehouse integration.

- Priority: High - Reduces support tickets, improves UX, enables self-service help

Target Teams: Backend (2), Frontend (2), QA (1), Product/Design (1)

license

- Business Value: 30-40% reduction in support tickets, faster user onboarding, better feature adoption, competitive

differentiation
- Rollout Plan: Phase 1 (Core pages: 20 pages), Phase 2 (All pages: 79 pages), Phase 3 (Optimization based on user
feedback)

time-intensive (79 pages x 30 min = 40 hours)

Mitigation: Bulk import from Excel (already created with 79 pages content), iframe loading optimization, content

review process before production

- Lazy loading for iframe to improve initial load

- Error boundaries for graceful degradation

- Accessibility: ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, focus management

Backend:

- PostgreSQL JSONB for warnings arrays (flexible, indexed)
- Soft delete pattern (is_active flag) for data retention

## Page 1287

App Inbox - Action Buttons & Campaign Tag Filtering Enhancement

Overview

Problem

Multiple enterprise customers (Knet,

lyzico, N11) cannot effectively utilize

App Inbox due to missing critical

features:

Action Buttons Not Returned:
When push notifications with
action buttons are saved to App
Inbox, the SDK's
getInboxMessages
function response does not
include action button data (button
text, button action URLs). This
prevents customers from
rendering interactive buttons in
their App Inbox UI, forcing users
to click the entire notification
instead of specific action buttons.

. No Category-Based Filtering:

Customers using App Inbox for
multiple notification types
(transactional, campaigns,
coupons, order updates) cannot
filter or categorize inbox
messages. The SDK returns
messages without
campaign_tags, making it
impossible for customers to
implement category-based
filtering in their apps. lyzico and
N11 both want to categorize
notifications by type (e.g.,
Campaigns/Transactional/General
for lyzico,
Coupons/Campaigns/Orders/Acc
ount for N11).

. Record Limit in SDK: The

getInboxMessages
function has a maximum record
limit, preventing customers from
accessing their complete inbox
history for filtering and

pagination.

Implementation Approach: Additive API enhancement with backwards compatibility - existing integrations
unaffected

o Phase 2: iOS SDK update + Documentation
o Phase 3: Android SDK update + Documentation

1. Purpose and Definition
Purpose:

Add a "Contact Delete" node to Automated Flow that enables controlled bulk deletion of
contacts from master_contact table. This node will be restricted to Dengage email domain

users only and will require dual approval before execution to ensure data safety.

Current Behavior:

Â« API Limitation: Only single contact deletion available via API - no bulk deletion capability

- DB Team Dependency: Customers request bulk deletion from DB team, creating

operational overhead
- Risk Factor: Manual DB operations are risky and error-prone
- Time Consuming: Both Support and DB teams spend significant time on deletion requests

- No Self-Service: Customers cannot manage their own contact cleanup operations

Expected Behavior:

- New Node: "Contact Delete" node added to Automated Flow canvas

- Access Control: Only users with @dengage.com email domain can see and use this node
- Selection Options: Radio button to choose between Segment or Table source

- Two-Step Configuration: Page 1 (radio selection) > Page 2 (segment/table dropdown)

- Approval Required: Second Dengage user must approve before flow can be activated

- Scheduled Execution: Flow runs on schedule, deleting ALL contacts in selected

segment/table each time
- Deletion Tracking: Node displays count of deleted contacts after execution

- Error Handling: Flow fails if deletion operation encounters errors

[] Additional Notes

Business Impact: Eliminates operational overhead for Support and DB teams. Reduces
risk of manual DB operations. Enables self-service contact cleanup for billing optimization
and contact_key management.

Security Priority: Dual approval + email domain restriction ensures controlled access to
destructive operations.

Customer Value: Particularly valuable during onboarding when incorrect contact_key
used, or when customers need to manage contact_key changes.

Risk Mitigation: Approval workflow prevents accidental deletions. Audit logging provides

complete traceability. Transaction-based deletion ensures data consistency.

Estimated Effort: 33 story points total (~4-5 weeks with backend + frontend + QA

resources).
Implementation Priority: High - addresses operational pain point for both internal teams

and customers.

Rollout Strategy: Gradual rollout to @dengage.com users only. Monitor for 2 weeks before

considering customer-facing expansion (if needed).

Future Considerations:

o Potential expansion to allow selective deletion filters (date range, custom criteria)
o Scheduled deletion reports sent to admins

o Backup/restore mechanism for accidentally deleted contacts

Â¥& Technical Considerations

Database Performance: Bulk deletion of large contact sets should use batched operations
to avoid table locking. Consider DELETE in chunks of 10,000 contacts with commit

between batches.

## Page 1319

Transaction Management: Wrap entire deletion operation in database transaction.
Rollback on any error to maintain data consistency.

Cascade Rules: Verify master_contact table foreign key constraints. Ensure related tables
(events, send_history) handle deletion appropriately (CASCADE or restrict deletion if
references exist).

Email Domain Check: Token already contains email - extract and validate against
@dengage.com pattern. Cache validation result per session to avoid repeated checks.
Approval System Architecture:

o New flow_approvals table with indexes on flow_id and approval_status

o API endpoints: POST /flows/approval-request, POST /flows/approve, POST /flows/reject
o Validation: prevent self-approval, ensure approver has @dengage.com domain
Execution Monitoring: Leverage existing flow job status system. Extend to show deletion
progress and final contact count.

Audit Trail: Create deletion_audit_log table with: flow_execution_id, node_id, user_email,
segment/table_name, contact_count, execution_timestamp, success/failure,
error_message.

Error Recovery: No automatic retry on failure. Require manual intervention to prevent

unintended repeated deletions.

1. Purpose and Definition
Purpose:

Redesign the Homepage (Home) to provide a comprehensive, data-rich dashboard experience. The layout consists
of predefined sections (widgets) that are common across all users, but each user can reorder these sections via drag
& drop. The reordered layout must be automatically persisted per user without any explicit save action. This

approach ensures every user sees the same set of data sections but can prioritize what matters most to them.

Current Behavior:

- Homepage shows a basic dashboard with limited data sections
- Layout is static and identical for all users â€” no personalization
- Missing key sections: Communication Highlights, Campaign Performance Trends, System Status Overview

Â« No drag & drop or reordering capability

Expected Behavior:

- New Layout: Homepage displays all sections from the Figma design (Campaign Status, Campaigns, Audience
Reachability, Engagement, Communication Highlights, Campaign Performance Trends & Activities, System Status
Overview)

Default Order: All users see the default section order defined in the Figma design on first visit

Drag & Drop Reordering: Users can drag sections to rearrange their order

Auto-Save: When a user reorders sections, the new order is automatically saved (no Save button). On next visit,

the user sees their custom order

Per-User Persistence: Each user's layout preference is stored independently

Consistent Content: All users see the same sections â€” only the order changes. Sections cannot be hidden or

removed
Key Design Decision: Auto-Save Without Save Button

When a user drags and drops a section to a new position, the system must immediately persist the new order to the
backend. There is no "Save Layout" button. This means the frontend must call a save/update API after every drag &
drop action. Debouncing should be implemented to avoid excessive API calls if the user is rapidly rearranging

multiple sections.

4. Design

UI/UX Design Details:

- Drag Handle: Each draggable section should have a visible (or on-hover) drag handle icon (grip dots / :!) at the

top-left or top-center of the section header. This communicates to the user that the section is draggable.

- Drag Feedback: When dragging, the section should show a semi-transparent ghost. The target drop zone should

show a highlighted line or placeholder area.

Â« Section Cards: Each section behaves like a card/widget. Internal content (tabs, charts, tables) functions

independently within the section.

- No Save Button: There is explicitly NO save button for layout changes. The save happens automatically.

Save Indicator: A brief, non-intrusive indicator (e.g., small checkmark animation near the drag handle, or a
transient toast "Layout saved") appears after successful save.

Responsive: On desktop, drag & drop is fully functional. On mobile/tablet, sections display in saved order but drag
& drop interaction is disabled for this phase.

Loading States: Each section should display a skeleton loader independently while its data is being fetched.

## Page 1335

- Error States: If a section's API fails, that specific section shows an error state with a retry option. Other sections

are not affected.

(Refer to the attached Figma design for visual specifications, spacing, colors, and component details.)

4% Technical Considerations
. Drag & Drop Library: Evaluate react-beautiful-dnd , @dnd-kit , or native HTML5 Drag & Drop API.
@dnd-kit is recommended for modern React apps due to better performance and accessibility.

- Debounce Strategy: Use 500ms-1000ms debounce on the save API call after drag & drop events. Store pending
order in local state and flush to API after debounce window.

- localStorage Fallback: Optionally cache the layout order in localStorage as a fallback for failed API saves. On
page load: API preference > localStorage > default order.

- Section Identifiers: Use stable string IDs (e.g., â€œcampaign_status_bar", "engagement") rather than numeric
indices to avoid issues with future section additions.

## Page 1343

- Independent Data Fetching: Each section should fetch its data independently using separate API calls. Use
React Query or SWR for caching, refetching, and error handling per section.

- Skeleton Loaders: Each section should have a tailored skeleton matching its layout (card skeleton for Campaigns,
chart skeleton for Trends, table skeleton for Engagement).

- Accessibility: Drag & drop must support keyboard navigation (arrow keys to move sections, Enter to confirm).
Screen reader announcements for reorder actions.

| Segment Limitation Audience - Segments - Interactive Segment - Create New Segment A new feature will be added to the segment creation screen that allows users to define limits specific to each segment group. When the user clicks on the limit icon, a modal will open, allowing them to set a limit for the selected segment group. During this process, the number of people in the segment group will not be calculated. For example, if a segment group contains 80 people but a limit of 100 is defined, the process will proceed without any restrictions. In larger segment groups that include multiple segment groups, the limitation will be applied based on the defined limit of the largest segment group. | Sending geofence to segment In geofence targeting, the goal is to send notifications to a specific audience when creating a campaign. This development aims to allow targeted push notifications to individuals entering an event area, such as inviting only selected people to showroom events for clients like Borusan. As a result, only designated contacts or devices will receive notifications in specific events or locations. Business Requirements Adding a Segment Selection Screen A segment selection section should be added to the campaign creation screen specifically for geofence targeting. When launching a geofence push campaign, users should be able to select their target audience. Audience Definition via Segments The geofence push campaign audience should be restricted based on a predefined segment. For example, push notifications should only be sent to contacts within segments like "Attendees from Borusan" or "Participants from Dengage." Segment Integration into Campaign Flow Users should be able to select the target segments for geofence push notifications within the campaign flow. The segment selection screen should allow choosing from previously created and saved segments. Alignment of Geofence Criteria with Segments Geofence targeting criteria should be aligned with segment criteria. For instance, if a segment is created for invited event attendees, the segment should only be active when individuals enter the geofence area. Workflow 1. Segment Selection: Users select the target audience from the segment selection screen during campaign creation. 2. Geofence Area Definition: A geofence area is assigned to the selected segment, and notifications are triggered only when individuals enter this area. |

| Language Support for Onsite Template Content anguage support has been added to onsite content. When the "Add Language" option is clicked on an empty content screen, the user is presented with two options: Copy From Content: Copies the filled fields from the existing content to the new language. Create Blank Onsite Content: Creates entirely blank content of the same type. The language addition option is displayed only if no language has been added yet. If multiple languages already exist in the content, a new language can be added using the "+" button in the language list. Language Addition and Management Process When the user clicks the "Add Language" option, a modal appears. This modal lists the languages added in Settings â†’ Content Language. The user selects the desired language and fills in the content. If the required language is not listed, the user must activate it from Settings â†’ Content Language. The user can edit the content of added languages and deactivate them if necessary. Mandatory Fields and Save Process To save the content as "Save Draft" or "Publish", all required fields must be filled in for each language. A default language can be set in Settings â†’ Content Language. Newly created content starts with the designated default language. The user can change the default language in the language addition modal but cannot remove it completely. Therefore, the checkbox next to the default language in the modal appears as disabled. Copy From Content Option If the "Copy From Content" option is selected: The filled fields from the existing content are copied to the new language. The user can edit and modify the copied content. |

Each language card includes an AI translation icon, allowing users to trigger translation manually. Use Cases and System Behaviors: 1. When "Copy from Content" is selected: The content from the default language is used as the reference. If the AI option is selected: All selected languages are automatically translated using AI. | Push Inbox - Delete and Mark All Notifications as Read Functionality Dengage Push Inbox - Delete and Mark All Notifications as Read Functionality Analysis 1. Purpose The goal is to add bulk delete and mark-as-read functionalities to the Push Inbox feature in Dengage. With this enhancement, users will be able to delete all notifications at once or mark them as read in their inbox. 2. Scope The backend team will develop two new endpoints: Delete All Notifications Endpoint Mark All Notifications as Read Endpoint These endpoint details will be provided to the SDK team for integration. The frontend will include UI components to enable users to utilize these functions. 3. Technical Details Backend Development: Requests will be processed on a per-user basis. The delete operation will be permanent and irreversible. The mark-as-read operation will update all unread notifications of the user to "read" status. SDK Integration: The SDK team will receive endpoint details and required parameters. The SDK will use these endpoints to support delete and mark-as-read operations. 4. User Scenarios The user presses the "Delete All" button in the Push Inbox screen, the system sends a request to the backend, and all notifications are deleted. The user presses the "Mark All as Read" button, a request is sent to the backend, and all notifications are marked as read. 5. Test Scenarios Verify that all notifications are successfully deleted. Verify that all notifications are successfully marked as read. Test user authorization controls. Check data synchronization in multi-device scenarios. |
| --- |
|  |


|  |
| --- |

| Superset Analytics Authorization Rules This document defines the authorization structure and access control rules for users of the Superset Analytics product within the Dengage platform. Authorization Model Overview All built-in dashboards, charts, and datasets will be automatically created and managed by a Dengage Admin account. These assets will be owned by the Dengage Admin account. Authorization is enforced based on ownership. Users cannot edit objects they do not own. Customer User Access Rules Roles Write Permission Read Permission Restrictions Customer users, even with write permissions, cannot edit the dashboards, charts, or datasets owned by the Dengage Admin. These built-in assets will be read-only to all non-owner accounts. Users can only duplicate dashboards or charts using the â€œSave Asâ€ feature to create their own copies. SQL Lab Access Users with write access will have access to SQL Lab, enabling them to create virtual datasets from queries. However, their access will be restricted to specific tables only. They will not have access to the full schema. Custom Metrics & Calculations If a user wants to create and save a new metric at dataset level, they must submit a request to Dengage. Users can perform temporary calculations within chart visualizations. These calculations cannot be saved globally or reused across multiple charts. Feature / Action Dengage Admin Customer (Write Customer (Read Permission) Permission) |
