| AppsFlyer Integration This document outlines the proposed one-way integration between AppsFlyer and Dengage to ingest attribution metadata such as media_source , campaign , af_channel , and install_time into Dengage contact profiles. The goal is to enable customers to create meaningful segments and launch personalized campaigns based on user acquisition data. This integration is possible to support two models: 1. Pull-based integration (via scheduled backend API calls) 2. Push-based integration (pending AppsFlyer partner status) Customers want to leverage mobile attribution data to: Identify which ad network or campaign brought in each user Create dynamic segments (e.g., "Facebook-acquired users") Run targeted push/in-app/SMS campaigns Personalize journey flows based on acquisition source Integration Scenarios 1. Pull-Based Integration Dengage will retrieve attribution data from AppsFlyer using the Pull API. Process: 1. The mobile app sets customer_user_id via the AppsFlyer SDK. 2. Backend retrieves install data using: API: https://hq.appsflyer.com/export/{app_id}/install_data/v 5 3. The data includes, but is not limited to: customer_user_id media_source â€“ e.g., facebook, googleadwords_int campaign â€“ full campaign name af_channel â€“ campaign channel (if set) |

Key Features â€“ Phase 1 Scope Feature Description Unlimited Variants Dengage Users can create any number of variants (A/B/C/Control/etc.) Sticky Assignment Each user is consistently assigned to the same variant Manual Traffic Split Custom % assignment per variant Winner Metric Clicks only (no selection UI in Phase 1) Statistical Model Frequentist Z-Test Confidence Threshold Fixed at 95% (p-value < 0.05) Min. Sample Size 100 users AND 25 conversions per variant Real-Time Evaluation Automatic winner evaluation after thresholds are met Manual Override Dengage Users can override the winner manually Reporting Enhancements Updated UI with p-values, confidence, and winner status Export Support CSV download and API endpoint for test logs Max Test Duration 30 days default (configurable) UI Changes Required â€“ Phase 1 A. | Confidence Threshold | Fixed at 95% (p-value < 0.05) |
| Min. Sample Size | 100 users AND 25 conversions per variant |
| Real-Time Evaluation | Automatic winner evaluation after thresholds are met |
| Manual Override | Dengage Users can override the winner manually |
| Reporting Enhancements | Updated UI with p-values, confidence, and winner status |
| Export Support | CSV download and API endpoint for test logs |
| Max Test Duration | 30 days default (configurable) |


| Rule | Default Value | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Max Duration | 30 days | Auto mark as Stale/Inconclusive after this |
| Warning Threshold | 14 days | Show a warning to the user |


| Scenario | System Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| One variant is significantly better than all others | Declare a winner and lock it for new users |
| Thresholds not met (low traffic/conversions) | Continue test in "Collecting Data" state. Show progress indicators |
| No stat. significance between the top variants | Mark the test as Inconclusive. Show: â€œNo clear winner between top performers.â€ |
| Marketer chooses manual winner | Allow override with required explanation. Update UI with "Manually Overridden" badge |
| One or more variants fail to serve | Pause test. Notify admins. Auto-redistribute traffic or require intervention |
| Test exceeds 30 days | Auto-close and mark as inconclusive if no winner is declared |

| Triggers Overview This document defines the complete list of triggers available for Dengage's One-to-One Journeys. Triggers represent the entry points that initiate personalized, real-time flows based on user behaviors, profile changes, system events, and external calls. This new trigger model is aligned with best practices from ActiveCampaign, Braze, MoEngage, WebEngage, and Segment. Only meaningful user actions are included. No delivery events like "sent" or "delivered". Full support across channels (Email, SMS, Push, In-App, Onsite, WhatsApp). E-commerce, CRM, Behavioral, and Location events are included. | Push - Custom Parameters The Custom Parameters feature in Push Notifications allows you to add extra data to your push messages beyond the standard fields (title, message, etc.). These parameters are sent along with the push and can be used by your application for custom behaviors. With Custom Parameters, you can: Pass additional information (e.g., how to open a link). Customize how the push is displayed by handling it yourself in your app (instead of letting the SDK render it). Track specific events or attributes for analytics. Send design or functionality details (e.g., background color, image URL, button behavior) that your app can interpret. The SDK only delivers these parameters. What happens next is completely decided by your appÊ¼s development team. How to Access 1. Navigate to: Content > Mobile/Web Push > New. 2. On the Content screen, scroll to the section called Custom Parameters. How to Configure Custom Parameters Step 1: Define Custom Parameters in Settings 1. Go to Settings > Campaign Configurations > Push Custom Parameters. 2. Click Add to define a parameter. 3. Enter: Key â†’ The name of the parameter. Default Value â†’ A default value to appear when creating new pushes. 4. Click Add to save, or Cancel to discard. These parameters will then appear by default whenever you create a new push message. Step 2: Add or Edit Custom Parameters in a Push 1. When creating a new push (Content > Mobile/Web Push > New), go to the Custom |

| Parameters section. |

| Alert for No Audience in One-Time Campaigns An alert email notifies users when a campaign has no target audience. This setting helps users stay informed and take action if needed. Previously, this feature was only available for Recurring Campaigns. Now, it has been added for One-Time Campaigns as well. A new field has been added to the Alert Emails screen, placed just below the existing one for Recurring Campaigns. How to Access 1. Go to Settings > Campaign Configurations. 2. Click on Alert Emails. 3. You will see a new field called â€œNo Audience in One-Time Campaign Alertâ€ below the existing field for Recurring Campaigns. How to Use 1. Navigate to the Alert Emails screen as described above. 2. In the No Audience in One-Time Campaign Alert section, enter the email addresses where alerts should be sent. 3. Check the "Get alerts without time constraints" box if you want to receive alerts immediately, regardless of time settings. Checked â†’ Alert emails are sent instantly. Unchecked â†’ Alert emails are sent within the defined Earliest Time and Latest Time range. 4. Save your settings. With this update, users will now receive alert emails for One-Time Campaigns when the segment result is zero, ensuring better campaign monitoring and management. |

| â€œUpload Fileâ€ Function for Transactional Content The "Upload File" function, previously available for creating content in Marketing Emails, is now extended to Transactional Emails. This feature allows users to generate HTML email content from ZIP files quickly and efficiently. How to Access To use the "Upload File" feature for transactional emails: 1. Navigate to Content > Transactional > Email. 2. Click New to create a new transactional email. 3. In the email creation screen, select "Upload File" as the content type. 4. Upload a ZIP file containing the HTML email structure. How to Use 1. Prepare a ZIP file containing your email's HTML file and any associated assets. Inside the ZIP file, there should be a folder with a name matching the ZIP file itself. Inside this folder, you should find one HTML file and one subfolder. The subfolder should only contain image files. Avoid using special characters (such as " " and "_") or Turkish characters in the folder and image file names. The ZIP file size should not exceed 10MB. 2. Follow the steps under How to Access to upload the file. 3. In the General Section, enter: a. Content Name: Give a name to your content. |

| Adding Total Targeted Column to Channel Report A new column named Total Targeted has been added to the Download feature on the Channel Report page. This column represents the total targeted audience and is calculated as the sum of Total Send and Unsend values from campaign reports. How to Access 1. Navigate to Analytics > Report > Flow > Channel Report. 2. The Channel Report page displays a list of campaigns and their existing data. 3. A new column named Total Targeted is now available. How to Use Viewing Total Targeted Column The Total Targeted column is now visible in the campaign list. This column shows the sum of Total Send and Unsend values. Downloading the Report with Total Targeted Column 1. On the Channel Report listing page, click the Download button. 2. A Select Columns window appears. 3. Choose which columns to include in the downloaded report. 4. Select Total Targeted along with other desired columns. 5. Click Download to generate the report. |

| CDMP User List - Login Error Count The CDMP User List page in the API Users section provides administrators with user access management capabilities. Previously, there was no direct way to reset the login error count for blocked users, leading to usability challenges. To address this, a Reset Login Errors button has been introduced, allowing authorized users to reset the login error count for blocked users. How to Access 1. Navigate to Settings. 2. Click on Identity & Access Management. 3. Select API Users. 4. The CDMP User List page is displayed. How to Use Identifying Blocked Users A new Status column indicates whether a user is Active or Blocked. All users have a three-dot menu (â‹®) at the end of their row, but only blocked users have the Reset Login Errors option. Resetting Login Errors for a Blocked User 1. Locate the blocked user in the list. 2. Click the three-dot menu (â‹®) at the end of the user's row. 3. Select Reset Login Errors. 4. The login error count for the selected user is reset. Access Requirements |

In the General Section: Enter the Name. Choose a Folder. Below the Name field, find the new Description box. 6. For In-App content: Navigate to Content > In-App. Choose a template. Click the Event Details link to view a breakdown of conversions by event: Total Conversions: Displays the total number of conversions. Event Name 1: Shows the number of conversions attributed to the first event. Event Name 2: Shows the number of conversions attributed to the second event. Example: Total Conversions: 10 Event Name 1: 7 |

| Segment Limitation User Guide The Segment Limitation feature allows users to define specific limits for segment groups within the segment creation screen. This feature provides greater control over audience segmentation by enabling independent limit settings for each group without affecting the segment's functionality. How to Access 1. Navigate to Audience > Segments. 2. Click on the New button, then choose Interactive Segment. 3. Type a name, choose a folder, and click the Next button. 4. Proceed to the segment creation screen. How to Use After adding filters, hover over any filter to see the Limitation Icon. Click on the Limitation Icon to open a modal. In the modal, set a limit for the selected segment group. Click OK to apply the limit. The segment group will now have the defined limit applied independently of other groups. If multiple segment groups are combined, or if new filters are added, the defined limit will remain unchanged unless manually updated. In larger segment groups containing multiple sub-segments, the limitation is applied |
| --- |
| based on the widest segment group's defined limit. |

| Preventing Reuse of Last 3 Passwords To help protect your account, the system now prevents the reuse of your last three passwords. This policy encourages stronger password practices and reduces security risks. How It Works Password Change Validation When you try to set a new password: 1. Your new password is securely encrypted and compared with the protected versions of your last three passwords. 2. The password change request is: Approved if your new password has not been used recently. Rejected if it matches any of your last 3 passwords. Password History Management After a successful password change: 1. The encrypted version of your new password is added to your history. 2. If more than 3 passwords are stored, the oldest one is removed to keep only the most recent three. This enhanced password policy is designed to protect your account from unauthorized access and promote better security habits. Keeping your passwords fresh and unique helps ensure your information stays safe and secure. |

| Adding Column Length Information to the Automated Job Screen - User Guide To improve data accuracy and make troubleshooting easier, the Automated Flows screen now includes column length information alongside column names and data types. This update applies to the Data Export Node and Incremental Logs and helps users correctly map their tables and quickly identify errors like "Value Too Long." Adding column length information to this screen provides the following advantages: Customization and Table Mapping: Displaying column lengths with the column names allows users to build tables on their side and ensure accurate mapping. This helps maintain consistency between the exported data and their internal structure. Easier Error Diagnosis: If a job fails due to a "value too long" error, users can easily check the column lengths on the screen to diagnose the issue. How to Access 1. Go to Data Space. 2. Navigate to the Automated Flows Screen. 3. Select the Data Export Node section. 4. Click on Incremental Logs. 5. Choose a template from the list. Once a template is selected, the system will display the column details, including: Column Name Column Type Column Length (new field added) |

In the opened analytics dashboard, scroll to the Button Clicks section. Flow Campaigns Navigate to Analytics > Flow > Channel Report. Click on Filter and set Channel Type to In-app. From the filtered list, click on the campaign name you wish to analyze. | Session Termination After Password Change - User Guide To enhance account security and protect user data, the system now terminates all active sessions when a user changes their password. This means that after updating the password, the user will be logged out of all sessions and must re-login using the new password. This update is an important step in preventing unauthorized access and maintaining account integrity. How to Access Settings > My Profile > Change Password Navigate to Settings. Click on My Profile. Select Change Password. Enter the new desired password. Confirm the new password and save changes. Once the password change is confirmed, the system will automatically log the user out of all active sessions.The user must sign in again using the new password to continue using the system. This change ensures that any unauthorized access using previous sessions is immediately cut off after a password update, helping to keep your account secure. |

| In-App â€“ Dismiss / Close Button Action Types A new Button Action Type called â€œCloseâ€ has been added to In-App content. This option allows you to add a button that simply closes the in-app message without triggering any additional actions. It is different from the existing â€œDismissâ€action, which interacts with Dismiss Behaviour settings in the flow and acts like a â€œRemind Me Laterâ€ option. How to Access Go to Content > In-App > New. Select the type as Visual Editor. Choose a template that includes a button (e.g., Modal). After selecting the template, in the opened screen go to the Actions section. Under Call to Action, youÊ¼ll see the â€œButtonâ€ configuration. In the Button Action Type dropdown menu, you'll now also find: Close â€“ Closes the in-app message immediately. How the Close & Dismiss Button Action Types Work Close: When a user clicks a button set to Close, the in-app message is dismissed immediately without triggering any other flow actions or reminders. Dismiss: The Dismiss action allows you to control what happens next based on Dismiss Behaviour settings in the In-App node in your flow. It behaves like a "Remind Me Later" option, depending on the selected conditions. |

| Roles and Permissions â€“ Manage Table without PII Previously, when assigning the Manage Table permission under Roles & Permissions, the system automatically required enabling Show PII Data permission as well. With this update, the dependency between these two permissions has been removed. You can now grant users access to manage data tables without giving them access to view Personally Identifiable Information (PII). The Manage Table permission no longer depends on the Show PII Data permission. This allows more flexible role creation by separating data management capabilities from sensitive data visibility. Users with Manage Table can create and edit data tables but will only see non-PII data unless Show PII Data is explicitly granted. How to Access & Use Navigate to Settings > Identity & Access Management > Roles & Permissions. Click + New Role to create a new role. In the Permissions section of the new role screen: Scroll down to the Data Space section. Toggle on Manage Table to grant permission to create and manage data tables. Note that Show PII Data has no longer dependency. If needed, you can still manually toggle Show PII Data to grant visibility of sensitive data. This update enhances control over data access by allowing users to manage tables without exposing PII. |

| GDPR User Guide Dengage GDPR The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is a comprehensive data protection law enforced across the European Union (EU) that gives individuals greater control over their personal data. It outlines specific rights for individuals and applies to all organizations that operate in the EU or handle the personal data of EU residents. A key operational component of GDPR is the Data Subject Request (DSR)â€”an action taken by individuals (data subjects) to exercise their rights under data protection laws. These rights include accessing, correcting, deleting, or transferring their personal data. This user guide explains how to comply with GDPR requirements within our platform. It provides practical steps for addressing Data Subject Requests (DSRs), such as data access, deletion, and outlines how to configure platform features to align with GDPR standards. Understanding GDPR Roles in Your Dengage Integration This guide explains how the key roles defined under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)â€”Data Subject, Data Controller, and Data Processorâ€”relate to your integration with Dengage. Understanding these roles is essential for ensuring that personal data is handled lawfully, transparently, and in line with individualsÊ¼ rights, especially when responding to Data Subject Requests (DSRs). Data Subject In the context of GDPR, the Data Subject refers to the individual whose personal data is being collected and processed by your organization. This person has the right to submit DSRs, which may include requests to access, correct, or delete their personal data. Before any action is taken in response to such a request, it is critical that the Data Subject is properly authenticated. Data Controller As the organization using Dengage, you are considered the Data Controller. This means you are the party that decides why and how personal data should be processed. When a |
| --- |
| Data Subject submits a DSR, it is your responsibility to receive, verify, and respond to that |

| SMS â€“ Test Send Logging & Type-in GSM Field Removal This update improves experience when testing SMS content. The "Type-in GSM" field, which was used to manually enter test numbers instead, youÊ¼ll be asked to select a recipient from a Predefined Audience. This ensures a more controlled and secure test process. Additionally, every test SMS you send is now logged, so you can easily review your test history in the new Test Logs section. Sending Test SMS â€“ Removal of Type-in GSM Field Previously, users had two options when sending test SMS messages: entering a number manually using the Type-in GSM field or selecting a Predefined Audience. With this update, it will only be possible to select a Predefined Audience. This change helps standardize test sending practices and ensures better logging and traceability. How to Send a Test SMS Go to Content > SMS/MMS > New. Enter the required details and create your SMS/MMS content. On the content screen, click the Test button at the top-right corner. In the opened modal, click Send Test SMS. In the Send Test modal: Only the Predefined Audience dropdown will be available. Select a predefined audience and send your test message. Viewing Test Logs To improve visibility and traceability, all test sends performed using predefined audiences are now logged in a dedicated Test Logs screen. How to Access Test Logs Navigate to Content > SMS/MMS. In the left-hand panel, under â€œAllâ€ and â€œCreated by Meâ€, click Test Logs. |

| Improved Login Redirection With the new improved login redirection feature, users who access Dengage will now experience better redirection after login. Previously, even if a user was already logged in, clicking on the login link or being redirected for authentication would still keep them on the /login page. Also, when a user logged out from any page, they were redirected to the login page by default. Now, if the user is already authenticated, they will no longer stay on the login page. Instead, they will be automatically directed to the page they originally intended to visit. Additionally, after logging out from any page, users are redirected to the login screen, but once they log back in, they will return to the last page they were on before logging out. This update ensures a smoother experience by preventing redirects to the login screen and allowing users to pick up exactly where they left off. |

| Panel Audit Logs via FTP This feature enables exporting detailed Panel Audit Logs via FTP, making it easier to track user activities for compliance and auditing. These logs are available under the Incremental Logs section and can now be exported to a remote FTP target. The Panel Audit Logs feature allows you to monitor user activities. It supports exporting log data using Incremental Log export via Automated Flows, with the newly added option to use FTP Export as the remote target. These logs include detailed tracking of user actions, such as request times, log id, user name, actions taken, and more. How to Access Data Space > Data Management > Automated Flows How to Use Follow the steps below to export Panel Audit Logs using Automated Flows: 1. Create a New Automated Flow Navigate to Data Space > Data Management > Automated Flows Click the New button Select Automated Flow Enter a name for your flow Choose Start Date and End Date Click Next 2. Configure Flow Screen On the flow design screen: Drag and drop the Recurring trigger to the canvas Set the frequency for how often the export should occur (e.g., daily) Drag and drop the Data Export node to the Actions area 3. Configure Data Export Node Click on the Data Export node Select Incremental Logs |

| In-App Drag and Drop Editor ( In-App Builder) The In-App Builder is a new feature that introduces a drag-and-drop interface for creating in-app content. It allows users to design banners, modals, and more using a simple visual editor, without the need for HTML or coding skills. How to Access Navigation Path: Content > Marketing > In-App To access the In-App Builder, go to the main navigation menu and select Content > Marketing > In-App. This will take you to the listing page where all your in-app content is managed. The In-App Builder is available as a new creation option when starting a new in- app message. How to Use the In-App Builder 1. Start Creating with the New In-App Builder Begin by clicking the New button located at the top-right corner of the In-App listing page. This opens the content type selection screen where youÊ¼ll now see a new third option labeled In-App Builder, in addition to the existing Visual Editor and HTML Editor. Select In-App Builder to continue. This option is specifically designed for users who prefer a no- code, visual design experience. 2. Enter Basic Content Information Once you've selected In-App Builder, youÊ¼ll be prompted to define the basic properties of your content. Enter a Name for your in-app content, choose a Folder to store and organize it, and optionally provide a Description for internal notes or context. These details help maintain structure and clarity across your in-app campaigns. |

| Exporting Campaign Control Group Information via Incremental Logs The Campaign Control Group Contacts log type is now available under Incremental Logs, allowing users to export detailed control group data used in campaigns. This enhancement supports transparency and auditability by providing direct access to contacts excluded from campaign sends due to control group logic. How to Access Navigation Path: Data Space > Data Management > Automated Flows To access this feature, navigate to Data Space > Data Management > Automated Flows. This is where you can define and manage export flows using various trigger and action configurations. How to Use Follow the steps below to export Campaign Control Group Contacts using Automated Flows with Incremental Logs: 1. Create a New Automated Flow Begin by navigating to Data Space > Data Management > Automated Flows. Click the New button. From the options, select Automated Flow. Give your flow a meaningful name, set the Start Date and End Date, and click Next to continue. 2. Configure the Flow Screen Once inside the flow design interface, drag and drop the Recurring trigger onto the canvas. Set the frequency according to how often you'd like the data exported (e.g., daily). Then drag the Data Export node into the Actions section. 3. Configure the Data Export Node Click the Data Export node to begin configuration. Select Incremental Logs as the data source type, and click Next. |

| Frequency Capping Exclusion Guide The Frequency Capping Exclusion feature introduces a new way to manage exceptions to your send limits. Located under the Audience Settings section, this enhancement allows you to define specific contact groups that are not subject to frequency capping rules, ensuring that high-priority users can receive uninterrupted communications. Frequency Capping helps control how many times a contact can receive messages within a certain timeframe (e.g., daily or weekly). With this new feature, you can now exclude certain users from these limits by specifying them using a contact key. This is particularly useful for critical operational communications, or specific business use cases where messaging limits should not apply. How to Access Navigation Path: Settings > Campaign Configurations > Frequency Capping To use this feature, navigate to Settings > Campaign Configurations > Frequency Capping. Scroll to the bottom of the page to locate the newly added Audience Settings section. This section is where you can define which users should be excluded from frequency capping logic. How to Use Frequency Capping Exclusion 1. Select a Contact Key In the Audience Settings section, use the search field to look up individual users by entering a contact key value.This search helps you locate the exact user you wish to exclude from frequency capping rules. |

| Automated Flow - Data Export to Google BigQuery for Segment/Table This feature allows users to export data from a selected Segment or Table to Google BigQuery using the Automated Flow structure. How to Access Navigation Path: Data Space > Data Management > Automated Flows To access the export setup, go to Data Space, then click Data Management, and select Automated Flows. This is where you can create new export flows and configure actions such as sending data to remote targets like Google BigQuery. How to Use 1: Create a New Automated Flow To begin, navigate to the Automated Flows section and click the New button. From the options presented, select Automated Flow. YouÊ¼ll be prompted to name your flow, define its Start Date and End Date, and then click Next to proceed to the configuration screen. 2: Add the Trigger Once inside the flow editor, you will see a canvas for building your automation. Start by dragging and dropping the trigger node onto the canvas. Configure the frequency setting based on how often you want the export to occur (e.g., daily etc.). 3: Add the Data Export Node Next, drag the Data Export node into the Actions section of the canvas. This node allows you to configure where and how the data will be exported. Click on the Data Export node to open its configuration screen and begin setup. 4: Choose Export Frequency and Data Source You will first be asked to select the export frequency again. After confirming, click Next. Then, choose whether you want to export a Segment or a Table. After selecting the data source, click Next once more. |

| Exporting Data to MySQL via ODBC in Automated Flows The ODBC integration in Dengage allows users to export data from the Automated Flow module to various database systems, including MySQL.With the latest enhancements, users can now export data directly to their MySQL databases by defining an ODBC connection. Important: MySQL is not listed as a standalone Remote Target option. However, it can be used seamlessly by configuring it under the ODBC type using the appropriate MySQL ODBC driver. Prerequisite: Defining ODBC for MySQL To export data to MySQL, you must first define it as an ODBC Remote Target. 1. Navigate to Remote Targets: Settings > Integrations > Remote Targets 2. Add a New Remote Target: Click Add to open the configuration window. 3. Enter Remote Target Details: Name: Enter a recognizable name (e.g., MySQL_Export). Type: Select ODBC. Driver: Choose the appropriate MySQL ODBC driver. Provide the necessary server information and user information. 4. Save: Click Save to register the connection. |

Important: MySQL is not listed as a standalone Remote Target option. However, it can be used seamlessly by configuring it under the ODBC type using the appropriate MySQL ODBC driver. Prerequisite: Defining ODBC for MySQL To export data to MySQL, you must first define it as an ODBC Remote Target. 1. Navigate to Remote Targets: Settings > Integrations > Remote Targets 2. Add a New Remote Target: Click Add to open the configuration window. 3. Enter Remote Target Details: Name: Enter a recognizable name (e.g., MySQL_Export). Type: Select ODBC. Driver: Choose the appropriate MySQL ODBC driver. Provide the necessary server information and user information. 4. Save: Click Save to register the connection. |

| Targeting Onsite A/B Test User Guide The A/B Test feature enables you to test multiple content variations in an (targeting) on-site campaign to identify the best-performing version. By distributing your audience across different variants and analyzing their engagement, you can optimize content effectiveness and improve conversion rates. The system uses statistical analysis to automatically determine the winning variant or allows manual winner selection if needed. How to Access 1. Navigate to Campaign > Targeting > On-Site. 2. Click on the New button to create a campaign. How to Use 1. Campaign Settings On the Settings screen, configure the basic campaign details such as campaign name, schedule, website, platform (web or mobile web), audience, and trigger time. These are standard setup steps before enabling A/B testing. 2. Enable A/B Testing Scroll to the Testing section. Toggle A/B Testing ON to test multiple content variants. Click Next to move to the Content screen. 3. Configure Content Variants In the Variant Selection section: Predefined variants (e.g., Control Group, Variant A, Variant B) are displayed. Next to each variant, click the "Select Content" button to choose unique content for that specific variant. |

| Microsoft Dynamics Integration User Guide This guide explains how to integrate Microsoft Dynamics 365 by setting up an application in Azure, configuring permissions, and creating an application user in the Power Platform Admin Center. Step 1: Sign in to Microsoft Dynamics 365 Go to Agentic CRM and ERP Solutions / Microsoft Dynamics 365 , click Sign In, and log in with your Microsoft account. Once signed in, navigate to Dynamics 365 Sales and click on to open the Sales application by filling correct email details Step 2: Access Microsoft Azure Open https://portal.azure.com and sign in using the same Microsoft account. From the left-hand menu, select Microsoft Entra ID to access app registration settings. Step 3: Register a New Application On the Microsoft Entra ID page, click Add and choose App Registration. On the Register an application page, enter a display name for your application in the Name field, ensure that Accounts in this organizational directory only remains selected under Supported account types, and then click the Register button at the bottom of the page. Step 4: Review the Registered Application Once the application is registered, you will be directed to its Overview page, where you can view details such as Display name, Application (client) ID, Object ID, Directory (tenant) ID, and Supported account types. Step 5: Configure API Permissions On the applicationÊ¼s Overview page, you will see all the details of your application. From the left-hand menu under Manage, go to API Permissions. On the Configured permissions section, click the Add a permission button. In the Request API permissions window, select Microsoft APIs, then choose Dynamics CRM. Scroll down to the Permissions section,and click on â€œDelegated permissionsâ€ section. Check the box for user_impersonation (Access Common Data Service as organization users), and click Add permissions button to update the permissions. |

| Muted Push Notification The Muted Push Notification feature allows you to send push notifications without sound. Previously, sound settings were limited to either the default sound or a custom value. With this update, a dropdown menu has been introduced, offering three sound options: 1. Default â€“ Uses the systemÊ¼s default push sound. 2. Custom â€“ Allows you to define a specific sound file by entering a value. 3. Muted â€“ Sends the notification without any sound. This enhancement improves flexibility and makes it easier to configure notification sounds. How to Access You can configure sound settings, including muted push notifications, while creating new push content: Content > Marketing > Push > Platform Settings How to Use To create a push notification with the new sound options, go to Content > Marketing > Push and click the New button. In the General section, you can enter a name for your notification, add an optional description, and choose a folder if needed. Once these details are set, click Next to move forward. In the Select Platform step, choose your preferred platform iOS, Android, or Web. As soon as you select a platform, the relevant platform settings will appear. Among these settings, you will find the Sound option. Previously, this field only allowed a default sound or a custom value. Now, it has been replaced with a dropdown menu that provides three clear options. If you select Default, the system sound will be used automatically. If you choose Custom, an additional Add Customization field will appear, where you need to enter the value of your custom sound. Finally, if you select Muted, the notification will be delivered silently, without playing any sound. |
| --- |
|  |


|  |
| --- |

| Password Reset Link Validity Period by Account This feature introduces the ability to define a custom validity period for password reset links on a per-account basis. Previously, password reset links had a fixed expiration time, but with this enhancement, the duration is now dynamic and depends on the configuration set for each account. How It Works When a user requests to reset their password, the system generates a password reset link. This link is only valid for the time period defined in the accountÊ¼s settings. Once the specified time elapses, the link expires automatically, and the user will no longer be able to use it. To proceed, the user must request a new password reset link. Configuration The validity period is configured in minutes and can be adjusted for each account by the support team through the back-office system. The minimum validity that can be assigned is 5 minutes, while the maximum period allowed corresponds to seven days, which equals 10,080 minutes. If no configuration is applied, the system uses the default value of 30 minutes. For instance, if an account is configured with a validity period of 120 minutes, the password reset link sent to its users will only remain active for two hours. After this time has passed, the link will automatically expire, and any attempt to use it will be unsuccessful. |
| --- |
|  |


|  |
| --- |

| Activating Analytics Tool Flag Per Account The Hotjar and Google Analytics Tracking flag allows accounts to enable or disable third- party analytics tools. For now, this flag supports Google Analytics and Hotjar only. By default, the flag is enabled for all accounts. If an account does not want to use these analytics tools, the support team can disable it in the back office upon request. How It Works The flag is managed by the support team at the account level. When the flag is enabled, Hotjar and Google Analytics tracking remain active and continue to collect data. If the flag is disabled, both tools stop collecting data immediately.Re-enabling the flag restores tracking functionality. Configuration The flag is named Hotjar and Google Analytics Tracking in the back office. Default state: Enabled. To disable: Navigate to the back office and turn the flag off for the relevant account. To enable again: Simply switch the flag back on in the back office. |

| Multi Conversion â€“ Event-Based Segmentation The Multi Conversion â€“ Event-Based Segmentation feature allows you to create segments of users based on the specific conversion event they completed in a campaign. When creating a campaign, you can define a conversion goal and select the conversion method: Segment: tracks overall conversions. Event : tracks up to two specific conversion events (e.g., add to cart, view category). Once the campaign is completed and conversions are recorded, you can create new segments that target users according to the specific event they triggered. This ensures your audience segmentation is event-specific, not just based on overall conversions. How to Use Set Up Conversion in Campaign 1. Open your campaign and go to Flow > Delivery Settings > Conversion Tracking. 2. Turn on the Conversion Goal toggle. 3. Select Conversion Method: Segment |

| Event: select up to 2 specific conversion events (e.g., add_to_cart, view_category). |

| Coupon Codes The Coupons feature allows you to create and manage reusable coupon lists that can later be used across campaigns, such as email, SMS, or push. Each coupon list acts as a container for coupon codes, making it easier to track usage, monitor availability, and set up automated reminders. How to Access Navigate to: Content > Assets > Coupons This opens the Coupons Listing Page, where you can view all previously created coupon lists. Coupons Listing Page On the listing page, you can search, filter, and review details of all coupon lists. Each list displays: Name: Internal name of the coupon list. Snippet: A short identifier usable in content. Total Coupons: Total number of coupon codes in the list. Available Coupons: Number of unused coupons still available. Status: Current state of the coupon list: Active, Expired, or Archived. Expiry Date: Optional, if a date-based expiration is set. Filters You can filter coupon lists using: Status: Select from Active, Expired, or Archived to view only lists in that state. Date Range: Filter lists created or expiring within a specific date range. |

| Flow Components Flow Components Flow Overview Flow is a visual campaign builder that helps you create customer journeys step by step.You can use Flow Components to build these journeys by dragging and dropping of various flow nodes to design complex customer interactions. When Can You Use Flow? Flow helps you create personalized, cross-channel customer journeys that adapt to each userÊ¼s needs. You can use Flow at any stage of the customer journey to build stronger relationships and drive engagement. For example: Welcoming New Users: Send a series of helpful messages to introduce your product and keep new users interested. Bringing Users Back: Reach out to users who havenÊ¼t been active in a while with personalized messages to get them re-engaged. Rewarding Loyalty: Send special offers or thank-you messages to loyal customers to keep them coming back. Advantages of Flow Flow offers several benefits to help you engage users more effectively: Delivers Personalized Experiences: Use customer data to send the right message at the right time, across multiple channels. Supports Omnichannel Engagement: Communicate with users through email, SMS, push notifications, and more. Improves User Retention: Keep users active and interested by staying relevant and timely. AI-Powered Optimization: Test, learn, and improve your flows using AI to find what works |
| --- |
| best for your audience. |


|  |
| --- |
| Flow Components |

| Setting up a Flow | Start by entering the basic details and settings for your Flow. This step defines how and when your campaign will run. Select a Folder: Organize your Flow by choosing a folder to store it in. Add Tags (Optional): Use tags to label and group related Flows for easier tracking. Set a Schedule: Scheduled â€“ One-Time: Set a specific date and time for a single run. Scheduled â€“ Recurring: Set the Flow to repeat periodically. | Last Run Time | Date and time when the flow was last executed. |
| Next Run Time | Date and time when the flow is scheduled to run next. |


| Node Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Email | Sends an email to users using your selected template. |
| SMS | Sends a text message to users. You can define the message content. |
| Push Notification | Sends a push notification to usersÊ¼ mobile devices. You can customize the content. |
| In-App | Displays a message inside your app. |
| On-Site | Shows messages or actions (like pop-ups or banners) on your website based on the userÊ¼s journey. |
| WhatsApp | Sends a message through WhatsApp. |
| A/B Split | Splits users into different paths to test which version of a message or journey performs better. |
| Export | Exports user data at a specific stepâ€”such as contact details or engagement metricsâ€”for use outside the platform. |
| Update Tag | Adds or updates tags for users. Useful for organizing or targeting users later based on behavior. |
| Update Contact | Updates contact details or attributes, such as status or preferences, based on user actions. |
| Paid Social | Adds or removes users from an advertising network audience, such as Google Customer Match or Facebook Custom Audience |
| Web API | Sends data to or receives data from another system using an API call. |

| Status | Description | Channel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sent | The message has been sent from the system and is on its way to the user's device or contact method. | All channels (Email, SMS, Push, In-App, On-Site, WhatsApp |
| Delivered | The message has successfully reached the userÊ¼s device (e.g., phone, inbox, app). | Email, SMS, Push, WhatsApp, A/B Split |


| Opened / Opens | The user has opened the message (e.g., email opened, WhatsApp message read). | Email, WhatsApp |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clicks / Click | The user clicked a link or element in the message. | SMS, Push, In-App, On-Site |
| Displayed | The message appeared on the userÊ¼s screen (e.g., an in- app pop-up was shown). | In-App, On-Site |
| Dismissed | The user closed or ignored the message after it was displayed. | In-App, On-Site |


| Node Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Optimize Time | This node sends the message at the time when each user is most likely to engage. It analyzes past behavior and automatically schedules the message to be delivered at the user's most active or responsive time. |
| Optimize Channel | This node selects the most effective communication channel for each userâ€”such as email, SMS, or push notificationâ€”based on their past response patterns. If no history exists, it uses your default channel. |


| Node Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Engagement Split | Routes users based on how they interacted with previous messagesâ€”for example, whether they opened an email or clicked a link. |
| Random Split | Randomly splits users into different paths. Great for testing different versions of a journey. |
| Decision Split | Sends users down different paths based on specific criteria, like location, purchase history, or specific attributes. |
| Wait | Adds a delay before moving to the next step in the journey. Useful for pacing communication. |
| Join | Merges multiple paths back into one after a split. |
| End | Marks the end of a journey. Once users reach this node, no further steps are taken. |

| Advanced Personalization Dev Guide Advanced Personalization is a powerful feature in Dengage that lets you create content that adapts to each individual user. By leveraging data from your Master Contact or Master Device tables, you can make messages more relevant, engaging, and effective. This goes beyond simple name personalization, your content can dynamically respond to user attributes, behaviors, and preferences. But it doesnÊ¼t stop there. Using Query Data From Data Space, you can fetch data from any table in your data space. This allows you to create even more advanced, personalized experiences by including information from multiple sources and applying conditions based on that data. The result is dynamic content that automatically changes for each recipient, helping your campaigns feel truly personal and impactful. How It Works You can use JavaScript to make dynamic content in the DÂ·engage platform. This template system is similar to the Embedded JavaScript (EJS) template language (EJS site). Template System The difference is that in DÂ·engage, the open and close delimiters for JavaScript blocks are: 1. With {% â€¦ %}, you can write JavaScript code directly in your template. {% if ($Contact.name) { %} <h2>Hello, {%= $Contact.name %}!</h2> {% } else { %} <h2>Hello, valued customer!</h2> {% } %} This code checks if the contact has a name field. If the data exists, it shows Hello, [Name]!. If thereÊ¼s no name, it shows Hello, valued customer!. |

|  |


|  |

| Import - Products & Orders The Products & Orders import type is designed specifically for e-commerce accounts. It allows you to import products and order data or update existing records. This data is essential for segmentation, personalization, and dynamic content creation. In e-commerce accounts, four dedicated tables are available: Orders table Order Details table Product table Product Variant table These tables store key information about products and customer transactions. Data must be provided either through backend integrations or by uploading files. How to Access Data Space > Data Management > Import > Select Import Type > Products & Orders Alongside Contacts, Tokens, and Tables, you will see Products & Orders as an available import type (only visible for e-commerce accounts). Products Import Use this option to import new products or update existing product data. When you click Products as the import type, the following upload options are displayed: Upload File Drag & Drop files, or click Select to browse. Maximum allowed size is 100 MB (accepted formats: .CSV or .ZIP). Manual Enter data directly in the provided fields. Cancel Exit the import screen without uploading. To check the required format at any time, click See Sample File to download the sample templates. Two sample types are available: Product and Product Variant. You can download these sample files before selecting/uploading your file to ensure your data matches the expected format. The system automatically detects which table to update: |

| Push Notifications Overview Engage your audience in real time with powerful, personalized Push Notifications available for both mobile and web platforms. Whether you want to deliver instant updates, promote new content, or re-engage inactive users, our Push Notification system ensures your message reaches the right users at the right moment. Cross-Platform Support Reach users wherever they are, send notifications seamlessly via Mobile Push and Web Push. Rich Notification Types Mobile Push supports multiple notification types: Text, Rich (media), and Carousel. Web Push supports Text and Rich formats, ensuring visually engaging notifications across browsers. Dynamic & Interactive Content Customize your message style and interactivity: Include text, images, or GIFs to attract attention. Add action buttons for direct user engagement. Define custom sounds to make your push notifications stand out. Carousel Push (Mobile) Send carousel-style push notifications featuring multiple images or cards. Each user can receive dynamic, personalized carousel content, making every message uniquely relevant, a standout feature for personalized marketing. Web Push Flexibility Deliver visually appealing web push notifications with or without images, all tailored to your campaign needs. Multilingual Messaging Connect with your global audience by sending multilanguage push notifications. You can even deliver customized messages per user, ensuring maximum localization and impact. Geofence Targeting Send location-based push notifications triggered automatically when a user enters a specific area. Perfect for location-driven engagement such as store visits, events, or region-specific promotions. Push Inbox Keep your most important messages easily accessible through the Push Inbox feature. |

| Automated Flow â€“ Exporting Incremental Logs to Databases via Remote Target With this update, database export capability in the Automated Flow module has been enhanced. Create a New Automated Flow In the Automated Flows section, click New, then select Automated Flow. Enter a name for your flow, set the Start Date and End Date, then click Next to continue. 2. | Contact Extension The Contact Extension feature enables you to store and manage multiple email addresses or phone numbers for a single contact. By default, the master contact table holds only one email address and one phone number per contact, along with their related permissions and subscription statuses (such as email and GSM consent). In some cases, however, you may need to manage more than one email address or phone number for the same userâ€”for example, when a customer has both personal and work contact details. The Contact Extension feature solves this need by allowing you to add and manage alternative contact details for each user. This flexibility allows you to decide which contact information to use in your campaigns, ensuring more precise targeting and better campaign performance. Step 1: Define Contact Extension Types 1. Navigate to Settings > Campaign Configurations > Contact Extension Types. 2. Click Add. 3. Fill in the following fields: Name: Enter a name for the extension type.Example: Personal Email Channel: Select whether this extension type applies to Email or SMS/MMS campaigns. Column Order: Define the order in which this extension type will appear. The Column Order value is important when multiple contact extensions exist, it ensures that the system knows which one to use first in campaign delivery. This determines its priority order during campaign delivery. Smaller numbers (e.g., 1) have higher priority, followed by 2, 3, and so on. |
| --- |
|  |


|  |
| --- |
| Contact Extension |

Add the Recurring Trigger Drag and drop the Recurring Trigger node onto the canvas. Set the desired frequency for the export (e.g., daily, weekly). Incremental Logs can only be used with the Recurring Trigger set to a Daily period. |

| Targeting Channel Report (In-app and Onsite) The Targeting Channel Report is designed to provide insights into the performance of targeting campaigns delivered via On-Site and In-App channels. It allows you to monitor important metrics such as displays, clicks, unique clicks, and CTR. This helps you understand how well your campaigns are engaging your audience and identify opportunities for optimization. How to Access To reach the Targeting Channel Report, navigate through the following path: Analytics > Targeting > Channel Report > Inapp or Onsite Reports Once you open the report, you will see the overall campaign metrics at the top, a list of all campaigns in the middle, and the option to view detailed analytics for individual campaigns. Channel Filters At the top of the screen, there is a Filter button that allows you to focus the report on specific campaigns or channels. You can filter by Channel, choosing between On-Site or In-App. This ensures you only see campaigns relevant to the selected channel. You can also filter by Campaign if you want to focus on a particular campaign, and by Date Range to limit the report to a specific period. There are additional options such as Clear Filter, which removes all filters and shows all data, and Cancel, which closes the filter menu without applying any changes. |
| --- |
|  |

| Badge Number The Badge feature controls the number that appears on the app icon. This number helps users understand how many notifications they have. You can choose how this number is calculated by selecting a Badge Count Type. Custom The Custom option allows you to set a fixed badge number of your choice. This number stays the same for all users and does not change automatically. This option is mainly useful when you want to show a small static number to attract attention, or when developers need a specific number for testing and design checks. Increased (Dynamic) The Increased option updates the badge number automatically for each user. It shows the actual number of unread mobile push notifications that the user has. Because it is dynamic, every user may see a different number based on how many of your push messages they havenÊ¼t opened yet. This is the recommended setting if you want the badge to always stay accurate and reflect each userÊ¼s real notification status. It helps users know exactly how many messages are waiting for them. |

| AI Split The AI Split Node is an advanced feature specifically designed for recurring campaign flows. This node works on a campaign basis and utilizes AI to determine the most effective communication channel. Key Features: Campaign-Based Functionality: The AI Split Node is tailored for recurring campaign flows, ensuring consistent optimization over time. Metric Selection: After adding the AI Split Node to your workflow, you must select the metric that will be used to determine the winning channel. The available metrics are: Opens: Measures the count of recipients who open the campaign messages. Clicks: Measures the counts of recipients who click on links within the campaign messages. Conversion Rate: Measures the percentage of recipients who complete a purchase. Channel Testing Period: When you split the campaign by channels (e.g., Email, SMS), the AI Split Node sends the campaign to each channel for a duration of up to one week. Winner Selection: After up to one-week testing period, the AI analyzes the selected metric (Open, Click, Conversion Rate) to determine the most effective channel. Subsequent campaign messages are then sent exclusively through the winning channel, maximizing engagement and effectiveness. Summary The AI Split Node ensures that your recurring campaigns are continuously optimized for maximum engagement and effectiveness. |

| WhatsApp Unsubscribe The WhatsApp Unsubscribe feature allows you to automatically unsubscribe contacts from WhatsApp communications when they send predefined keywords. How to Access Unsubscribe Settings The Unsubscribe section can be accessed through the WhatsApp Business API integration settings, applicable to both existing and new integrations. Navigate to Settings > Integrations > 3rd Party > WhatsApp. 2. Open your WhatsApp Business API integration. 3. Go to Step 3: Unsubscribe. For New WhatsApp Integration Setup To configure unsubscribe settings when setting up a new WhatsApp Business API integration: 1. Go to Settings > Integrations > 3rd Party > WhatsApp. 2. Select New WhatsApp (New WSP). 3. Choose WhatsApp Business API as the integration type. 4. Proceed to Step 3: Unsubscribe. Unsubscribe Configuration The Unsubscribe section lets you add keywords that users can reply with if they no longer want to receive WhatsApp messages. When a user sends one of these keywords in response to your WhatsApp message, Dengage automatically stops sending WhatsApp messages to that contact. |

| AI Text Creation AI Text Creation allows you to create marketing content faster and more efficiently by using generative AI. While content is created separately within each channelÊ¼s own editor, the same AI capabilities can be used across Email, SMS/MMS, Push, WhatsApp, In-App, and Onsite channels. To do this correctly, the AI first needs to understand who your brand is, how it looks, and how it speaks. That is why AI Text Creation is built on two key foundations: Brand Kit (visual identity) AI Brand Persona (tone and communication style) Once these are defined, the AI can produce content that feels consistent, professional, and aligned with your brand, just like content created manually by your team. Before You Start: Required Setup To use AI Text Creation effectively, you must complete the following steps: 1. Create a Brand Kit 2. Create an AI Brand Persona These steps are required because the AI cannot generate meaningful or accurate content without understanding your brandÊ¼s identity and communication style. 1. Brand Kit What is a Brand Kit and Why Is It Needed? A Brand Kit defines the visual identity of your brand. It tells the AI how your brand should look, not just in AI-generated content, but also in manual content creation. Without a Brand Kit, AI-generated visuals and layouts may look generic or inconsistent. By creating a Brand Kit, you ensure that every piece of content follows the same visual rules, such as colors, fonts, and logo usage. How to Access Brand Kit Go to: Settings > Campaign Configurations > Brand Kit This page displays all Brand Kits created in your account. For each Brand Kit, you can see key details such as: |

| SmartTag with ZekiAI Smart Tags is an AI-powered feature that helps you create meaningful tags automatically by using your existing business and product data. Instead of defining all tags manually, the system analyzes your data and suggests ready-to-use tags that can later be assigned to users based on their behaviors. Smart Tags can be created in multiple ways: you can use AI-suggested tags as they are, edit them to fit your needs, or create completely new tags from scratch. What is a Smart Tag? A Smart Tag is a tag generated with AI support. The system looks at your products, categories, then suggests tags that represent customer interests or purchasing tendencies. These tags help you better understand your audience and build more accurate segments for campaigns. What You Can Do with Smart Tags With Smart Tags, you can: See AI-generated tag recommendations Edit recommended tags before using them Activate recommended tags Create completely new smart tags on your own How to Access Smart Tags To start using Smart Tags, go to Audience > Tags from the main menu. On the Tags page, you will see multiple tabs. Open the Smart Tags tab to view and manage AI-supported tags. This page is designed to clearly separate the tags you are already using from the tags that are suggested by AI. This helps you review recommendations safely before deciding to use them. The first area shows the Smart Tags that are currently active in your account. These are the tags you have already chosen to use. The second area shows Smart Tags that are recommended by AI but are not active yet. |

| Monthly Active Users (MAU) Report The Monthly Active Users Report provides a centralized view of user, contact, and device activity based on the last 30 days of activity. This report enables you to analyze and monitor engagement trends from a single screen, helping you understand how actively your platform is being used over time. Prerequisites The â€œMonthly Active Users Reportâ€ feature flag must be enabled. How to Access the MAU Report To access the Monthly Active Users (MAU) Report, navigate to Analytics > Reports > Monthly Active Users. Once selected, the MAU Report screen opens and displays the latest engagement data. Summary Metrics At the top of the MAU Report screen, three high-level metrics are displayed: Total Active Users, Active Contacts, and Active Devices. These numbers show how many users, contacts, and devices were active at least once during the last 30 days. It is important to note that these values are always calculated using the most recent 30- day window. They are not affected by any date range selected in the report. | Managing Default Values for NOT NULL Columns in Data Space Tables When working with Automated Flow and the Data Space Update node, tables that contain NOT NULL columns without default values may prevent jobs from being created. This ensures tables remain compatible with Automated Flow without requiring database-level changes. With this feature, you can now assign default values to table columns so that: Empty (NULL) values are handled automatically Automated Flow continues to work smoothly If a column receives an empty value, the system uses the default value instead. How to Use the Feature Step 1: Create an Automated Flow Go to Data Space > Automated Flows Click New Choose Automated Flow Give your flow a name Choose a schedule Step 2: Add Flow Components On the flow screen: 1. Drag and drop Recurring as the trigger 2. Add Data Builder as the first action 3. Add Data Space Update as the second action Step 3: Create Data (NULL Values Are Allowed) In Data Builder, create your data using SQL Your query may return empty (NULL) values |

| Campaign â€“ Conversion & Visit Tracking Shared Deadline - Info Text Update This feature improves how tracking deadlines are defined and understood in Campaigns by introducing a single, shared deadline for both Conversion Goal and Visit Tracking. By unifying the deadline logic, users can now control how long campaign outcomes are measured in a clearer way. Whether you are tracking a conversion action or a visit, the same deadline applies, starting from the moment the message is delivered to the contact. This eliminates confusion and ensures consistent tracking behavior across campaigns. This update gives users a clearer mental model of how tracking works in flow campaigns. Instead of managing tracking durations separately or wondering how visit tracking is affected, users define one deadline that governs all post-delivery tracking. The added informational text on the screen explicitly explains what it applies to, helping users confidently set tracking windows for time-sensitive campaigns. How to Access You can access this feature while creating or editing a flow campaign. Navigate to Campaigns > Flow Campaigns, then click New and choose either One-Time or Recurring. After completing the Name & Schedule step, continue to the Campaign Workflow screen. From there, open Delivery Settings and switch to the Conversion Tracking tab. This is where both Conversion Goal and Visit Tracking settings are managed together. |

| Segment Permissions â€“ Select Segments Without Data View Access This feature improves access control in segments by allowing users to select and use existing segments without giving access to full data-level details. Users who work on segmentation often need to include existing segments while creating new ones, but they do not need to see raw data or detailed data information. With this update, users can now select existing segments in the segment screen without requiring the View Data permission. This means they can focus on segmentation tasks without being exposed to data they do not need or should not access. As a result, roles can be defined more flexibly while still maintaining strong data privacy and security. How to Access and Configure Permissions are managed from the Roles & Permissions settings. Navigate to Settings > Identity & Access Management > Roles & Permissions. From the roles listing page, you can open an existing role or create a new one. In the role details screen, scroll down to the Data Space section. The Data Space section includes multiple permissions. For this feature, two specific permissions are relevant. View Segment/Table allows users to see and select existing segments and tables. View Data controls access to detailed data information and raw data content. These permissions work independently, so you can allow segment selection without granting data-level visibility. The Select Segments Without Data View Access feature enables safer and more precise role definitions. It improves usability for segmentation-focused users, protects sensitive data, and supports scalable segmentation workflows without unnecessary data exposure. |
| --- |
|  |


|  |
| --- |

| Salesforce and Shopify Product Tags Mapping to Dengage The Salesforce and Shopify Product Tags Mapping feature allows you to synchronize your existing product tags from Salesforce and Shopify directly into DengageÊ¼s Product table. With this feature, product tags from Salesforce and Shopify can be synced directly into Dengage. This allows you to use the same product tags you already manage in your commerce platforms without changing your existing product structure. By syncing product tags, you can keep your categories as they are, while still using product tags for segmentation, personalization, and analysis in Dengage. This makes product data easier to manage and ensures consistency across platforms. How to Access To prepare and use this feature, you will work within the Product table in Dengage. Navigate to: Data Space > Data Management > Tables > Product From this screen, you can create and manage the column used for syncing product tags from Salesforce and Shopify. How to Use Step 1: Create the Tags Column in the Product Table The tags column does not exist by default and must be created before synchronization. 1. Go to Data Space > Data Management > Tables 2. Open the Product table 3. Add a new column with the following settings: Column Name: tags Data Type: Text 4. Save the changes Once the column is created, the system becomes ready to receive product tag data. Step 2: Enable Tag Synchronization from Salesforce and Shopify After the column is defined: Make sure the Salesforce and Shopify plugins are updated Configure product data synchronization so that: Salesforce product tags are mapped to the tags column Shopify product tags are mapped to the tags column The synchronization process will populate the Product table with tag values from your connected platforms. | Transactional Email Preview & Test Smart JSON Generation Transactional Email Preview & Test â€“ Smart JSON Generation automatically identifies dynamic variables used in transactional email templates and generates a structured JSON payload for testing and preview purposes. With this feature, you no longer need to manually prepare test data from scratch. All required variables are shown automatically, so you can easily see what needs to be filled in. This makes testing faster, reduces mistakes, and helps you preview even complex transactional emails with confidence. How It Works When you click Preview & Test, the system checks your transactional email template and detects all dynamic variables used in the content, such as names, order details, or IDs. After detection, a JSON structure is created automatically. Each detected variable is added as a field, and its value is filled with a placeholder using the variable name itself. This makes it clear which values you can change for testing. You can freely edit this JSON: Replace placeholder values with your own test data Add new fields if you want to test extra data Remove fields you do not need Any changes you make stay available during your session, so you can easily update values and preview again. How to Access 1. Go to Content > Transactional > Email. 2. Create a new transactional email or open an existing one. 3. Select Code Editor as the content type and add your email template code. 4. Save the email as a draft. The Preview & Test feature becomes available after saving. 5. Click Preview & Test. The system automatically detects variables and generates the JSON. |

| Segment Versioning for Interactive and SQL Segments - User Guide Segment Versioning allows you to view and inspect historical versions of Interactive and SQL segments directly from the segment detail screen. This helps you understand which segment logic was active at a specific point in time, making it easier to analyze past campaigns and flows that were triggered based on that segment. By default, only the current version is editable. Previous versions are preserved and displayed in read-only mode for reference. How Segment Versioning Works On the segment detail page, a version selector is displayed near the header. By default, the Current Version is shown. When you select a historical version, the segment definition updates to reflect the selected version and opens in read-only mode. For each version, the creation date and time is displayed to help you identify when that version was active. How to Access 1. Navigate to Audience from the main menu 2. Click Segments 3. From the segment list, select an Interactive or SQL segment Viewing Segment Versions 1. Open the selected segment 2. At the top of the segment screen, locate the Current Version dropdown 3. Click the dropdown to view all available versions 4. Each version is listed with its creation date and time 5. Select a version to view the corresponding segment definition |

| WhatsApp Auto Reply - User Guide WhatsApp Auto Reply allows you to automatically respond to messages sent by users who initiate a WhatsApp conversation with your business. When a user starts a chat, WhatsApp opens a 24-hour conversation window. During this window, messages can be sent directly via REST services. This feature enables you to define a single, optional automatic reply for each WhatsApp number configured in your account. The auto-reply is sent immediately when a user initiates a conversation, helping you acknowledge incoming messages instantly and improve response experience. How to Access To configure WhatsApp Auto Reply, navigate to Settings > Integrations > 3rd Party Integration. Find WhatsApp in the list and click Details. On this screen, locate your WhatsApp Business API, hover over it, and click the Edit button. In the configuration screen, go to the Auto Reply tab (the 5th tab). How to Use In the Auto Reply tab, enable the auto-reply toggle. Enter your message content and click Update WSP to save your configuration. |

Instead of giving broad access to all users, you can now define permissions in detail and assign them through roles. This helps you protect sensitive settings, avoid accidental changes, and give each user access only to what they need. Users see a cleaner interface, and administrators gain better control over access across the platform. How to Access This feature works in two steps. From there, select a role from the User Role dropdown. The dropdown lists the roles defined in the Roles and Permissions section. | Last 3 password cannot be use Current System Behavior The system currently prevents the user from reusing their most recently used password. When the user sets a new password that is different from the current one, the change is successful, and the new password is compared against the previous one for validation. Updated Requirements According to the new requirement, the system must prevent the reuse of the last three passwords. If a user attempts to set a password that matches any of their previous three passwords, the system will reject it. Password Change Validation Mechanism When the user sets a new password: The new password is hashed. It is compared against the stored password history. If the new password matches any of the last 3 passwords, the change is rejected. If there is no match, the password change is allowed. Updating Password History After a successful password change: The new password is added to the password history list. If the list contains more than 3 passwords, the oldest one is removed, and the list is updated accordingly. |

| Idle Timeout Management with Backoffice Flag Current Situation: User session management is handled through access and refresh tokens: Access Token: Has a default expiration time of 15 minutes. Refresh Token: Automatically activates when the access token expires to obtain a new access token, keeping the session active without requiring the user to log in again. In the current setup, even if the user is inactive on the screen, the session remains active due to the refresh token being triggered in the background. Objective: Some clients request that users be automatically logged out of the system if they remain inactive (idle) for a certain period. Instead of disabling the refresh token mechanism altogether, an idle-time-based session termination feature will be developed. This feature will be controlled via a flag configurable per client in the backoffice panel. Scope: A new flag named â€œIdle Time Logout Enabledâ€ will be added to the client settings section in the backoffice panel. When this flag is enabled: If the user does not perform any actions or API calls within a specific time period (e.g., 15 minutes), their session will be terminated, and they will be redirected to the login screen. When the flag is disabled: The current behavior will remain, allowing the session to be automatically refreshed in the background via the refresh token. The idle timeout period will initially be fixed at 15 minutes. Acceptance Criteria: The â€œIdle Time Logout Enabledâ€ flag should be visible and editable on the client detail screen in the backoffice panel. If the flag is enabled and the user remains inactive for the defined idle time, the session |
| --- |
| should be terminated and the user should be redirected to the login screen. |

Log Collection for All Channels: Logs will be collected for In-app and Onsite, enhancing data tracking. 2. Operational Ease: Unified log collection across all channels will simplify data access. 3. Customer Satisfaction: New logs will streamline campaign tracking and error detection. Requirements: 1. New Endpoints: New sends and content endpoints for In-app and Onsite channels will be created. 2. Data Integrity: The new endpoints will be functional and compatible with the existing infrastructure. 3. Documentation: The API usage guide will be updated. |

For this reason, the "Email Send" text in the content nodes must be editable and can be named in this way. There should also be a â€œsaveâ€ button next to this editable title. This feature enhances reporting and organization by allowing users to assign unique names to each content node, reducing confusion and manual work. With this update, users can easily differentiate between content nodes in campaign flows, making the process more efficient and user-friendly. |

| Silent Push Test Sends There are pushes sent to determine whether the user has deleted the application. Normally, in order to understand whether the user has deleted the application, we send this feature once a day and for a certain time, if the customer wishes to turn it on. However, some of the customers stated that they could not test this and therefore could not understand whether the pushes were sent or not. For this purpose, an improvement will be made so that the customer can send silent push via the app he wants. "Silent push" are push notifications sent in mobile applications to perform data update or synchronization operations in the background without showing any notification (sound, vibration or visual alert) to the user. The user cannot see these notifications, but the party that sends the push notification can perform test requests and updates. Here, users can send their messages via iOS, Android and Huawei apps. (not on the web) settings - app â€“ select any app (other than web) - in the top bar on the right User Guide The Silent Push Send Test feature allows users to send silent push notifications to test whether the application is still installed on users' devices. Normally, silent push notifications are sent once a day at night when Uninstall Tracking is enabled. However, some customers were unable to verify whether the silent pushes were being sent. With this enhancement, users can now manually send a Silent Push Test for verification. What is a Silent Push? Silent push notifications are background push messages that update or synchronize data in mobile applications without triggering any visible notifications (no sound, vibration, or visual alert). The user does not see these notifications, but the sender can track responses to confirm if the app is still installed. How to Access and Use the Silent Push Send Test 1: Navigate to Application Settings Go to Settings > Integrations > Applications. |

| Email Builder Autosave When clicked to the "back to concent" on the content preparation page through the email builder, it is automatically saved and redirected to the content page. However, there are concerns about customer requests that this may be confusing and may result in logout when left on the screen for a long time. At this point, if the user somehow logs out and tries to log in again and create a new email content, he will see his old and unsaved work and will be asked if he wants to continue his old work. If the user wants to continue his old work, he will be able to continue working with the last changes he made. USER GUIDE The Email Builder Autosave feature ensures that your work is automatically saved when working on email content. If a user closes their browser, logs out, or accidentally exits the page, their unsaved progress will be retained and restored upon returning. How to Access 1. Navigate to Content > Email. 2. Click on the New button. 3. Select Email Builder as the content type. 4. Choose a template or start with Blank Content. 5. Enter a Name and select a Folder for your content. 6. Click Next to proceed to the Email Builder. Autosave and Recovery Process If you accidentally close your browser or lose your session, the system will retain an unsaved draft of your last work. Upon creating a new email content via email builder, you will see a notice: "Unsaved Template Available" "You have an unsaved draft template. Would you like to continue editing?" No â€“ Discard the draft and start a new email. Yes â€“ Resume editing from the last saved state. |
