| Moving Gray Log Errors into Automated Flow Dalnet - THY The customer uses automated job with file drop trigger by dropping files to FTP. They do two types of work in flows. Automatic table creation and flow triggering. During these operations, they receive graylog level errors that are not reflected in the interface. The scenarios and errors received are explained below. 1- With Automated Sendable Contact Import, they leave files and create automatic tables. In this scenario, they sometimes transmit CSV files that have Turkish characters in their names, markups that we do not support, or very long names. In this case, the name of the CSV file may not be suitable for us to use in table names. For this reason, the table cannot be created, data cannot be transferred and an error is received. 2- In normal flows, they send us a zip file with a file drop trigger, write it to a table and trigger the campaign. From time to time, errors occur in the zip files they send to us, and we receive an error that the zip could not be read. Again, the flow cannot be triggered at all. The following situation occurs in all of these errors. Since the flows are never triggered, no error occurs in the history field. In fact, there is no reaction in the flows as if no data was left. However, they can find out about this by opening a ticket with us. We can also see the details from the graylog. The customer wants these errors to appear in the flow in the interface so that they can follow them. Errors received accordingly will also be shown on the listing screens. In this way, items 1 and 2 above will be resolved. USER GUIDE This feature ensures that Gray Log errors appear within the automated flow interface, making them easier to track. Errors received will also be displayed on listing screens for better visibility. How to Access 1. Navigate to Data Space. 2. Go to Automated Flows. 3. Click on one of the flows you want to inspect. |

| Using Table's Allowed Columns in SQL Segment Within the scope of this development, creating segments of some columns (columns with segmentEnabled: false) is not allowed in the Master Device and Master Contact Tables. At this point, an improvement has been made to show these unusable columns in error messages and to prevent them when trying to create a segment with these columns. This development was carried out for two different areas: 1. For SQL: These columns cannot be validated as SQL query and will return an error message. Error massage: â€œThe â€˜column nameÊ¼ column you are trying to use is not able to set up or allowed to be used in this context for creating segments.â€ 2. For Interactive Segment: These columns do not show contact fields or device fields drop- down list. Columns that cannot be used in tables are listed below: For Master Device: is_device_active, created_by, update_by, wp_subscription, install_date For Main Contact: created_by, updated_by, contact_id User Guide To ensure data integrity and prevent unauthorized segmentation, certain columns in the Master Device and Master Contact tables cannot be used when creating segments. This update enhances error handling by: Preventing the use of restricted columns in SQL queries. Displaying error messages when attempting to create a segment with these columns. Hiding restricted columns from the dropdown lists in Interactive Segment creation. Restricted Columns The following columns cannot be used for segment creation: Table Restricted Columns Master Device is_device_active, created_by, updated_by, wp_subscription, install_date Master Contact created_by, updated_by, contact_id |

| InApp - Screen Name in Test Feature Explanation: The "Screen Name" field has been added to the InApp test screens to test the inapp on a specific screen. This helps in identifying and tracking inapp across different screens more effectively. How to Use It: Screen Name Field: Each test screen now includes a "Screen Name" field. This field indicates the name of the screen being tested, making it easier to identify and manage inapps on different screens. Api structure: As the inapps are coming in the getMessages endpoint. These inapps contain every filters including screen name.there would be no change in the api structure.Same endpoint would be used to fetch the test screen name inapps.Example Scenario: In an e-commerce application: When a user views the "Product Detail" page, the screenName parameter will include "ProductDetail" in the API call. The user will call function set navigation("productDetail") in order to get this inapp visible to the user.Summary: This new feature helps in better tracking and testing of InApp screens by specifying the screen name in the screen name filter. This makes it easier for developers and testers to understand which screens are being tested and how users are interacting with them. USER GUIDE The "Screen Name" field has been added to the InApp test screens to allow testing of in-app messages on a specific screen. This enhancement helps users track and identify in-app messages across different screens more effectively. How to Access 1. Navigate to the InApp Test Screens section in the platform. 2. Select the test screen where you want to test an in-app message. 3. Locate the Screen Name field in the test screen interface. |

| App Inline / Personalization Overview â€œApp Inlineâ€ is a new feature on â€œIn-Appâ€ as an Inline Personalization. The customer will be able to add images to the areas they choose within the application using this feature. They will be able to do this on a segment basis as well as make adjustments based on specific rules. Prerequisites The SDK version should be: 1 IOS: 5.59.x 2 3 Android: 6.0.57.x 4 To use the App Inline the user need to call the function â€œshowInappInlineâ€ with the following parameters Property ID: The user should define an id for the selected inline zone on the application wi th their own developer. It should be â€œstringâ€. Screen Name: This is an extra filter if the user wants to add screen name also ,to show on which screen along with property id. inappinlineElement: This is the layout that the user will provide in order to get the App Inline displayed on that specific area. hideIfNotFound: If hideIfNotFound set to true ,this will hide the inappinlineElement view. By default its false. **Custom Params:**These are the extra custom filters that users want to utilize. App Inline content can be used only on â€œTargetingâ€ (Real-time) Campaigns. App Inline Content should be only â€œImageâ€ type. The BackOffice Flag should be enabled for this feature that called â€œInapp Inline Personalization Enabledâ€ Steps for Set-up App Inline for Targeting Campaigns 1. | Tokenized Send This new feature allows to clients who prefer not to store personally identifiable information data like name, surname, email and phone numbers etc. outside their own systems. The client utilize the encoded data on Email and Sms sendings. Prerequisites 1. The client can not merge identified and tokenized data in one account. a. Tokenized Send feature flag must be enabled on Back Office. 2. The API implementation must be defined to utilize this feature. Settings > Tokenazation API Definition a. 2 types of APIs are supported. i. JSON ii. GZip (Recommended) ðŸ“Œ Technical Documents Tokenized Sending API Definition Tokenized Sending Development Guide 1 b. The API supports HTTP Basic Auth or API Key authorization. 2 If the â€œBASIC AUTHâ€ type is selected, API URL, username, and password must be provided. The clients can utilize SSL connection to encrypt username or password. If â€œAPI KEYâ€ type is selected, Key and Value must be passed through the request header. If the â€œGZipâ€ format (recommended) is used, the request and response should be developed in accordance with GZip as follows: For the request and response: Set the header "Content-Encoding" to "gzip". Set the header "Content-Type" to "application/octet-stream". This ensures that both the request and response are properly encoded and decoded using gzip compression. |

| TB - Moving Gray Log Errors into Automated Flow Sprint 24 Team Blue Dalnet - THY The customer uses automated job with file drop trigger by dropping files to FTP. They do two types of work in flows. Automatic table creation and flow triggering. During these operations, they receive graylog level errors that are not reflected in the interface. The scenarios and errors received are explained below. 1- With Automated Sendable Contact Import, they leave files and create automatic tables. In this scenario, they sometimes transmit CSV files that have Turkish characters in their names, markups that we do not support, or very long names. In this case, the name of the CSV file may not be suitable for us to use in table names. For this reason, the table cannot be created, data cannot be transferred and an error is received. 2- In normal flows, they send us a zip file with a file drop trigger, write it to a table and trigger the campaign. From time to time, errors occur in the zip files they send to us, and we receive an error that the zip could not be read. Again, the flow cannot be triggered at all. The following situation occurs in all of these errors. Since the flows are never triggered, no error occurs in the history field. In fact, there is no reaction in the flows as if no data was left. However, they can find out about this by opening a ticket with us. We can also see the details from the graylog. The customer wants these errors to appear in the flow in the interface so that they can follow them. Errors received accordingly will also be shown on the listing screens. In this way, items 1 and 2 above will be resolved. User Guide https://www.notion.so/Moving-Gray-Log-Errors-into-Automated-Flow- 1974945df33780eca58fdbd47a0c1d8c?pvs=4 |

| TB - Silent Push Test Sends Team Blue Sprint 24 There are pushes sent to determine whether the user has deleted the application. Normally, in order to understand whether the user has deleted the application, we send this feature once a day and for a certain time, if the customer wishes to turn it on. However, some of the customers stated that they could not test this and therefore could not understand whether the pushes were sent or not. For this purpose, an improvement will be made so that the customer can send silent push via the app he wants. "Silent push" are push notifications sent in mobile applications to perform data update or synchronization operations in the background without showing any notification (sound, vibration or visual alert) to the user. The user cannot see these notifications, but the party that sends the push notification can perform test requests and updates. Here, users can send their messages via iOS, Android and Huawei apps. (not on the web) settings - app â€“ select any app (other than web) - in the top bar on the right User Guide https://www.notion.so/Silent-Push-Test-Sends-9fb9c7f082904d999dd6ba2998b3d931? |

Segment When entering a new segment, there could be a guideâ€”this can be written easily, step-by- step, showing what to do. A site-wide map or product tour can also be used here. For example, when you click â€œAdd Exclusion Filter,â€ how is that different from others? This can be explained with an "i" icon, as we donÊ¼t consider our users advancedâ€”especially those using interactive segments. SQL is clear enough; those who use it will understand. Segment Shaper is already new. When we enter a segment using filters and return, the filter is removed. It shouldnÊ¼t beâ€”it should stay applied. The section headings could include available actions, but there should also be step-by- step explanations on what happens next. Preview unavailable Content In the Image Library section, after clicking â€œCopy Link,â€ it should be explained where these links can be used. This could also be a motivational message when entering the section, like: â€œChoose your image, copy the link, and start your campaign!â€ In the Dynamic Contents section, when I clicked it, I suddenly saw a "Snippet" at the top â€”which made me think I clicked the wrong thing. Also, the options shown while creating Dynamic Contents felt too technical. If itÊ¼s not a complex topic, either a user guide or UI/UX improvements should make it feel simpler. | Ostrovok / RU, EU Cloud /Warning for disabling real-time segments https://dev-app.dengage.com/#/segments/editSegmentV2/2291 RealTime Segment Sync RP-562: Ostrovok / RU, EU Cloud /Warning for disabling real-time segments RELEASED Description Add a warning alert when a user disables Real-Time Segment Sync. DC EU, RU Account ostrovok, b2b-ostrovok, rate_hawk, roundtrip What is the clientÊ¼s problem? (please, explain in-depth) Users sometimes disable Real-Time Segment Sync without realizing that the affected segment is still being actively used in multiple campaigns. Since there can be many campaigns running simultaneously, it's easy to forget which segments are linked where. This can lead to unintended campaign behavior or targeting issues. Describe the cost of not doing this request: Campaigns may continue running with outdated or incorrect segment data. Risk of sending irrelevant messages to the wrong audience. Operational inefficiencies due to the lack of visibility on segment usage. Increased support inquiries due to unexpected campaign behavior. Additional Information Suggested behavior: When a user attempts to disable Real-Time Segment Sync, display a *warning popup* indicating that the segment is currently used in active campaigns, and list or link to those campaigns if possible. This will help prevent accidental disruptions and improve user awareness. stories: |

| Appsflyer Partner Integration - Phase 1 Overview What is AppsFlyer? AppsFlyer is a mobile marketing attribution and deep linking platform used by mobile marketers, product teams, and developers. It helps companies: Attribute mobile app installs to specific ad campaigns, partners, and channels. Track in-app events (e.g., purchases, sign-ups, trial starts) with real-time reporting. Understand user journeys and optimize advertising spend across networks like Meta, Google Ads, TikTok, and more. Enable deferred deep linking to send users to specific app content even after install via a single OneLink URL. Manage audience segmentation and re-engagement through push, email, or ad networks. AppsFlyer acts as a critical analytics and campaign attribution layer in the mobile ecosystem, especially for performance-driven and multi-channel marketing teams. 1. Why This Is Needed Customer Demand: Ostrovok and another key mobile-first customer have requested AppsFlyer integration to enhance campaign targeting and visibility. Market Expectation: Competitors like MoEngage, WebEngage, CleverTap, and Braze already offer this integration. Customers expect install source tracking, journey attribution, and deep-link consistency in mobile campaigns. Failing to offer this could lead to churn or lost opportunities with mobile-centric clients. 2. Objective Develop and deploy a two-way integration between Dengage and AppsFlyer, covering: Inbound Postbacks: Receive install and event attribution from AppsFlyer. Outbound Events: Send re-engagement or conversion events back to AppsFlyer. Enable customers to activate this integration from the Dengage dashboard. 3. Competitor Comparison |

| WhatsApp Channel â€“ Unsubscribe Messages and Block Scenarios Reason for Development Following the WhatsApp (WP) Channel enhancement, our users can now create WhatsApp templates and prepare them for sending directly from the Dengage panel. However, unlike SMS and email scenarios, unsubscribe [{{unsubscribe-link}}] functionality is not currently available for WhatsApp messages. It is essential that users are also able to send unsubscribe links in this message type. Additionally, when a recipient blocks the sending number, this action should be detected on our side, and the WhatsApp permission for the relevant contact in the target audience should be automatically updated in the permissions section. Planned Enhancements 1 - Unsubscribe Messaging The structure and process here will be very similar to the unsubscribe flows used in SMS and email. This way, an unsubscribe link will be sent in WhatsApp messages, and when clicked, the user will be redirected to a page where they can complete the unsubscribe process, just like in SMS and email messages. 1.1 - WhatsApp Customized Unsubscribe Page First, a new configuration area will be added to the Settings > Campaign Configurations > Customized Unsubscribe Page section specifically for WhatsApp, in addition to the existing configurations for SMS and email. The configuration layout will be exactly the same as the others, and users will be able to configure the following settings within this section: General Font Family General Font Color Logo Logo Width Logo Align Title |

| GDPR Complience |
|  |
| This document includes the developments to be implemented for GDPR compliance and the solutions to be provided through the existing APIs |
|  |
| GDPR vs. DSR Chart |


| Aspect | GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) | DSR (Data Subject Request) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Definition | A privacy law from the EU that regulates data collection and processing. | A request made by a person to exercise their rights under data laws. |
| What it is | A regulation or legal framework. | A process or action under GDPR (or similar laws). |
| Who is involved | Governments, companies, and individuals in the EU (and outside, if processing EU data). | Individuals (data subjects) and the companies holding their data. |
| Purpose | To protect personal data and privacy. | To allow individuals to control their personal data (access, delete, etc.). |
| Examples | Rules about consent, data storage, security, breach notification, etc. | A person asking to access, delete, correct, or transfer their data. |
| Legal requirement? | Yes, it is a binding law in the EU. | Yes, companies must respond to DSRs under GDPR and similar laws. |
| Applies to | All organizations processing EU citizens' | Individuals (data subjects) using their GDPR rights. |
|  | data. |  |


| Role | Description | DSR Responsibilities |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Data Subject | The individual whose personal data is being processed. | Submits DSRs (e.g., access, delete, update) Must be authenticated before action |
| Data Controller | The organization that decides why and how personal data is processed. | Accepts DSRs from data subjects Verifies identity Ensures DSR is fulfilled Communicates with the data subject |
| Data Processor | The organization that processes data on behalf of the controller (e.g., Dengage). | Helps the controller fulfill DSRs Provides APIs, tools, or direct actions (e.g., data deletion) Does not act independently |


| Aspect | Explanation |
| --- | --- |
| Identifier | Use a unique ID (e.g., user_id , customer_id , email , or phone number ) to map a user's data. |


| Scope | Include all personal data linked to this user across your systems. |
| --- | --- |
| Authentication | Ensure that the person making the DSR is authenticated, to avoid fraudulent requests. |
| User Types | Can include: Registered users Anonymous visitors (if cookies/IDs exist) App users |


| Type | Identifier Example |
| --- | --- |
| Registered User | Email address, Username, User ID |
| Anonymous User | Cookie ID, IP address, Session ID |
| Mobile User | Device ID, App User Token |
| CRM Customer | Customer ID, Loyalty ID, Phone Number |
| E-commerce User | Order ID + Email combination |


| API Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| POST /consent | Record new user consent (e.g., marketing opt-in/out). |
| GET /consent/{user_id} | Retrieve the current consent status of a user. |
| PUT /consent/{user_id} | Update consent preferences (e.g., unsubscribe). |
| DELETE /consent/{user_id} | Revoke consent or erase consent records. |


| Feature / Platform | Braze | WebEngage | MoEngage | Dengage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Built-in consent pop- up/banner | âŒ Not provided | âŒ Not provided | âŒ Not provided | âŒ Not provided |
| Consent collected via | Client-built UI or 3rd- party tool | Client-built UI or 3rd- party tool | Client-built UI or 3rd- party tool | Client-built UI, Dengage SDK, or 3rd- party CMP |
| SDK/API to store consent status | âœ… Yes â€“ via custom attributes & subscription groups | âœ… Yes â€“ via custom attributes & segments | âœ… Yes â€“ via SDK consent flags |  |
| Supports per-channel consent | âœ… Yes â€“ Email, Push, SMS, In-App | âœ… Yes â€“ Email, SMS, Web Push, etc. | âœ… Yes â€“ Multi- channel | âœ… Yes â€“ Multichannel |
| User segmentatio n by consent | âœ… Yes â€“ via Subscription Groups | âœ… Yes â€“ via dynamic segmentatio n | âœ… Yes â€“ consent- based segmentatio n |  |
| Integration with external CMPs | âœ… Supported (OneTrust, Cookiebot, etc.) | âœ… Supported | âœ… Supported |  |
| Excludes non- consenting users | âœ… Yes â€“ campaigns & journeys | âœ… Yes â€“ via filters | âœ… Yes â€“ via suppression logic |  |


| Consent Type | Description | Example Use Case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Marketing Consent | Permission to send promotional content via email, SMS, push, etc. | Email campaigns, newsletters |
| Profiling Consent | Consent to use personal data to create user profiles or segments. | Behavior-based recommendations |
| Analytics/Tracking Consent | Consent to track user behavior across apps/sites, often via cookies or SDKs. | Web analytics tools like GA, Hotjar |
| Third-Party Sharing Consent | Consent to share data with external partners or platforms. | Sharing data with ad platforms or CRMs |
| Sensitive Data Consent | Explicit consent required for special category data (e.g., health, race, religion). | Health app collecting medical history |
| Geolocation Consent | Consent to collect and process user's real-time location. | Local offers, delivery tracking |
| Cookie Consent | Consent to use cookies that are not strictly necessary. | Tracking pixels, social media cookies |
| Automated Decision- Making Consent | Consent to decisions made solely by algorithms (e.g., credit scoring). | Loan approvals, job filtering systems |


| API Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| GET /user- data/{user_id} | Retrieve all personal data held for a given user. |
| GET /dsr- request/{request_id}/s tatus | Track the status of an access request (optional for async processing). |


| API Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| DELETE /user- data/{user_id} | Permanently delete all personal data related to the user. |


| API Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| PUT /user- data/{user_id} | Update personal data fields (e.g., name, email). |


| API Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| GET /user- data/export/{user_id} | Export personal data in a machine- readable format (e.g., JSON, CSV). |


| API Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| POST /api/restrict- processing/{user_id} | Request to restrict further data processing |
| GET /api/restrict- processing/{user_id} | View current restriction status |
| PUT /api/restrict- processing/{user_id} | Update restriction reason or extend restriction period |
| DELETE /api/restrict- processing/{user_id} | Remove restriction (e.g., once legal verification ends) |


| API Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| POST /api/user- object/{user_id} | Submit an objection to data processing. |
| GET /api/user- object/{user_id} | Retrieve current objection status. |
| DELETE /api/user- object/{user_id} | Withdraw an objection (optional, if user changes mind). |


| API Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| GET /api/automated- processing/{user_id} | Inform users if automated decision- making applies to them. |
| POST /api/automated- optout/{user_id} | Allow user to opt out of profiling or automated decision systems. |
| PUT /api/manual- review/{user_id} | Request a manual review of an automated decision (where applicable). |


| API Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| POST /dsr-request | Initiate a new DSR (access, delete, etc.) |
| GET /dsr-request/{id} | Check the status of a DSR |


| DSR Type | Description | API Method Typically Used |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Right to Access | The user can request to see all personal data your system holds about them. | GET /user- data/{user_i d} |
| Right to Erasure (Right to be Forgotten) | The user can request permanent deletion of their personal data. | DELETE /user- data/{user_i d} or POST /dsr-request (type: "delete") |
| Right to Rectification | The user can request corrections or updates to their personal data. | PUT /user- data/{user_i d} |
| Right to Data Portability | The user can request their data in a machine-readable format to transfer to another service. | GET /user- data/export/ {user_id} |
| Right to Restrict Processing | The user can request a temporary block on processing of their data (e.g., during dispute). | POST /dsr- request (type: "restrict") |
| Right to Object | The user can object to processing of their data (e.g., for marketing purposes). | POST /consent (type: "withdraw") or |


|  |  | POST /dsr- request (type: "object") |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Right Not to be Subject to Automated Decision-Making | The user can object to decisions made solely by algorithms. | Usually handled through manual escalation; rare via API |

| E-commerce App Documentation This document provides an overview of the e-commerce test application developed for both Android and iOS platforms. It includes details about the app, categories, products, and login functionality to assist other teams in understanding and utilizing the application effectively. Application Details Domain: app.dengage.com Account: ecomm_dengage Android Application: dengageecommercetest_android iOS Application: dengageecommercetest_ios_production Android Application: Download Here iOS Application (TestFlight): Access Here Categories The application consists of 4 categories, with 3 products per category. Category IDs are displayed under category names on the category list page. When a category is selected, the setNavigation method is triggered on the product list page. In-app messages can be configured by defining the category ID as the screen name in the panel. Example: A sample in-app campaign is defined for "category_01": View Campaign Products Each category contains 3 products, and product IDs are displayed under product names in the product list. When a product is selected, the setNavigation method is triggered on the product detail page. In-app messages can be configured by defining the product ID as the screen name in the panel. |

| Geofence Notifications Not Triggering on Re-entry (iOS) Task Name: Geofence Notifications Not Triggering on Re-entry (iOS) JIRA Ticket: https://dengage.atlassian.net/browse/TM-23Can't find link Issue Summary: Previously, iOS devices were only receiving geofence notifications on the first entry into the geofence area. No notifications were triggered on re-entry, which was incorrect behavior. Resolution: The issue has been identified and fixed. Notifications now trigger every time a user enters the geofence area, including on re-entry. The fix has been successfully tested across all iOS devices. Outcome: Notifications are now sent on every geofence entry. Deployment Details: Sprint: TM Sprint 5 |

This was unintended behavior and affected user experience. Current Behavior: Users were able to swipe up or down on in-app popups, making them scrollable. This caused unexpected movement in the UI. The issue was present across multiple devices and platforms. Expected Behavior: In-app popups should remain static and should not be swipeable. Resolution: The issue has been identified and fixed. Popups now remain static and are no longer swipeable. The fix has been successfully tested and confirmed. |

| Push Custom Buttons JIRA Ticket: https://dengage.atlassian.net/browse/TM-5Can't find link Issue Overview: Rich Push notifications allow users to interact through custom action buttons. Each button is expected to redirect users to a specific URL when clicked. Current Problem: The first button works correctly, directing users to the right URL. The second and subsequent buttons do not work correctly, redirecting users to the wrong URLs. Expected Behavior: Every custom button should redirect users to its assigned URL. The system should handle multiple buttons correctly, ensuring each one functions independently. Fix Implemented: Corrected button indexing to ensure proper URL assignment. Updated notification logic to manage multiple buttons separately. Re-tested on various devices to confirm the fix. Verified successful redirection for all buttons. Post-Fix Results: All buttons now redirect correctly to their respective URLs. The issue is fully resolved, and Rich Push notifications work as expected. |

| Other Option Input Field Issue in In-App Feedback Jira Ticket: https://dengage.atlassian.net/browse/TM-27Can't find link Issue Overview: The input field for the "Other" option in the in-app feedback form was not appearing consistently on Android and iOS devices. This caused users to be unable to enter custom feedback when selecting "Other." Current Behavior: When users clicked the "Other" option, the input field did not always appear. The issue was observed on both Android and iOS platforms. This prevented users from providing custom feedback. Expected Behavior: When users select the "Other" option, the input field should always appear. Users should be able to enter and submit their custom feedback without any issues. Fix Implemented: 1. Updated UI Logic: Ensured the input field is always present in the background and becomes visible when "Other" is selected. 2. Improved Event Handling: Fixed the trigger so that selecting "Other" always displays the input field. 3. Tested on Multiple Devices: Verified the fix works across different Android and iOS versions. |

| Session Termination After Password Change To enhance account security and protect user data, the system now terminates all active sessions when a user changes their password. This means that after updating the password, the user will be logged out of all sessions and must re-login using the new password. This update is an important step in preventing unauthorized access and maintaining account integrity. How to Access Settings > My Profile > Change Password Navigate to Settings. Click on My Profile. Select Change Password. Enter the new desired password. Confirm the new password and save changes. Once the password change is confirmed, the system will automatically log the user out of all active sessions.The user must sign in again using the new password to continue using the system. This change ensures that any unauthorized access using previous sessions is immediately cut off after a password update, helping to keep your account secure. |
| --- |
|  |


|  |
| --- |

This change ensures that any unauthorized access using previous sessions is immediately cut off after a password update, helping to keep your account secure. |

| Whatsapp Contact Extension 1. Purpose and Objective Purpose: To enable multi-address management for each contact across communication channels (Email, SMS, WhatsApp), ensuring that during message delivery, the system can select one or multiple addresses per contact based on configurable rules. The goal is to extend the existing serviceâ€”currently supporting Email (E) and SMS (S)â€”with WhatsApp (W) channel support. Objectives: To store multiple communication addresses per contact in a unified data model. To enhance the API and UI to support WhatsApp addresses in addition to Email and SMS. To provide flexible address selection logic at the time of message delivery (manual, automatic, multi-address, or fallback). 2. Current Situation Currently, the system stores one email and one GSM number per contact in the main contact table. Additional email addresses and GSM numbers are stored in an extension table. During campaign delivery, users can select which email(s) or phone number(s) should receive the message. Multiple selections are supported. However, WhatsApp is not yet supported. To align WhatsApp with the same logic, the extension table and related services must be enhanced to handle this third channel type. Story 1 â€“ Add WhatsApp Extension in Settings Description: A user should be able to add a WhatsApp extension record from the Settings screen. This record includes the WhatsApp number, label, and consent information. List should be searchable UATs: UAT-1.1: User opens Settings > Contact Extension Types and sees â€œAddâ€ option. When the user adds a new WhatsApp number and saves, the record is successfully created. UAT-1.2: Validation prevents saving invalid WhatsApp numbers or empty required fields. |

| Remote Segment Columns to Customization Purpose and Description Problem: Currently, when a remote segment is defined via a remote source connection, the SQL query written for that remote source returns columns correctly, but these columns are not stored during the segment creation process. As a result, when users try to create dynamic content (email, onsite, in-app, WhatsApp, etc.), remote segment columns are not available as variable placeholders â€” unlike standard SQL-based or table columns Need / Objective: To ensure remote source segment columns can be used as dynamic variables in content creation modules, by storing the column metadata during segment creation and exposing it in the variable selection modal. Expected Outcome: Remote source segment SQL result columns are saved along with the segment definition. When creating a content or campaign linked to that segment, users can view and insert these columns as variables within the editor modal. Story 1 - Store Remote Source Segment Columns Description: When a user defines a remote segment based on a remote source SQL, the system should extract all column names and data types from the query result and persist them during the save operation. These columns will later be exposed to the content and campaign modules as selectable variables. Acceptance Criteria: 1. When saving a remote segment, the system should automatically detect and store SQL result column metadata (name + type). 2. Editing a remote segment should update the column list accordingly 3. | Coupon Code Upload Feature (Phase 1) 1. Overview Dengage provides a self-service Coupon List Upload feature, allowing users to import and manage coupon code lists via CSV, REST API, or FTP. 2. Competitors Platform CSV API FTP Alerts Snippe Flow Appen Upload t Node d Braze Yes No No Yes Yes No No MoEngag Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes No Yes e WebEnga Partial No No No No No No ge CleverTap No No No No No No No Dengage Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes Braze relies on snippet-based assignment with {% promotion('key') %} used inside Canvas. It does not support conditional assignment or fallback through a dedicated node. MoEngage supports snippets via Jinja, but coupon distribution occurs when the message is rendered. There is no node to separate assignment logic from message sending. WebEngage allows partial CSV upload but lacks proper coupon lifecycle management. Coupons are treated more like user data. CleverTap does not support any coupon code upload. Dengage will be the only platform to support a dedicated Coupon Assignment Node in automation flows, enabling precise assignment timing, fallback logic, and campaign-level tracking. 3. Upload Methods We will support three coupon code import methods: |

| Appsflyer Partner Integration What is AppsFlyer? AppsFlyer is a mobile marketing attribution and deep linking platform used by mobile marketers, product teams, and developers. It helps companies: Attribute mobile app installs to specific ad campaigns, partners, and channels. Track in-app events (e.g., purchases, sign-ups, trial starts) with real-time reporting. Understand user journeys and optimize advertising spend across networks like Meta, Google Ads, TikTok, and more. Enable deferred deep linking to send users to specific app content even after install via a single OneLink URL. Manage audience segmentation and re-engagement through push, email, or ad networks. AppsFlyer acts as a critical analytics and campaign attribution layer in the mobile ecosystem, especially for performance-driven and multi-channel marketing teams. 1. Why This Is Needed Customer Demand: Ostrovok and another key mobile-first customer have requested AppsFlyer integration to enhance campaign targeting and visibility. Market Expectation: Competitors like MoEngage, WebEngage, CleverTap, and Braze already offer this integration. Customers expect install source tracking, journey attribution, and deep-link consistency in mobile campaigns. Failing to offer this could lead to churn or lost opportunities with mobile-centric clients. 2. Objective Develop and deploy a two-way integration between Dengage and AppsFlyer, covering: Inbound Postbacks: Receive install and event attribution from AppsFlyer. Outbound Events: Send re-engagement or conversion events back to AppsFlyer. Enable customers to activate this integration from the Dengage dashboard. 3. Competitor Comparison |

| Recommendation Engine The Dengage Recommendation Engine enables marketers to deliver personalised, context- aware product recommendations across all communication channels (email, SMS, push, in- app, onsite, WhatsApp). It combines behavioural data, catalogue attributes, and business rules to maximise relevance and conversion. This document contains: Recommendation types Dengage supports Events required to power them Example scenarios of usage Fallback strategies for cold start or missing data 1. Concepts Catalogue: A product feed uploaded to Dengage, containing product attributes (ID, title, category, brand, price, discount, images, stock, etc.). Events: User actions collected from web, app, or backend systems ( product_view , purchase , add_to_cart ). Recommendation Models: Algorithms combining event/user/session data and catalogue attributes to generate suggestions. Fallbacks: Predefined rules ensuring recommendations are always served even if personalised data is missing. 2. | Dengage Recommendation Models Specification (Phase 1) 1. Overview Phase 1 of DengageÊ¼s Recommendation Engine focuses on non-session-based recommendation algorithms built from existing event and catalog data. The goal is to provide customers with scalable and flexible product recommendation logic that can be used across all Dengage channels. Each recommendation model can be created once and reused in any channel or campaign through widgets or API calls. Key Terms Input (Seed) This is the data point that drives the recommendation. It can be a product, category, or user- level attribute, derived from static selections or event attributes. Possible sources for input data: Static Product or Category ID: Customer manually chooses a product or category. User Attribute: Derived from user profile data (e.g., last purchased category). Event Attribute: Derived dynamically from an event (e.g., product added to basket). Dengage automatically interprets the input to deliver the correct recommendation logic. Event Events are tracked user or system activities that provide behavioral or transactional data to the recommendation models (e.g., ProductView, AddToBasket, PurchaseOrder). Filter Filters allow customers to refine recommendation results (limit by category, brand, discount range, or exclude low-stock items.) Global Rules Defines high-level behavioral exclusions and logic settings applied across all recommendation outputs. Fallback Specifies what to show if a recommendation produces insufficient results (fallback to Category Bestsellers if â€œFrequently Bought Togetherâ€ has no matches). Refresh Frequency |

| Recommendation Engine Design Document 1. Overview The Recommendation Engine allows users to create reusable recommendation models under Content > Assets > Recommendation Engine. These models are used across Email, Web, Mobile, and Push through Product Box and Web Widgets. A recommendation model defines how results are calculated. The actual inputs such as categoryId or productId are provided later at placement time. This makes each model reusable in multiple contexts. | Allow Custom Column Creation for Product and Order Tables Overview This request aims to allow customers to extend Product and Order tables by adding custom columns via both UI and API. The core table structure must remain fully protected. Only customer-created custom columns can be updated (e.g. name change), while system- defined columns cannot be modified in any way. Problem Product and Order tables currently have a fixed schema. Customers cannot store additional business-specific attributes. Customer Name - Request Link - Figma Link - Technical Analysis - Link Feature Flag No Prerequisites - 1. Purpose and Definition Enable controlled schema extensibility by allowing customers to add custom columns to Product and Order tables. Critical Constraint: Core (system-defined) table structure must not be altered. Only custom-added columns are manageable by users. Why Dengage needs this: Preserves data integrity and backward compatibility. Prevents accidental breaking of existing data flows. Provides flexibility without compromising platform stability. 2. Scope and Objectives In Scope |

| Segment Versioning for Interactive and SQL Segments Overview Problem Clients can view only the latest version of a segment in the panel. Historical segment definitions are not accessible via the UI. This creates a significant gap when analyzing why a campaign or flow was triggered for a specific audience in the past. Client Name All Clients Request Link RP-708: ALL / ALL DC (Cloud & OnPrem) / Segme nt VersiyonlarÄ±nÄ±n Panel Ãœzerinden GÃ¶rÃ¼ntÃ¼lenebilme si Ä°Ã§in GeliÅŸtirme Talebi IN SPRINT Figma Link - Technical Analysis - Link Feature Flag No Prerequisites - 1. Purpose and Definition Currently, users can only view the latest version of a segment from the panel. Historical segment definitions are not accessible via the UI. This creates a significant gap when analyzing why a campaign or flow was triggered for a specific audience in the past. When an unexpected delivery occurs, the support team must identify which segment logic was active at send time. Today, this is only possible by manually querying the sys_panel_audit_log table in the database. This process: Requires technical expertise Is time-consuming Increases operational and support workload Delays root cause analysis and customer communication |

| Shopify Custom Product & Order Column Sync Configuration Overview This task enables Shopify merchants to select which custom Product and Order columns should be synced to Dengage. A new configuration screen will be added to the Dengage Shopify application settings. The Shopify app will first ensure selected custom columns exist in Dengage (via API) and then start sending data for those columns. This feature is dependent on the completion of Custom Column Support for Product & Order Tables. Problem After enabling custom columns in Dengage Product and Order tables, Shopify merchants need control over which Shopify custom fields are synced. Automatically syncing all fields can cause unnecessary data load. | Coupon Code Generation for Shopify This document outlines how Dengage will manage unique coupon code generation through Shopify's Admin API. It covers Shopify's API rate limits, performance across plan tiers, implementation strategies, supported coupon types, and the recommended architecture for scalable, reliable code generation. 1. Shopify API Limits & Cost System What Is a Leaky Bucket Algorithm? Leaky bucket Shopify uses a leaky bucket algorithm to manage API traffic and prevent overloading their systems. Think of it like a bucket with a small hole at the bottom: The bucket size is the maximum burst capacity (1,000 cost units). Water (API calls) is added when you send a request. Water leaks out at a fixed rate (50 cost units/second). If you try to pour too much water too quickly (send too many requests), the bucket overflows and Shopify returns a 429 Too Many Requests error. Shopify uses it to throttle API usage on its GraphQL Admin API. Understanding this system is crucial to designing a reliable and scalable coupon-generation feature. Key Rate Limiting Concepts Term Value Bucket Size 1,000 cost units Refill Rate 50 cost units per second Max Cost/Query 1,000 units (hard cap) Typical Coupon Call ~50 units per 250 codes (bulk mutation) Max Array Input 250 items per GraphQL call Example: 1 request = 250 codes = ~50 units You can safely make 1 request per second (matching refill rate) Bursting: You can send ~20 requests instantly (1,000 / 50), then wait for refill (which is a risky way to manage) |
| --- |
|  |


|  |
| --- |

| Sticky Bar Improvement Overview This document outlines a proposed enhancement to Dengage's sticky bar feature, enabling a new optional behavior for top-positioned bars to appear as a banner on page load and become sticky upon scroll. This update is based on client feedback regarding mobile usability conflicts (e.g., overlapping login buttons). Problem Statement Clients using the sticky bar on mobile have reported UX issues where the bar, fixed at the top of the screen, interferes with critical UI components (e.g., login or register buttons). Current positioning options are limited to top or bottom , without scroll behavior or margin offset. Objective Introduce a scroll-triggered behavior that allows the sticky bar to initially appear in a non- fixed position (like a banner), and then become sticky (fixed) after the user starts scrolling. This improves usability, particularly on mobile, while preserving visibility and conversion potential. Proposed Behavior For Position: Top State Behavior Page Load Sticky bar is placed statically at the top of the page (before content). On Scroll Sticky bar becomes fixed and remains visible. Optional Controlled via new toggle: Stick on Scroll . For Position: Bottom No change in behavior. Always position: fixed; bottom: 0; |

| MAU Report 1. Overview The MAU Report provides a consolidated view of user, contact, and device activity over a rolling 30-day period. The report is placed under Analytics â†’ Reports and becomes visible only for accounts where the MAU billing feature flag is enabled. The design attached in this PRD is a mockup and illustrates the intended layout and user experience. 2. Objective Allow customers to view how many users, contacts, and devices were active at least once in the last 30 days. Provide transparency for MAU-based billing. Offer day-by-day visibility through a line chart showing the historical trend of all three metrics. 3. Definitions Total Active User Info Tooltip: A user is counted as active if they have at least one session within the last 30 days. (Active Contact + Active Device = Total Active User) Active Contact Info Tooltip: A contact that has had at least one session within the last 30 days. Active Device Info Tooltip: A device that has had at least one session within the last 30 days. All three values are calculated using a rolling 30-day window, not a calendar month. Blue Infobox â€œThe values shown in Total Active Users, Active Contacts, and Active Devices are all based on activity from the last 30 days. Each metric reflects how many users, contacts, or devices were active at least once during this 30-day period.â€ Metric Calculation |

| Multi-Segment Selection in Target Audience for Campaigns Overview Problem Currently, n11 creates multiple new segments for each campaign by combining existing segments externally using logical AND / OR conditions. Each campaign-specific combination results in a new segment, leading to excessive segment proliferation and increased operational overhead. Over time, this leads to poor segment manageability, reduced clarity, and a higher risk of misconfiguration. | AC-01 | The user must be able to select more than one segment in the Flow Campaign Audience node. |
| AC-02 | The user must be able to define the logical operator (AND / OR) between the selected segments. |
| AC-03 | When AND is selected, the system must calculate the target audience as the intersection of the selected segments. |
| AC-04 | When OR is selected, the system must calculate the target audience as the union of the selected segments and remove duplicate users. |
| AC-05 | If a user exists in multiple selected segments, the user must appear only once in the final campaign audience. |
| AC-06 | The audience calculation must be triggered and behave consistently with the existing Calculate mechanism. |


| AC-07 | When the campaign is saved, the system must not create a new persistent segment; the segment combination must be stored only at the campaign level. |
| --- | --- |
| AC-08 | Campaign logs and campaign details must clearly display all selected segment IDs and the applied logical operator. |
| AC-09 | Existing campaigns using a single segment must continue to work without any behavioral or calculation changes. |
| AC-10 | The multi-segment audience selection must be available in both Flow Campaigns and Quick Campaigns. |
| AC-11 | The campaign must not be allowed to start unless the audience calculation is successfully completed. |
| AC-12 | For campaigns using multiple segments, the campaign-to-audience relationship must remain traceable through logs for retrospective analysis. |

| Customization Tag Fallback Modal & Auto If/Else Script Generation Overview Problem Whenever a user selects a customization tag, it is immediately inserted into the active editor. This behavior creates inconsistent, error-prone personalization because users cannot define fallback behavior at insertion time and must manually craft fallback logic (or accept blank values). Customer Name Wizz Air Request Link Figma Link Technical Analysis Link Feature Flag No Prerequisites 1. Purpose and Definition Problem: Today, whenever a user selects a customization tag, it is immediately inserted into the active editor. This behavior creates inconsistent, error-prone personalization because users cannot define fallback behavior at insertion time and must manually craft fallback logic (or accept blank values). Requested change: The improvement must be available everywhere customization is available (all editors/areas where the customization selector is used), not only a single channel/editor. 2. | Salesforce Einstein Overview This document outlines the features of Salesforce Einstein AI, grouped by functional domain, and evaluated against Dengage platform capabilities. Feature of Einstein What it does End-to-End Campaign Creation AI helps generate campaign briefs, pick target segments, draft email/SMS content, build customer journeys (flows), provide campaign summaries. Helps speed up campaign launch with less manual overhead. (Salesforce) Personalization Decisioning 1-to-1 personalization: delivering the right content/products/offers to each customer using real-time customer insights. (Salesforce) Paid Media Optimization The agents can monitor ad performance, pause underperforming ads, suggest improvements/optimizations, dynamically adjust campaigns to meet goals. (Salesforce) Loyalty & Promotion Automation Automates workflows for promotions & loyalty-program management; makes creating and applying promotions easier & faster, especially when they span ongoing campaigns. | Master Contact Extensions Reporting Enhancement Overview This document outlines proposed enhancements to Dengage's reporting and history features to properly display Master Contact Extensions data. Currently, when users utilize the Master Contact Extensions feature to communicate via alternative email addresses or phone numbers, all reporting and history records default to the master contact's primary email/phone rather than the actual recipient used for communication. This creates confusion and prevents clients from accurately tracking which contact method was used for each campaign. Problem Statement Clients using the Master Contact Extensions feature report the following issues: 1. Campaign Canvas Reports: When a campaign is sent to an extension email (not the master contact's primary email), the campaign canvas shows the master contact email instead of the actual recipient email used for delivery. 2. Contact Card Campaign History: There is no indication of which specific email address received the campaign when viewing a contact's campaign history, making it impossible to distinguish between sends to primary vs. extension emails. 3. Permission History Gaps: Permission history logs do not include actions related to extension emails and phone numbers, creating incomplete audit trails. These limitations prevent clients from: Accurately reporting on multi-email/phone communication strategies Understanding which contact method is most effective Maintaining complete permission and compliance records Objective Enhance reporting and history features to accurately reflect the actual email address or phone number used for each communication, rather than defaulting to the master contact's primary identifiers. This will enable clients to: Track campaign performance by specific contact methods Maintain accurate communication histories Ensure complete permission and compliance logging |

| Proposed Changes |

| Additional Security Feature - Role based access Overview This document outlines a comprehensive permission system enhancement for Dengage's Settings page. Currently, users with "Account Settings" permission can edit all settings items. The proposed system introduces granular, role- based permissions at both category and individual item levels, with three permission types (View, Edit, No Access) and automatic UI visibility control based on permissions. Problem Statement The current permission system has several limitations: 1. All-or-Nothing Access: Users with "Account Settings" permission can edit all settings, creating security and operational risks. 2. No View-Only Access: There's no way to give users view-only access to settings for audit or reference purposes. 3. Visibility Issues: Users see settings they cannot access, leading to confusion and unnecessary support requests. These limitations prevent clients from: Implementing principle of least privilege Providing audit access without edit rights Maintaining proper separation of duties Objective Implement a hierarchical, granular permission system that: Allows role-based permission assignment at both category and item levels Supports three permission types: View, Edit, and No Access Automatically hides UI elements based on permissions Maintains backward compatibility with existing roles Enables flexible role creation for diverse organizational needs Proposed Permission Structure Permission Types Permission Type Description UI Behavior Edit Full View and write Shows item as access interactive/editable View View-only access, no Shows item as View- modifications allowed only (disabled state or view mode) No Access(implicit) Neither Edit nor View Item is completely selected hidden from navigation Note: No Access is not explicitly selectable - it's the default state when neither Edit nor View permissions are granted. |
| --- |
| Permissions |


|  |
| --- |
| Additional Security Feature - Role based access |

| Gmail Promotions Tab Integration for Email Service Overview This document outlines the integration of Gmail Promotions Tab features into Dengage's email service. Gmail's Promotions Tab allows marketers to enhance their promotional emails with rich annotations including product images, discount offers, expiration dates, and deal badges. These annotations appear directly in Gmail's Promotions Tab, increasing email visibility and engagement without any cost. This feature is available only to consumer Gmail users (not Google Workspace users) and uses Schema.org - Schema.org structured data markup. Problem Statement Dengage currently has a partial implementation of Gmail Promotions Tab annotations, but it suffers from several critical issues that prevent the feature from working properly: 1. Date Format Error: The existing implementation uses an incorrect date format, causing Gmail to reject the annotations. The current format does not comply with ISO 8601 standard required by Gmail, resulting in annotations not being displayed. 2. Limited Annotation Types: Only 2 out of 4 available Gmail annotation types are currently supported, preventing clients from using the full range of promotional features Gmail offers. 3. Missing Fields: Clients cannot utilize many optional fields that could enhance their email's appearance and effectiveness in Gmail's Promotions Tab. 4. HTML Stripping Issue: When clients attempt to manually add Schema.org - Schema.org markup to their email HTML, the system strips it out during the save process. This prevents technically savvy users from implementing workarounds or using advanced features not available in the UI. 5. No Validation or Error Messaging: Without proper validation, clients have no way to know why their annotations aren't appearing in Gmail or how to fix the issues. These issues result in: Wasted client effort in setting up annotations that don't work Support burden from clients reporting "Gmail annotations not showing" Competitive disadvantage against ESPs with working implementations Loss of potential engagement and conversion improvements Objective Fix and enhance Dengage's Gmail Promotions Tab integration to: Fix Date Format: Implement correct ISO 8601 date formatting to make existing annotations work Add Missing Annotation Types: Implement 2 missing types Expose All Fields: Enable all optional Schema.org - Schema.org fields for each annotation type Preserve Manual Markup: Stop stripping Schema.org - Schema.org markup from HTML, allowing advanced users to add custom markup Success criteria: All 4 annotation types functional and displaying correctly in Gmail Clients can use all available Schema.org - Schema.org fields Manual markup preserved in HTML editor |
| --- |
| Date format issues resolved (ISO 8601 compliance) |

| In Scope |  |

| Actionable Recommendations | Context-sensitive tips to reduce content size when Warning/Danger thresholds are exceeded (remove formatting, shorten content, reduce links, etc.) |

| All Email Editor Types | Support Rich Text Editor, Code Editor, and Email Builder (drag-and- drop) with consistent calculation methodology |
| Multi-Language Support | Calculate size correctly for emails with "Add Languages" feature enabled (measure each language variant separately) |

| Automatic Content Compression | No automated size reduction, minification, or compression features (users manually optimize) |
| --- | --- |
| Image Size Management | Image file sizes (hosted on CDN) are not included in calculation - only HTML structure counts |
| Historical Data Analysis | No retroactive analysis of past campaigns or size-related failure reports |
| Hard Send Blocking | Indicator is informational/warning only - does not prevent campaign publishing or sending (same as Spam Score pattern) |

| User Role "No Access" - Automatic Status Management Overview Problem When a user's role is changed to "No Access", the system does not automatically update their status in sys.account_user table to 'P' (Passive). Similarly, when the role is changed back to any other role (Admin or custom roles), the user_status is not automatically reactivated to 'A' (Active). This creates inconsistency where users with "No Access" role remain active in the system at the account level. Purpose and Definition Purpose: To automatically synchronize user status in sys.account_user table when their User Role is changed to or from "No Access". This ensures that users without access permissions are properly marked as passive at the account level, while users granted access are automatically activated. |

| Backend Logic - No Access Assignment | When User Role is changed to "No Access" via user management UI, automatically update sys.account_user.user_status to 'P' (Passive) |
| Backend Logic - Role Reactivation | When User Role is changed from "No Access" to any other role (Admin or custom roles), automatically update sys.account_user.user_status to 'A' (Active) |
| Manual Role Changes | This feature applies only to manual role changes performed by admins through the user management interface |
| Multi-Account Support | Changes affect only the specific account where the role is modified. Same user can have different statuses in different accounts. |
| Audit Logging | Status changes should be logged in audit trail with timestamp, admin user, and reason (role change) |
| Out of Scope |  |


| Automatic Subscription Changes | This feature does NOT apply to automatic role changes triggered by subscription system (e.g., subscription expiration, downgrade) |
| --- | --- |
| sys.user Table Modifications | We do not modify sys.user.user_status - only sys.account_user.user_status is affected |
| Bulk Status Updates | Bulk user status updates or role assignments are out of scope (if needed, can be added as future enhancement) |
| Historical Data Fix | No retroactive status updates for users who were previously assigned "No Access" role |

| Overview Problem When users enter incorrect passwords during login, the system currently locks their account after 5 |


| In Scope |  |
| --- | --- |
| Frontend - Warning Message Display Logic | Implement UI logic to display countdown warnings based on failed_login_attempts count returned by backend API |
| Backend - Failed Attempts Count in API Response | Modify login API error response to include current failed_login_attempts count when authentication fails |
| Warning Message Threshold | Display warnings starting at attempt 3 (showing "2 attempts remaining") through attempt 4 (showing "1 attempt remaining") |
| Visual Design - Warning States | Design warning messages with appropriate visual severity (yellow warning at attempt 3, red critical warning at attempt 4) |
| Password Reset Link Emphasis | Highlight "Forgot Password?" link within warning messages to guide users to password reset flow |
| Mobile Responsiveness | Ensure warning messages display correctly on mobile devices and smaller screens |
| Out of Scope |  |


| Account Lock Threshold Change | The 5-attempt lock threshold remains unchanged - this feature only adds warnings, not threshold modification |
| --- | --- |
| Automatic Account Unlock | Time-based automatic unlock (e.g., unlock after 30 minutes) is out of scope - accounts remain locked until admin unlocks |
| CAPTCHA Implementation | Adding CAPTCHA challenge before lockout is out of scope for this phase |
| Failed Attempt History Display | Showing timestamp/IP of previous failed attempts is out of scope |
| Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) | MFA implementation is a separate security enhancement project |
| Account Lock Notification Email | Sending email notifications when account is locked is out of scope for this phase |

| Username enumeration via different error messages | Low | Medium | Ensure counter ONLY increments for valid usernames. Show generic errors for non- existent users. |
| Cross- browser/session counter inconsistencies | Low | Medium | Counter is user- specific (server- side), not session-specific. |

|  | Engagement Split - Multi-Channel Enhancement |  |  |
|  | Overview |  |  |
|  | Problem | Current Engagement Split node only checks engagement from the immediately preceding send node. When customers use multiple |  |
|  |  | send channels in parallel (e.g., Email + Push sent simultaneously) or want to track engagement across multiple previous sends in a flow, they cannot evaluate combined engagement behavior. This limitation prevents customers from implementing sophisticated engagement-based routing logic such as "engaged with either Email OR Push" or "engaged with all previous communications." |  |
|  | Customer Name | Endeksa |  |
|  | Request Link | RP-749: Endeksa / TR (Cloud) / Campaign Flow Engagement Split ek Ã¶zellik talebi IN SPRINT |  |
|  | Figma Link | https://www.figma.com/design/HNmEr90jf YVRmFaOXEZCjG/Campaign?node-id=9686 -59033&t=OwfCehvrRQxSpVzI-0 Connect y our Figma account |  |
|  | Technical Analysis Link |  |  |
|  | Feature Flag | Not required - Enhanced functionality for all users |  |
|  | Prerequisites | Understanding of Flow Designer architecture and node relationships Access to engagement event data for all channel types (Email, SMS, Push, InApp, Onsite) Knowledge of current Engagement Split |  |
|  |  | node implementation |  |


| In Scope |  |
| --- | --- |
| "Add Content" Button UI | Add "Add Content" button to Engagement Split node settings that opens a modal displaying all previous send nodes in the flow |
| Send Node List Display | Display all previous send nodes in chronological order (position #1, #2, #3, etc.) with channel-specific icons, send name, campaign info, and metadata |
| Multi-Select Functionality | Allow users to select multiple send nodes via checkboxes. Users can select any combination of previous sends from any channel type. |
| Exclude Functionality | Provide ability to explicitly exclude certain send nodes from engagement evaluation (unchecked state means excluded) |
| Event Type Selection per Send | For each selected send node, display channel-appropriate event options (Delivery/Open/Click for Email, etc.) as radio buttons. Only ONE event type can be selected per send node. |
| Channel-Specific Event Options | Dynamically display event types based on send channel: Email: Delivery / Open / Click Push: Delivery / Click SMS: Delivery / Click |


|  | InApp: Display / Dismiss / Click Onsite: Display / Dismiss / Click |
| --- | --- |
| OR/AND Logic Selection | Provide radio button options for logic operator: OR Logic: User engaged in ANY of the selected sends AND Logic: User engaged in ALL of the selected sends |
| Backward Compatibility | Existing Engagement Split nodes continue to work with current "last send only" behavior. New functionality is opt-in via "Add Content" button. |
| Flow Validation | Validate that at least one send node is selected before allowing user to save Engagement Split configuration |
| Out of Scope |  |
| Multiple Event Types per Send | Users CANNOT select multiple event types for a single send (e.g., cannot select both "Open AND Click" for one Email send). Only ONE event type per send is supported in this phase. |
| Future Send Nodes | Cannot evaluate engagement from send nodes that appear AFTER the Engagement Split node in the flow (only previous/preceding sends) |
| Time-Based Engagement Windows | No support for time-window filtering (e.g., "engaged within last 24 hours"). Time windows should be controlled by Wait nodes in the flow. |
| Negative Engagement Logic | No direct support for "did NOT engage" selection in this modal. Users follow the "Not Engaged" path from the node naturally. |
| Cross-Flow Engagement | Cannot check engagement from send nodes in OTHER flows - only within the current flow |

|  | InApp Logs API Enhancement - Button Click Tracking & Contact Identification |  |  |
|  | Overview |  |  |
|  | Problem | Customer is using InApp messages with multiple buttons (e.g., credit application InApp with 3 buttons: "Yes", "No", "Maybe") and needs to identify which specific button was clicked. Current GetInAppLogs API ( GetInAppLogs ) |  |
|  |  | returns click events (CL) but does NOT include button identifier in the eventAttr field. GetRealtimeInAppLogs API ( GetRealtimeInAppLogs ) ALREADY has eventAttr field for button tracking - we need to ensure consistency across both APIs. Technical Note: eventAttr field stores button_id identifier (primary_button, secondary_button, tertiary_button). GetRealtimeInAppLogs already returns this field, GetInAppLogs needs to be enhanced to include it. Customer needs real-time data transfer to call center systems to reach interested contacts immediately. Without button identification via eventAttr, they cannot filter which contacts clicked which button. Current workaround using sys table queries and segment export with scheduled flows is not real-time enough for business needs. |  |

| Automated Flow - Contact Delete Node for Master Contact Cleanup Overview Problem Customers need to delete contacts from master_contact table for various reasons: incorrect contact_key during onboarding, contact_key changes, or reducing billing amounts. Currently, this can only be done through API (single contact deletion) or DB team intervention, which is risky and time-consuming. There is no self- service mechanism for bulk contact deletion, causing operational overhead for both Support and DB teams. | Automated Flow - Contact Delete Node for Master Contact Cleanup |
| Overview Problem Customers need to delete contacts from master_contact table for various reasons: incorrect |


| In Scope |  |
| --- | --- |
| New Flow Node - Contact Delete | Add "Contact Delete" node to Automated Flow node library (not available in Campaign Flow) |
| Email Domain Restriction | Only users with @dengage.com email domain can see, create, and approve flows containing Contact Delete node. Validation performed at both flow creation and approval stages using token data. |
| Two-Step Configuration UI | Step 1: Radio button selection (Segment / Table) Step 2: Dropdown to select specific segment or table based on Step 1 choice |
| Approval Workflow | Second Dengage email user must approve flow before activation. Approval managed through panel (no external notifications). Both flow creator and approver must have @dengage.com domain. |
| Deletion Logic | Delete ALL contacts from master_contact table that exist in selected segment/table at time of flow execution. Each scheduled run performs fresh deletion. |
| Execution Monitoring | Node displays execution status (running, completed, failed) similar to existing flow job visualization. Shows count of deleted contacts after successful completion. |
| Error Handling | If deletion operation fails (DB errors, connection issues), flow status changes to "Failed" and stops execution. |


| Audit Logging | Log all deletion operations: user who created flow, approver, timestamp, selected segment/table, contact count deleted, success/failure status. |
| --- | --- |
| Out of Scope |  |
| Campaign Flow Integration | Contact Delete node will NOT be available in Campaign Flow - only in Automated Flow |
| Contact Count Preview | No preview of contact count during configuration - only shown after deletion execution |
| Selective Deletion Filters | No "delete only new contacts" or date-based filters - ALL contacts in segment/table are deleted |
| External Notifications | No email or external notifications for approval requests - approvers check pending approvals in panel |
| Undo/Rollback Functionality | No undo or restore capability for deleted contacts |
| Partial Deletion Handling | No partial success scenarios - if any error occurs, entire operation fails (no retry logic) |
| Cascade Deletion from Related Tables | Only master_contact table affected - related table cleanup (events, send history) handled by existing DB constraints |

| Frontend â€” Drag & Drop Section Reordering | Enable drag & drop reordering of sections 1â€“7. Users can grab a section and move it above/below other sections. Visual feedback (drag handle, drop indicator) must be provided during drag. Footer Links section is always pinned at bottom. |
| Frontend â€” Auto-Save Layout Preference | After each drag & drop action, automatically persist the new section order to the backend via API call. No "Save" button. Implement debouncing (e.g., 500ms) to handle rapid consecutive reorders. Show subtle save indicator (e.g., brief toast or checkmark). |
| Backend â€” User Layout Preferences API | New API endpoint to save and retrieve per-user homepage section order. Endpoint should accept an ordered array of section identifiers and store it against the authenticated user. |
| Backend â€” Communication Highlights API | New API endpoint returning campaign-level performance rankings: Top Performing (highest open/click rate), Needs Attention (lowest), Largest Sends, Smallest Sends. Filterable by date range. |
| Backend â€” Campaign Performance Trends API | New API endpoint returning time- series campaign performance data (daily/weekly) by channel. Metrics: Send count, Open Rate, Click Rate. Supports 7-day and 30-day ranges. |
| Frontend â€” Section Internal Features | Each section's internal UI (tabs, filters, charts, cards) as specified in Figma design. Includes: Campaign tabs (Recent/Running/Scheduled), Audience donut chart, Engagement channel table, Trends line chart, etc. |
| Out of Scope |  |
| Section Hide/Show Toggle | Users cannot hide or remove sections â€” only reorder. All sections are always visible. |


| Section Resize / Custom Widgets | Sections have fixed height/width as per design. No resizing or custom widget addition. |
| --- | --- |
| Admin-Controlled Default Layouts | Admins cannot set default layout for other users. Each user controls only their own order. |
| Mobile Responsive Drag & Drop | Drag & drop reordering on mobile/tablet devices is out of scope for this phase. Mobile will display the saved order but without drag interaction. |
| Home Dashboard Aggregated API | A single aggregated API combining all homepage data is optional and out of scope for initial delivery. Can be evaluated for performance optimization in a future phase. |
